kagerou hima wo
inu no yume
Kigo: 陽炎 【かげろう】 kagerō, （かげろふ）, heat shimmer [visual distortion in the air over a heated surface; sometimes misleadingly translated "heat waves"] (all spring).
Notes: 犬の夢 (inu no yume) = a dog's dream. A dog dozing in the lawn's shimmer—languid summer scene.
Ueda Haiku:
The grassy lawn:
amid the shimmering heat waves
a dog’s dream.

Poem: 霜の葱土深々と着たるかな
Romaji:
shimo no negi
tsuchi fukabaka to
kitaru kana
My translation:
frosty green onionsー
deep under a
coat of soil
Kigo: green onion

Romaji:
ringo wo tsumami
iitsukushitemo
kurikaesaneba naranu
My translation:
I pick up an apple:
I've said everything that was to be said,
But still must repeat.
Keene Dawn:
I pick up an apple:
I've said everything that was to be said,
But still must repeat.

Romaji:
omowazu mo
hiyoko umarenu
fuyu sōbi
My translation:
Quite to my surprise 
Some little chicks have been born:
Winter roses.
Keene Dawn:
Quite to my surprise 
Some little chicks have been born:
Winter roses.

Romaji:
onsen no yado ni
uma no ko kaeri
hae no koe
My translation:
At the hot-spring inn
A baby colt was hatched out:
The buzzing of flies.
Keene Dawn:
At the hot-spring inn
A baby colt was hatched out:
The buzzing of flies.

Poem: 行水を捨てて湖水のささ濁り
Romaji:
gyōzui wo
sutete kosui no
sasanigori
My translation:
From a bathing tub
I throw water into the lake—
slight muddiness appears.
Kigo: 行水 【ぎょうずい】 gyōzui, outdoor bathing in a tub (all summer).
Notes: 湖水のささ濁り (kōsui no sasa nigori) = the lake slightly clouded. Bathing water thrown out slightly clouds the lake.

Poem: 麦の秋盗人らしきもの通る
Romaji:
mugi no aki 
nusubito rashiki 
mono tōru
My translation:
Wheat harvesting time—
a man who looks like a robber 
passes by.
Kigo: 麦の秋 【むぎのあき】 mugi no aki, wheat harvest (early summer).
Notes: 盗人らしきもの (nusutto rashiki mono) = something thief-like. A suspicious figure passing through the wheat fields at harvest.

Poem: 愕然として昼寝さめたる一人哉
Romaji:
gakuzen to
shite hirune same-taru
hitori kana
My translation:
Startled
I wake from a midday nap
all alone.
Kigo: 昼寝 【ひるね】 hirune, midday nap / siesta (all summer).
Notes: 愕然として (gakuzen to shite) = with a start. Waking from a midday nap alone—the shock of solitude.

Poem: 泣きやまぬ子に灯ともすや秋の暮
Romaji:
naki yamanu
ko ni hi tomosu ya
aki no kure
My translation:
For a baby who
keeps crying she lights a lamp:
evening in autumn.
Kigo: 秋の暮 【あきのくれ】 aki no kure, autumn dusk (all autumn).
Notes: Lighting a lamp for the crying child in the autumn dusk.

Poem: 軒落ちし雪窮（港）を塞ぎけり
Romaji:
noki ochishi
yuki kyūkō wo
fusagi-keri
My translation:
Fallen off the eaves,
a pile of snow blocks the street
in a slum area.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: 軒落ちし雪 (noki ochishi yuki) = snow falling from the eave blocks the harbor entrance.

Poem: 断食の恋ふ夜半や稲光
Romaji:
danjiki no
mizu kou yowa ya
inabikari
My translation:
A fasting man
craves for water at midnight:
a flash of lightning.
Kigo: 稲光 【いなびかり】 inabikari, lightning flash (all autumn).
Notes: 断食 (danjiki) = fasting. Yearning in the fasting night—lightning flashes overhead. Asceticism and the violent sky.

Poem: 暴動の後にまたなき月夜かな
Romaji:
bōdō no
ato ni mata naki
tsukiyo kana
My translation:
After the riot
an incomparably beautiful
moonlit night.
Kigo: 月夜 【つきよ】 tsukiyo, moonlit night (all autumn).
Notes: 暴動 (bōdō) = riot. After the riot, an incomparably beautiful moonlit night—the world indifferent to human violence.

Poem: 思はずもヒヨコ生まれぬ冬薔薇
Romaji:
omowazu mo
hiyoko umarene
fuyu sōbi
My translation:
Unexpectedly
a chick has hatched—
midwinter rose.
Kigo: 冬薔薇 【ふゆばら】 fuyu-bara, winter rose (all winter).
Notes: ヒヨコ (hiyoko) = baby chick. A chick born beside a winter rose—startling, incongruous new life.

Poem: 馬ひとり忽と戻りぬ飛ぶ蛍
Romaji:
uma hitori
kotsu to modorinu
tobu hotaru
My translation:
The horse alone
has unexpectedly returned—
flitting fireflies
Kigo: 蛍 【ほたる】 hotaru, firefly (mid summer).
Notes: A horse returns alone suddenly; fireflies around it—mysterious, eerie homecoming.

Poem: 空をはさむ蟹死にをるや雲の峰
Romaji:
kū wo hasamu
kani shini oru ya
kumo no mine
My translation:
Clawing the void
lies the corpse of a crab:
mountains of clouds.
Kigo: 雲の峰 【くものみね】 kumo no mine, towering summer clouds (mid summer).
Notes: 空をはさむ蟹 (sora wo hasamu kani) = a crab pinching the sky. A dead crab with claws stretched toward towering clouds—absurdist observation.

Poem: ほの明けに花白き木や露の原
Romaji:
honoake ni
hana shiroki ki ya
tsuyu no hara
My translation:
In the faint light of dawn
a tree blossoming in white,
the field sprinkled with dew.
Kigo: 花 【はな】 hana, (cherry) blossoms [in haiku and haikai the simple word hana 花 refers to cherry blossoms, as do all kigo listed here; but note that in Manyōshū and some other early poetry hana was understood as referring to ume 梅【うめ】plum blossoms, an early spring topic] (late spring).
Notes: ほの明けに (hono-ake ni) = at the faint dawn. White flowers in the dewy field at first light.

Poem: 寝牛とも石とも見えて草萠る
Romaji:
ne-ushi to mo
ishi to mo miete
kusa moyuru
My translation:
A sleeping cow?
A boulder? It could be either.
Grass sprouts out.
Kigo: 草萠る 【くさもえる】 kusa moeru, grass sprouting (all spring).
Notes: 寝牛 (ne ushi) = reclining ox. A reclining ox or perhaps just a stone—the grass sprouting around it either way.

Poem: 相撲乗せし便船のなど時化となり
Romaji:
sumō noseshi
binsen no nado 
shike to nari
My translation:
Wrestlers are aboard
the ferry; why has it become 
stormy weather?
Kigo: 相撲 【すもう】 sumō, sumo wrestling (all autumn).
Notes: 便船 (binsen) = a transport vessel. A ship carrying sumo wrestlers runs into a storm.

Poem: 遠く高き木夏近き立てり畳む屋根に
Romaji:
tōku takaki
ki natsu chikaki tateri
tatamu yane ni
My translation:
In the distance
a tall tree
near summertime
stands
above multitudinous roofs.
Kigo: 夏近き 【なつちかき】 natsu chikaki, summer approaching (late spring).
Notes: A tall, distant tree standing near the arriving summer. Experimental form.

Poem: 蠅打つまで蠅叩きなかりし
Romaji:
hae utsu 
made hae-tataki
nakarishi
My translation:
Until I hit the fly
the fly-swatter
did not exist.
Kigo: 蠅叩き 【はえたたき】 haetataki, fly swatter (summer).
Notes: No fly swatter until you need one—comic frustration.

Poem: 山吹咲く工女が窓々の長屋
Romaji:
yamabuki saku
kōjo ga 
mado-mado no
nagaya
My translation:
Mountain roses bloom:
factory girls 
at the windows 
of a tenement house.
Kigo: 山吹 【やまぶき】 yamabuki, yellow rose / wild yellow rose [literally, "mountain breath"; Kerria japonica] (late spring).
Notes: 工女 (kōjo) = factory girl. Kerria roses blooming at the factory girls' windows.

Poem: 明白む障子の蛾高し
Romaji:
ake shiramu
shōji no ga
takashi
My translation:
Whitening with dawn,
the sliding screen:
on it a moth
high up.
Kigo: 蛾 【が】 ga, moth (all summer).
Notes: A moth high on the brightening shoji screen—morning light exposing what darkness hid.

Poem: 牡蠣飯冷えたりいつもの細君
Romaji:
kaki-meshi
hie-tari
itsumo no 
saikun
My translation:
Oyster stew
has become cold—
same old
wife of mine.
Kigo: 牡蠣 【かき】 kaki, oyster (all winter).
Notes: 細君 (saikun) = one's wife (humble). Oyster rice grown cold—the wife always the same. Wry domestic observation.

Poem: 父はわかつてゐた黙ってゐた庭薄
Romaji:
chichi ha wakatte-ita
damatte-ita
niwa susuki
My translation:
Father had known,
didn't say a word:
pampas grass in the garden.
Kigo: 薄 【すすき】 susuki, pampas grass (mid autumn).
Notes: 父はわかつてゐた黙ってゐた (chichi wa wakatte ita damatte ita) = father understood and kept silent. Pampas grass in the garden as silent witness to unspoken understanding.

Poem: 草をぬく根の白さ深さに堪えぬ
Romaji:
kusa wo nuku 
ne no shirosa
fukasa ni
taene
My translation:
I pull out a stalk of grass,
the root’s whiteness
and depth—
I bear with the sight.
Kigo: 草をぬく 【くさをぬく】 kusa wo nuku, pulling weeds (spring).
Notes: 根の白さ深さに堪えぬ (ne no shirosa fukasa ni taenu) = overwhelmed by the whiteness and depth of the root. Pulling weeds; struck by the white depth of the roots.

Poem: 春寒し水田の上の限なし雲
Romaji:
haru samushi
suiden no ue no
kagiri nashi kumo
My translation:
Cold spring...
clouds without roots above
the paddy fields
Kigo: 春寒 【はるさむ】 haruzamu, spring cold (early spring).
Notes: 限なし雲 (kagi nashi kumo) = limitless clouds. Spring cold; over the paddy fields, clouds stretch without end.

Poem: 赤い椿白い椿と落ちにけり
Romaji:
akai tsubaki
shiroi tsubaki tsubaki to
ochi ni keri
My translation:
A red camellia
then a white camellia
falls down
Kigo: 椿 【つばき】 tsubaki, camellia(s) (all spring).
Notes: One of Hekigotō's most celebrated poems. Red and white camellias falling—minimalist observation of contrasting color.

Poem: 春浅き水を渡るや鷺一つ
Romaji:
haru asaki
mizu wo wataru ya
sagi hitotsu
My translation:
spring is shallow     
crossing the water―     
a single heron
Kigo: 春浅き 【はるあさき】 haru asaki, early/shallow spring (early spring).
Notes: 鷺一つ (sagi hitotsu) = a single heron. A single heron crossing the water in early spring.

Romaji:
harukaze ya
tōshi idakite
oka ni tatsu
My translation:
In the spring wind,
Nursing my fighting spirit,
I stand on a hill.

Romaji:
kamakura wo
odorokashitaru
yokan ari
My translation:
Cold of winter,
Still lingering, has astonished
All Kamakura.

Poem: 夕立を真横に走る白帆かな
Romaji:
yūdachi wo
mayoko ni hashiru
shiraho kana
My translation:
The summer shower—
cutting straight through it, there goes
a white sailboat.
Kigo: 夕立 【ゆうだち】 yūdachi, （ゆふだち）, sudden (summer) shower [literally "evening shower"] (all summer).
Notes: 白帆 (shiroho) = white sail. A white-sailed boat running athwart the summer squall.

Poem: 裏戸より借るべき家の菊を見つ
Romaji:
urado yori
karu-beki ie no
kiku wo mitsu
My translation:
Through the back gate
of the house I am to rent
chrysanthemums are seen.
Kigo: 菊 【きく】 kiku, chrysanthemums (all autumn).
Notes: Looking through a neighbor's back gate at chrysanthemums—neighborly theft of beauty.

Poem: 遠山に日のあたりたる枯野かな
Romaji:
tōyama ni 
hi no atari-taru
kareno kana
My translation:
On the distant hills
the rays of the sun fall…
a withered moor.
Kigo: withered moor
Notes: auther walking through the feild. contrast of cold feild with warm sun
Other translation:
In the distant hills
A patch where sunlight touches
The withered meadows. Keene, Dawn

Poem: 桐一葉日当りながら落ちにえり
Romaji:
kiri hitoha
hi atari  nagara
ochinikeri
My translation:
A paulownia leaf
basking in the sunlight—
it’s dropped to the ground!
Kigo: 桐一葉 【きりひとは】 kiri hitoha, a single paulownia leaf (early autumn).
Notes: Famous poem. A single paulownia leaf falls in full sunlight—the traditional Japanese sign that summer is over.
Other translation:
A paulownia leaf
Caught all the while in sunlight
Flutters to the ground. Keene, Dawn

Poem: 金亀子＿＿つ闇の深さかな
Romaji:
koganemushi
nagetsu yami no 
fukasa kana
My translation:
A gold bug—
I hurl it into the darkness
and feel the depth of the night.
Kigo: 金亀子 【こがねむし】 koganemushi, golden beetle / scarab (all summer).
Notes: 闇の深さ (yami no fukasa) = depth of darkness. A beetle flies off with a hum—measuring the depth of the dark.

Poem: 蛇逃げて我を見し眼の草に残る
Romaji:
hebi nigete
ware wo mishi me no 
fukasa kana
My translation:
After the snake flees
the eyes that glared at me
remain in the grass.
Kigo: 蛇 【へび】 hebi, snake (all summer).
Notes: 草に残る (kusa ni nokoru) = remaining in the grass. The snake flees but leaves its eyes in the grass.

Poem: 夏の月皿の林檎の紅失す
Romaji:
natsu no tsuki
sara no ringo
kō shissu
My translation:
The summer moon—
on the plate lies an apple
with its redness lost.
Kigo: 夏の月 【なつのつき】 natsu no tsuki, summer moon (all summer).
Notes: 林檎の紅 (ringo no kurenai) = the apple's red. Under the summer moon, the apple's redness fades.

Poem: 秋天の下に野菊の花弁欠く
Romaji:
shūten no 
shita ni no-giku no
kaben kaku
My translation:
Under the autumnal
sky, a wild chrysanthemum
lacking a petal.
Kigo: 野菊 【のぎく】 nogiku, wild chrysanthemum(s)/aster(s) [any of several species of wild chrysanthemums or asters with thin-petalled, single white flowers with yellow centers] (mid autumn).
Notes: 花弁欠く (kaben kaku) = petals missing. Wild chrysanthemums under the autumn sky, some petals fallen.

Poem: 天日のうつりて暗し＿＿の水
Romaji:
tenjitsu no
utsurite kurashi 
kato no mizu
My translation:
The sun in the sky
is mirrored darkly on the water
where tadpoles live.
Kigo: 天日 【てんじつ】 tenjitsu, the sun in the sky (autumn).
Notes: 天日のうつりて暗し = the sun shifting and darkening. A moving cloud darkens the water.

Poem: 草を摘む子の野を渡る巨人かな
Romaji:
kusa wo tsumu
ko no no wo wataru
kyojin kana
My translation:
Over the children
picking herbs on the fields something
gigantic passes.
Kigo: 草を摘む 【くさをつむ】 kusa wo tsumu, gathering herbs (spring).
Notes: 野を渡る巨人 (no wo wataru kyojin) = a giant crossing the field. A child gathering herbs—seen as a giant from afar.

Poem: 芽ぐむなる大樹の幹に耳を寄せ
Romaji:
megumu naru
taiju no miki ni
mimi wo yose
My translation:
It begins to bud—
close to the trunk of the great tree
I strain my eyes to listen.
Kigo: 芽ぐむ 【めぐむ】 megumu, budding (all spring).
Notes: 大樹の幹に耳を寄せ (taiju no miki ni mimi wo yose) = placing an ear to the great tree's trunk. Listening for the sap rising in the budding season.

Poem: 流れ行く大根の葉の早さかな
Romaji:
nagare yuku
daikon no ha no 
hayasa kana
My translation:
Floating away—
the turnip leaves—and how
swiftly the go!
Kigo: 大根 【だいこん】 daikon, daikon [the Japanese white radish, Raphanus sativas, much used in cooking] (all winter).
Notes: 流れ行く大根の葉 (nagareyuku daikon no ha) = daikon leaves flowing. The speed of daikon leaves swept along—vivid observation.

Poem: ぱっと火になりたる蜘蛛や草を焼く
Romaji:
patto hi ni
nari-taru kumo ya
kusa wo yaku
My translation:
In an instant
it has become a flame: a spider
in the burning grass.
Kigo: 草を焼く 【くさをやく】 kusa wo yaku, burning grass (early spring).
Notes: A spider caught in the grass-burning—sudden transformation.

Poem: 凍蝶の己が魂追うて飛ぶ
Romaji:
itechō no
onoga tamashii
ōte tobu
My translation:
A butterfly
in the cold: it flies in pursuit
of its own soul.
Kigo: 凍蝶 【いてちょう】 ite-chō, frozen butterfly (all winter).
Notes: 己が魂追うて (onore ga tamashii oute) = chasing its own soul. A butterfly frozen in the cold seems to chase its own soul.

Poem: 川を見るバナナ皮は手より落る
Romaji:
kawa wo miru
banana no kawa wa
te yori ochi
My translation:
I gaze at the river.
A banana peel I held
slips from my hand.
Kigo: 川を見る 【かわをみる】 kawa wo miru, looking at the river (summer).
Notes: バナナ皮 (banana kawa) = banana peel. Distracted by the river, a banana peel slips from the hand.

Poem: もの置けばそこに生まれぬ秋の蔭
Romaji:
mono okeba
soko ni umarenu
aki no kage
My translation:
When I set
something down, there emerges 
autumn’s shadow.
Kigo: 秋の蔭 【あきのかげ】 aki no kage, autumn shadow (all autumn).
Notes: Put something down and immediately an autumn shadow forms around it—the season pressing in.

Poem: 大寒や見舞に行けば死んでをり
Romaji:
daikan ya
mimai ni yukeba
shinde-ori
My translation:
Midwinter’s cold:
I go to visit a sick man
—he is already dead!
Kigo: 大寒 【だいかん】 daikan, major cold / coldest period (mid winter).
Notes: Going to visit a sick friend during the coldest period—arriving to find them dead.

Poem: 枯菊に尚ほ或物をとどめずや
Romaji:
kare-giku ni
nao arumono wo
todomezu ya
My translation:
A dead chrysanthemum
and yet—isn't there still something
remaining in it?
Kigo: 枯菊 【かれぎく】 karegiku, withered chrysanthemums (all winter).
Notes: 尚ほ或物をとどめずや (nao aru mono wo todomedzu ya) = still retaining something. The withered chrysanthemum retains something—a remnant beauty.

Poem: 彼一語我一語秋深みくも
Romaji:
kare ichigo
ware ichigo aki
fukami kamo
My translation:
He says a word,
and I say a word—autumn
is deepening.
Kigo: 秋深み 【あきふかみ】 aki fukami, deepening autumn (late autumn).
Notes: 彼一語我一語 (kare ichigo ware ichigo) = his one word, my one word. A quiet conversation deepening like the autumn.

Poem: 去年今年貫く棒の如きもの
Romaji:
kozo kotoshi
tsuranuku bō no
gotoki mono
My translation:
Last year and this year—
piercing through the two, something
like a pole.
Kigo: last year, this year

Poem: 白牡丹といふといへども紅ほのか
Romaji:
shira-botan
iu to ie domo
beni honoka
My translation:
Even though
it is called a white peony,
a hint of crimson
Kigo: 白牡丹 【しろぼたん】 shiro-botan, white tree peony (early summer).
Notes: 紅ほのか (kurenai honoka) = a faint redness. The white peony—yet faintly touched with pink. Nuanced color observation.

Poem: 冬日今瞼のありて重たけれ
Romaji:
fuyubi ima
mabuta no arite
omota keri
My translation:
Winter sunlight
now lying on my eyelids
seems heavy
Kigo: 冬日 【ふゆび】 fuyu-bi, winter sun (all winter).
Notes: 瞼のありて重たけれ (mabuta no arite omotakere) = the eyelids present and heavy. The winter sun; eyelids heavy—languor of illness.

Poem: 春めきし野山消え去る夕かげり
Romaji:
haru mekishi
no yama kie saru
yu kageri
My translation:
the vernal 
fields and mountains fade away
into dusk shadows
Kigo:
Vernal signs
春めくharu-meku

Poem: 啓蟄の蟻が早引く地虫かな
Romaji:
keichitsu no
ari ga hayahiku
jimushi kana
My translation:
insects awake
ants already dragging
a grub
Kigo:
Insects awake
啓蟄 keichitsu

Poem: ただ霞む春の山ある遠眼鏡
Romaji:
tada kasumu
haru no yama aru
Tomegane
My translation:
only misted 
spring mountains are there
telescope
Kigo: Spring mountain

Poem: 花の冷え落柿舎は今西日なる
Romaji:
hana no hie 
rakushisha wa ima 
nishi-bi naru
My translation:
chill of flowers
at the Fallen Persimmon Hut now
the sun in the west
Kigo:
Flower chill
花冷 hana-bie

Poem: 藤垂れて立夏の急雨いたりけり
Romaji:
wisteria droops and
suddenly, a start of summer shower
has arrived
My translation:
fuji tarete
rikka no kyu-u
itari keri
Kigo: 立夏  Rikka  [Summer / Season]

Poem: 木より木に通へる風の春浅き
Romaji:
ki yori ki ni
kayoeru kaze no
haru asaki
My translation:
from tree to tree    
passes the wind    
spring is shallow
Kigo:
Shallow spring
春浅し haru asashi

Poem: 病めば蒲団のそと冬海の青きを覚え
Romaji:
yameba
futon no soto fuyu umi no
aoki wo oboe
My translation:
When sick, I sense
beyond my futon
wintry blue sea
Kigo: 冬海 【ふゆうみ】 fuyu-umi, winter sea (all winter).
Notes: 病めば蒲団のそと冬海の青きを覚え (yameba futon no soto fuyu-umi no aoki wo oboe) — ill in bed, outside the quilt one becomes aware of the winter sea's blue.

Poem: もつれつゝとけつゝ春の雨の糸
Romaji:
motsure tsutsu
toke tsutsu haru no
ame no ito
My translation:
while tangling 
and while untangling  spring's
threads of rain
Kigo: 春の雨 【はるのあめ】 haru no ame, rains of spring.

Poem: 分け入つても分け入つても青い山
Romaji:
wake-ittemo
wake-ittemo
aoi yama
My translation:
pushing in
and pushing in
emeral mountaint
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu free verse)
Notes: 6-6-5 rhythm, modern words

Romaji:
hito korosu
ware ka mo shirazu
tobu hotaru
My translation:
Perhaps—I don't know—
I may have killed somebody!
Flitting fireflies.

Romaji:
oku shirane
ka no yo no yuki wo
kagayakasu
My translation:
The depth of Shirane—
The snow sparkles with a light
From another world.

Poem: 花を見し面を闇に打たせけり
Romaji:
hana wo mishi
omote wo yami ni
utase keri
My translation:
Let my face
that saw the cherry blossom
be struck by darkness
Kigo: 花 【はな】 hana, (cherry) blossoms [in haiku and haikai the simple word hana 花 refers to cherry blossoms, as do all kigo listed here; but note that in Manyōshū and some other early poetry hana was understood as referring to ume 梅【うめ】plum blossoms, an early spring topic] (late spring).
Notes: 花を見し面を闇に打たせけり (hana wo mishi omote wo yami ni utasekeri) = the face that saw blossoms struck by darkness. The face that saw blossoms now struck by darkness.

Romaji:
sara wo      ayumu
rōrō           tsuki hitori
My translation:
It walks       the heavens
Radiantly    the moon, alone.

Romaji:
chikara ippai naku ko to
naku tori to no asa
My translation:
Morning with a baby crying with all its might
And a crowing rooster.

Romaji:
tsuma no tsuioku no
suppai mikan wo
suute iru
My translation:
I suck at
The sour tangerine of
Memories of my wife.

Poem: 日曜の釣人よ監獄の塀が映る水
Romaji:
nichiyō no turibito yo
kangoku no hei ga
utsuru mizu
My translation:
Sunday fisherman!
Prison wall
mirrored in the water
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 日曜の釣人 (nichiyō no tsuribito) = a Sunday fisherman. A Sunday fisherman; a prison wall reflected in the water. Free-verse, no fixed kigo.

Poem: 力一ぱいに泣く児と啼く鶏との朝
Romaji:
chikara ippai ni 
naku ko to 
naku niwatori to no asa
My translation:
A morning
of babies crying,
of roosters crowing,
with all their might.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 力一ぱいに泣く児と啼く鶏 (chikara ippai ni naku ko to naku niwatori) = a child crying and a rooster crowing with all their might. Morning; child and rooster both crying with all their strength.

Poem: 物売の老いし影夕日に伸びきりたり
Romaji:
mono-uri no
oishi kage
yūhi ni
nobikiri-tari
My translation:
Pedlar's
aged shadow
in the setting sun
stretches to its limit.
Kigo: 夕日 【ゆうひ】 yūhi, setting sun (all autumn).
Notes: 物売の老いし影 (mono uri no oishi kage) = the shadow of an aged peddler. An old peddler's shadow stretched full-length in the setting sun.

Poem: 毬を待つ少女等が手は林なして戦げり
Romaji:
mari wo matu
otome-ra ga te wa
hayashi nashite
soyogeri
My translation:
Awaiting the ball,
maidens' arms
form a grove
and sway.
Kigo: 毬 【まり】 mari, ball (New Year/spring).
Notes: 少女等が手は林なして戦げり (shōjo-ra ga te wa hayashi nashite soyogeri) = the girls' hands forming a grove and trembling. Girls' hands trembling like a grove while waiting for the ball.

Poem: 荷がおろされて寒い馬よ雨降る
Romaji:
ni ga orosarete
samui uma yo
ame furu
My translation:
The load taken down,
a chilly horse!
It rains.
Kigo: 寒い 【さむい】 samui, cold (all winter).
Notes: 荷がおろされて寒い馬よ (ni ga orosarete samui uma yo) = the horse from which the load has been removed, cold. The horse unloaded—cold, standing in the rain.

Poem: たんぽぽたんぽぽ砂浜に春が目を開く
Romaji:
tanpopo tanpopo
sunahama ni
haru ga me wo aku
My translation:
Dandelions,
dandelions
on the sandy shore--
spring
opens its eyes.
Kigo: たんぽぽ 【たんぽぽ】 tanpopo, dandelion (all spring).
Notes: Dandelions opening eyes in the spring sand dunes.

Poem: 水あれば田に青空が深く鋤かれある
Romaji:
mizu areba 
ta ni aozora ga 
fukaku sukare aru
My translation:
As there is water
in the rice paddy,
the blue sky 
is deeply ploughed.
Kigo: 青空 【あおぞら】 aozora, blue sky (all summer).
Notes: 水あれば田に青空が深く鋤かれある (mizu areba ta ni aozora ga fukaku sukikareru) = where there is water, the blue sky is deeply plowed into the paddy. Reflected blue sky plowed deep into the paddy water.

Poem: 空をあゆむ朗々と月ひとり
Romaji:
sora wo ayumu
rōrō to
tsuki hitori
My translation:
In the sky
walk
serenely--
the moon alone.
Kigo: 月 【つき】 tsuki, moon (mid autumn).
Notes: 空をあゆむ朗々と (sora wo ayumu rōrō to) = walking clearly through the sky. The moon walking clearly and alone through the sky.

Poem: 仏を信ず麦の穂の青きしんじつ
Romaji:
hotoke wo
shinzu mugi no
ho no aoki 
shinjitsu
My translation:
In Buddha 
I believe:
wheat-ears' green
truth.
Kigo: 麦の穂 【むぎのほ】 mugi no ho, wheat ear (early summer).
Notes: Believing in the Buddha: the wheat ears are truly blue.

Poem: 夜が氷嚢の白い沈黙でお前と私
Romaji:
yoru ga hyō no
shiroi chinmoku de
omae to watshi
My translation:
Night is 
ice-bag's
white silence--
you and I.
Kigo: 氷嚢 【ひょうのう】 hyōnō, ice bag (winter).
Notes: 夜が氷嚢の白い沈黙 (yoru ga hyōnō no shiroi chinmoku) = the night is the white silence of an ice bag. The night as ice bag—white silence between two people.

Poem: 霧に霧をいでてくる友を待ちておる
Romaji:
kiri ni kiri wo
idete kuru tomo wo
machite oru
My translation:
In the fog
for a friend to come out of the fog
I keep waiting.
Kigo: 霧 【きり】 kiri, autumn mist / fog [see note "On Haze, Mist, Fog"] (all autumn).
Notes: Waiting for a friend emerging from mist into mist.

Poem: 蝶の羽世にもうるわし蟻らこれを曳く
Romaji:
chō no hane
yo ni mo uruwashi
ari-ra 
kore wo hiku
My translation:
Butterfly's wings,
most beautiful in the world;
ants
pull them.
Kigo: 蝶 【ちょう】 chō, （てふ）, butterfly [the spring butterfly image is typically a cabbage white, white members of the family Pieridae; see also "summer butterfly", etc.] (all spring).
Notes: 蟻らこれを曳く (ari-ra kore wo hiku) = ants dragging it. A butterfly's wings most beautiful in the world; ants dragging its corpse.

Poem: 花があるのに花をさがしている蝶々
Romaji:
hana ga aru no ni
hana wo sagashiteiru
chōchō
My translation:
Flowers are there,
and yet,
looking for flowers,
a butterfly.
Kigo: 蝶々 【ちょうちょう】 chōchō, butterfly (all spring).
Notes: Flowers present but the butterfly is still searching—the irony of abundance.

Poem: 石のまろさ雪になる
Romaji:
ishi no marosa
yuki ni naru
My translation:
Stone's plumpness
turns into snow.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: 石のまろさ雪になる (ishi no marosa yuki ni naru) = the stone's roundness becomes snow. The stone's roundness transformed by snow.

Poem: 牡丹一弁一弁の動きつつ開きつつ姿ととのう
Romaji:
botan
ichiben ichiben no
ugoki-tsutsu hiraki-tsutsu
sugata totonou
My translation:
Peony:
one petal,
another petal,
moving,
opening,
puts itself in order.
Kigo: 牡丹 【ぼたん】 botan, tree peony (early summer).
Notes: 一弁一弁の動きつつ開きつつ姿ととのう (ichi-ben ichi-ben no ugokitsutsu hirakitsutsu sugata totonō) = each petal moving and opening, the form comes together. The peony opening petal by petal into its full form.

Poem: 石と石月夜寄りそう
Romaji:
ishi to ishi
tsukiyo
yorisou
My translation:
A stone
and a stone
in the moonlit night
nestle against one another.
Kigo: 月夜 【つきよ】 tsukiyo, moonlit night (all autumn).
Notes: 石と石月夜寄りそう (ishi to ishi tsukiyo yorisou) = stones lean toward each other in the moonlight. Two stones leaning together in moonlight.

Poem: うちの蝶としてとんでいるしばらく
Romaji:
uchi no cho toshite
tondeiru
shibaraku
My translation:
As the butterfly of my house,
it flies about
for a while.
Kigo: 蝶 【ちょう】 chō, （てふ）, butterfly [the spring butterfly image is typically a cabbage white, white members of the family Pieridae; see also "summer butterfly", etc.] (all spring).
Notes: うちの蝶 (uchi no chō) = my house's butterfly. A butterfly that for now is the house's butterfly.

Poem: かごからほたる一つ一つを星にする
Romaji:
kago kara
hotaru
hitotsu hitotsu wo
hoshi ni suru
My translation:
From the cage
fireflies
one by one
turn into stars.
Kigo: 蛍 【ほたる】 hotaru, firefly (mid summer).
Notes: かごからほたる一つ一つを星にする (kago kara hotaru hitotsu hitotsu wo hoshi ni suru) = making each firefly from the cage into a star. Releasing fireflies one by one, making each into a star.

Poem: 垣があるので隣のつばきうちにおちる
Romaji:
kaki ga aru node
tonari no tsubaki
uchi ni ochiru
My translation:
Because the fence is there
my neighbour's camellia
falls
into my yard.
Kigo: 椿 【つばき】 tsubaki, camellia(s) (all spring).
Notes: 垣があるので (kaki ga aru node) = because there is a fence. A neighbor's camellia falls on this side because of the fence—boundary and bloom.

Poem: 暑い日の空白、白い蝶一羽にて通る
Romaji:
atsui hi no
kūhaku shiroi 
chō ichiwa nite 
tōru
My translation:
Hot day's
hollowness:
white butterfly
all alone
passes.
Kigo: 暑い日 【あついひ】 atsui hi, hot day (all summer).
Notes: 空白 (kūhaku) = blank space. The blank of a hot day; a single white butterfly passing through.

Romaji:
gyōzui wo
sutete kosui no
sasanigori
My translation:
From a bathing tub
I throw water into the lake—
slight muddiness appears.

Poem: 空をあゆむ朗朗と月ひとり
Romaji:
sora wo ayumu
rōrō to
tsuki hitori
My translation:
Crossing the sky
so silvery and clear
the moon alone
Kigo: 月 【つき】 tsuki, moon (mid autumn).
Notes: Duplicate of Row 155. The moon walking alone through the sky.

Poem: 空はさびしよ家あれば煙をあげよ
Romaji:
sora wa sabishi yo
ie araba 
kemuri wo age yo
My translation:
sorrowful sky
if there is a house out there
please lit a fire
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 空はさびしよ (sora wa sabishiyo) = the sky is lonely. If you have a home, let the sky have smoke—hospitality toward the void.

Romaji:
gokukan no
chiri mo todomezu
iwabusuma
My translation:
Walls of stone
Do not hold back even the dust
Of the dead of winter.

Romaji:
oba yuite
karuki itami ya 
waka kaede
My translation:
A light stab of pain
When my aunt passed away…
The young maples.

Romaji:
imo no tsuyu 
renzan kage wo
tadashū su
My translation:
Dew on the taro leaf:
The chains of the hills and mountains
Correctly range their forms.

Poem: 夏めくや霽れ雷のひとつぎり
Romaji:
natsu meku ya
hare  kaminari no
hitotsu-giri
My translation:
summary-
in clear skies, thunder
one bolt
Kigo:
夏めくnatsu meku 
Summery or summer-like

Poem: 瀧おもて雲おしうつる立夏かな
Romaji:
taki omote
kumo oshi utsuri
rikka kana
My translation:
on the waterfall's surface
clouds pass over
start of summer
Kigo: 立夏  Rikka  [Summer / Season]

Poem: 白菊のしづくつめたし花鋏
Romaji:
shiragiku no 
shizuku tsumetashi 
hana-basami
My translation:
White chrysanthemums—
how cold the dewdrops are 
on my garden shears!
Kigo: 菊 【きく】 kiku, chrysanthemums (all autumn).

Poem: 眼近くの葵に蛇や昼寝覚
Romaji:
majikaku no 
aoi ni hebi ya 
hirune-zame
My translation:
Before my eyes
a hollyhock; on it a snake.
I wake from a nap.
Kigo: 葵 【あおい】 aoi, （あおひ）, hollyhock / althea [Alcea rosea; not to be confused with 木槿【むくげ】 mukuge, rose of Sharon / shrub althea, Hybiscus syriacus], and autumn kidai (mid summer).

Poem: 牡丹しろし人倫を説く眼はなてば
Romaji:
botan shiroshi 
jinrin wo toku 
me hanateba
My translation:
How white the peonies
as I stop sermonizing
and free my eyes!
Kigo: 牡丹 【ぼたん】 botan, tree peony.

Poem: 幽冥へおつるおとあり灯取虫
Romaji:
yūmei e 
otsuru oto ari 
hitorimushi
My translation:
To the Sea of Death
it plunged with a splash—
a tiger moth.
Kigo: 灯取虫
Notes: 幽冥へおつるおとあり (yūmei e otsuru oto ari) = there is a sound of falling into the underworld. A moth falls into the lamp — the sound of descent into death.

Poem: 死病えて爪うつくしき火桶かな
Romaji:
shibyō ete 
tsume utsukushiki 
hioke kana
My translation:
Sick unto death,
How lovely her fingernails 
on the wooden brazier!
Kigo: 桶

Poem: 紫陽花に八月の山たかからず
Romaji:
ajisai ni 
hachigatsu no yama t
akakarazu
My translation:
For the hydrangea
August mountains are never
sufficiently high.
Kigo: 夏の山 【なつのやま】 natsu no yama, summer mountain(s).

Poem: 落日に蹴合へる鶏や鳳仙花
Romaji:
rakujitsu ni 
keaeru tori ya 
hōsenka
My translation:
In the setting sun
cocks are engaged in a duel:
Touch-me-nots in bloom.
Kigo: 紫陽花 【あじさい】 ajisai, （あぢさゐ）, hydrangea (blossoms) [Hydrangea macrophylla] (mid summer).
Other translation:
as the sun sets
cocks kick at each other—
hydrangea

Poem: たましひのしづかにうつる菊見かな
Romaji:
tamashii no 
shizuka ni utsuru 
kikumi kana
My translation:
My soul moves along
quietly among the flowers—
a chrysanthemum exhibit.
Kigo: 菊 【きく】 kiku, chrysanthemums (all autumn).

Poem: 蚊の声や夜深くのぞく掛け鏡
Romaji:
ka no koe ya 
yo fukaku nozoku 
kakekagami
My translation:
A mosquito’s whine:
in the depth of night I peer
into a hanging mirror.
Kigo: 蚊 【か】 ka, mosquito(es) (all summer).
Notes: 夜深くのぞく掛け鏡 (yofukaku nozoku kakemirror) = a hanging mirror glimpsed deep in the night. A mosquito's whine; a mirror glimpsed deep in the night — nocturnal unease.

Poem: 月入れば北斗をめぐる千鳥かな
Romaji:
tsuki ireba 
hokuto wo meguru 
chidori kana
My translation:
As the moon has sunk
they fly round the Big Dipper—
the plovers.
Kigo: 千鳥 【ちどり】 chidori, plover(s) (all winter).
Notes: 月入れば北斗をめぐる (tsuki ireba hokuto wo meguru) = when the moon sets, the plovers circle the Big Dipper. Plovers wheeling around the Great Bear as the moon descends.

Poem: 遊泳やおぼるる水のかんばしき
Romaji:
yūei ya 
oboruru mizu no
kanbashiki
My translation:
Out for a swim:
the water that drowns people 
smells fragrant to me.
Kigo: 遊泳 【ゆうえい】 yūei, swimming (all summer).
Notes: 溺れる水のかんばしき (oboreru mizu no kanbashiki) = the fragrance of water one nearly drowns in. Swimming; the nearly-drowning water is fragrant.

Poem: 極寒のちりもとどめず巌ぶすま
Romaji:
gokkan no 
chiri mo todomezu 
iwa-busuma
My translation:
In the extreme cold
not a particle of dust
on the towering rock.
Kigo: 極寒 【ごっかん】 gokkan, extreme cold / midwinter (all winter).
Notes: 巌ぶすま (iwa-buton) = rock quilt. Extreme cold: the cliff-face holds not a speck of dust — absolute bareness.

Poem: 負馬の眼のまじと人を視る
Romaji:
make uma no 
me no majimaji to 
hito wo miru
My translation:
The eyes of a horse
that lost the race—how intently
they stare at men.
Kigo: 負馬 【おいうま】 oi-uma, pack horse / laden horse (autumn).
Notes: 眼のまじと人を視る (me no maji to hito wo miru) = looking at people with steady, unblinking eyes. A pack horse gazes at humans with an unwavering stare — unsettling reciprocity.

Poem: 雪山をはひまはりゐるこだまかな
Romaji:
setsuzan wo 
hai-mawari iru 
kodama kana
My translation:
Snow-covered mountains—
crawling about for a long while,
echoes and re-echoes.
Kigo: 雪山

Poem: 冬の蟇川にはなてばおよぎけり
Romaji:
fuyu no hiki 
kawa ni hanatebe 
oyogi-keri
My translation:
In winter, a toad.
I set it free in the river—
it begins to swim!
Kigo: 冬の蟇 【ふゆのがまがえる】 fuyu no gamagaeru, winter toad (all winter).
Notes: 川にはなてばおよぎけり (kawa ni hanateba oyogikeri) = when released into the river it swam. A winter toad released into the river — it swims. Surprise of life in the cold.

Poem: 夏真昼死は半眼に人をみる
Romaji:
natsu mahiru 
shi wa hangan ni 
hito wo miru
My translation:
High noon in summer:
Death, with half-closed eyes,
observes a man.
Kigo: 夏真昼 【なつまひる】 natsu-mahiru, summer high noon (all summer).
Notes: 死は半眼に人をみる (shi wa han-gan ni hito wo miru) = death looks at people through half-closed eyes. Summer high noon: death watches people with half-open eyes.

Poem: なにもゐぬ雪水ふかくうごきけり
Romaji:
nani mo inu 
yuki mizu fukaku 
ugoki-keri
My translation:
No creature is there—
And yet, deep in the thawing stream,
I have seen a stir.
Kigo: 雪水 【ゆきみず】 yukimizu, snowmelt water (early spring).
Notes: なにもゐぬ (nani mo inu) = nothing there. Snowmelt water moving deep and dark — nothing visible, yet clearly alive.

Poem: いのちつきて薬香さむくはなれかり
Romaji:
inochi tsukite 
yakukō samuku 
hanare-keri
My translation:
His life has ended—
the medicine’s smell coldly
leaves the body.
Kigo: 薬香 【くすりか】 kusuri-ka, scent of medicine (winter).
Notes: いのちつきて (inochi tsukite) = life exhausted. Life ebbing; medicine scent cold as it separates — a deathbed poem.

Poem: 父祖の地に闇のしづまる大晦日
Romaji:
fuso no chi ni 
yami no shizumaru 
ōmisoka
My translation:
In my forefathers’ land
darkness rests in calm
this New Year’s Eve.
Kigo: 大晦日 【おおみそか】 ōmisoka, New Year's Eve (New Year).
Notes: 父祖の地 (soso no chi) = ancestral land. Darkness settling on the ancestral land on New Year's Eve.

Poem: 凪ぎわたる地はうす眼して冬に入る
Romaji:
nagi-wataru 
chi wa usume shite
fuyu ni iru
My translation:
The perfectly still 
earth, with eyes almost closed,
enters on winter.
Kigo: 冬に入る 【ふゆにいる】 fuyu ni iru, entering winter (early winter).
Notes: 凪ぎわたる地はうす眼して (nagivwataru chi wa usumeite) = the becalmed land half-closes its eyes. The calm land squinting as it enters winter.

Poem: 焼き場の煙突の大いさをあふぐ
Romaji:
yakiba no 
entotsu no 
ōisa wo augu
My translation:
At a crematorium
I look high up
towards the chimney’s
immensity.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 焼き場の煙突 (yakiba no entotsu) = crematorium chimney. Looking up at a crematorium chimney. Free-verse haiku (jiyūritsu).

Poem: 夕日の中へ力いっぱい馬を追いかける
Romaji:
yūhi no 
naka e chikara ippai 
uma wo oikakeru
My translation:
Into the evening sun
with all my strength
I chase a horse.
Kigo: 夕日 【ゆうひ】 yūhi, setting sun (all autumn).
Notes: 力いっぱい (chikara ippai) = with all one's strength. Chasing a horse with all one's strength into the setting sun.

Poem: 柘榴が口あけたたはけた恋だ
Romaji:
zakuro ga 
kuchi aketa 
tawaketa koi da
My translation:
A pomegranate
has opened its mouth—
an idiotic
love affair.
Kigo: 柘榴 【ざくろ】 zakuro, pomegranate (mid autumn).
Notes: 口あけたたはけた恋 (kuchi aketa tawaketa koi) = foolish love that has opened its mouth. A pomegranate splitting open—a foolish love exposed.

Poem: 一日物云はず蝶の影さす
Romaji:
ichi-nichi 
mono iwazu 
chō no kage 
sasu
My translation:
Throughout the day
I did not speak a word:
the shadow of a butterfly
falls.
Kigo: 蝶の影 【ちょうのかげ】 chō no kage, butterfly shadow (all spring/summer).
Notes: 一日物云はず (ichinichi mono iwazu) = not saying a word all day. Not speaking all day; a butterfly's shadow passes.

Poem: 井戸の暗さにわが顔を見出す
Romaji:
ido no kurasa ni 
waga kao wo
miidasu
My translation:
In the darkness of a well
I recognize my face.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 井戸の暗さ (ido no kurasa) = the darkness of the well. Looking into the well's darkness and finding one's own face.

Poem: 人をそしる心をすて豆の皮むく
Romaji:
hito wo soshiru 
kokoro wo sute 
mame no kawa muku
My translation:
Trying to cast away
a slanderous heart
I shell the beans.
Kigo: 豆 【まめ】 mame, bean(s) (all summer).
Notes: 人をそしる心をすて (hito wo soshiru kokoro wo sute) = abandoning the heart that slanders. Stripping slander from the heart; peeling bean pods.

Poem: 烏がだまつてとんで行った
Romaji:
karasu ga 
damatte 
tonde itta
My translation:
The crow 
without saying a word 
flew away.
Kigo: 鴉 【からす】 karasu, crow (all autumn).
Notes: 烏がだまつてとんで行った (karasu ga damatsu tonde itta) = a crow flew away silently. A crow flying away in silence—the world without commentary.

Poem: 夜中の襖遠くしめられたる
Romaji:
yonaka no 
fusuma tōku 
shimeraretaru
My translation:
Late at night 
a sliding door 
in the distance 
is closed.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 夜中の襖 (yonaka no fusuma) = sliding door in the night. A sliding door shut far away in the night—distance and silence.

Poem: 山の夕陽の墓地の空海はかたぶく
Romaji:
yama no yūhi no 
bochi no sora umi e 
katabuku
My translation:
The sky above a mountain graveyard
in the evening sun
slants towards the ocean.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: Mountain sunset; graveyard; sky tilting to sea—elemental loneliness.

Poem: 淋しいからだから爪がのび出す
Romaji:
sabishii karada kara 
tsume ga nobi-dasu
My translation:
From a lonely body
fingernails begin to grow.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 淋しいからだから (sabishii karada kara) = from this lonely body. Nails growing from the lonely body—the body's inescapable autonomy.

Poem: うつろの心に眼が二つあいてゐる
Romaji:
utsurono kokoro ni 
me ga futatsu 
aite-iru
My translation:
In the hollow mind
a pair of eyes
opens.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: うつろの心 (utsuro no kokoro) = the empty heart. An empty heart with two eyes wide open.

Poem: 春が来たと大きな新聞広告
Romaji:
Spring is here—
so says a spacious
newspaper ad.
My translation:
haru ga 
kita to ōkina 
shinbun kōkoku
Kigo: 春が来た 【はるがきた】 haru ga kita, spring has come (early spring).
Notes: Spring announced in a large newspaper advertisement—modernity flattening the seasonal.

Poem: お祭り赤ん坊寝てゐる
Romaji:
The festival:
a baby
is asleep.
My translation:
omatsuri 
akanbō 
nete-iru
Kigo: お祭り omatsuri, festival (all autumn).
Notes: Festival; a baby sleeping—life indifferent to festivity.

Poem: すばらしい乳房だ蚊がいる
Romaji:
subarashii 
chibusa da 
ka ga iru
My translation:
Splendid breasts—
there is a mosquito.
Kigo: 蚊 【か】 ka, mosquito(es) (all summer).
Notes: A wonderful breast; but there's a mosquito—comic deflation.

Poem: 月夜の葦がおれとる
Romaji:
tsukiyo no 
ashi ga 
ore-toru
My translation:
Moonlit night:
a reed
is broken.
Kigo: 葦 【あし】 ashi, reed (all autumn).
Notes: 月夜の葦がおれとる (tsukiyo no ashi ga oretoru) = moonlit reeds are breaking. Moonlit reeds snapping—autumnal fragility.

Poem: 切られる花を病人見てゐる
Romaji:
kirareru
hana wo byōnin 
mite-iru
My translation:
An ailing person
watches
a flower
being cut.
Kigo: 花 【はな】 hana, (cherry) blossoms [in haiku and haikai the simple word hana 花 refers to cherry blossoms, as do all kigo listed here; but note that in Manyōshū and some other early poetry hana was understood as referring to ume 梅【うめ】plum blossoms, an early spring topic] (late spring).
Notes: 切られる花を病人見てゐる = a sick person watching flowers being cut. The sick person and the cut flower mirror each other.

Poem: 足のうら洗へば白くなる
Romaji:
ashi no ura 
araeba 
shiroku naru
My translation:
As I wash the sole of my foot 
it becomes white.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: Washing the soles of the feet—they become white. Free-verse haiku.

Poem: 流れに沿うて歩いてとまる
Romaji:
nagare ni 
sōte aruite 
tomaru
My translation:
With the flow of the stream
I walk
and pause.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: Walking along the stream, then stopping—contemplative wandering. Free-verse haiku.

Poem: 畳を歩く雀の足音を知って居る
Romaji:
tatami wo aruku 
suzume no ashioto wo 
shitte-iru
My translation:
The footsteps of a sparrow
walking on the tatami floor
sound familiar.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: Knowing the sound of sparrow footsteps on tatami. Free-verse haiku.

Poem: 墓のうらに廻る
Romaji:
haka no ura ni
mawaru
My translation:
To the back of a tombstone 
I go round.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: Going to the back of the grave—a humble act of private intimacy with the dead. Free-verse haiku.

Romaji:
ichinichi
mono iwazu
chō no kage sasu
My translation:
All day long
I don't say word:
A butterfly casts its shadow.

Romaji:
tsukemono oke ni
shio fure to
haha wa unda ka
My translation:
"Shake some salt
In the pickle tub!"
Is that why my mother bore me?

Poem: 咳をしても一人
Romaji:
seki wo shite mo
hitori
My translation:
even coughing
I'm alone
Kigo: cough

Poem: 岩つかむ鳶もよろめ東風強し
Romaji:
iwa tsukamu
tobi mo yorome
kochi tsuyoshi
My translation:
clutching a boulder
the black-kite totters
in the strong east wind
Kigo:
East wind
東風 kochi

Poem: 大火事に明るき空や手水鉢
Romaji:
ōkaji ni 
akaruki sora ya 
chōzubachi
My translation:
Under the sky,
brightened by a large fire, 
a washing basin.
Kigo: 大火事 【おおかじ】 ōkaji, great fire (winter).
Notes: 手水鉢 (chōzubachi) = stone water basin. The sky bright from the great fire; the water basin glows.

Poem: 花屑に口開く鯉や夏めきて
Romaji:
hana kuzu ni 
kuchi aku koi ya 
natsu-mekite
My translation:
To the falling shreds 
of blossoms a carp opens its mouth:
summer has come.
Kigo: 花屑 【はなくず】 hanakuzu, fallen blossom fragments (mid spring).
Notes: Carp surfacing for fallen petals; the season feels summery—夏めきて.

Poem: 朝寒や汽鑵車ぬくく顔を過ぐ
Romaji:
asazamu ya 
kikansha nukuku 
kao wo sugu
My translation:
The morning cold:
a stream engine passes
warmly before my face.
Kigo: 朝寒 【あさざむ】 asazamu, morning cold (late autumn).
Notes: Morning cold; a warm locomotive passes close to the face.

Poem: 向き定めて流れそめたる木の実かな
Romaji:
muki kimete 
nagare sometaru 
konomi kana
My translation:
After deciding
which way to turn, a berry
begins to float down.
Kigo: 木の実 【このみ】 konomi, nut/fruit/berry [or plurals; of a tree or shrub; note that the common vernacular pronunciation きのみ ki no mi, is not used for this term in haikai] (all autumn).
Notes: A tree nut finds its direction and starts to float downstream—autumn water carrying seeds.

Poem: 銀閣寺門前の田の案山子かな
Romaji:
ginkakuji 
monzen no ta no 
kakashi kana
My translation:
Silver Pavilion―
in the paddy before its gate,
a scarecrow.
Kigo: 案山子 【かかし】 kakashi, scarecrow (all autumn).
Notes: 銀閣寺 (Ginkakuji). A scarecrow in a rice field in front of Ginkakuji—the pastoral and the elegant.

Poem: 洋館の日本料理や松の花
Romaji:
yōkan no 
nihon ryōri ya 
matsu no hana
My translation:
At a western-style house
Japanese dishes are served:
blossoms on a pine tree.
Kigo: 松の花 【まつのはな】 matsu no hana, pine pollen / pine flower (all spring).
Notes: 洋館の日本料理 (yōkan no nihon ryōri) = Japanese food in a Western building. A Western building serves Japanese food in spring.

Poem: 箱庭に病葉落ちて大いなり
Romaji:
hakoniwa ni 
byōyō ochite 
ōinari
My translation:
Into the miniature
garden a sick leaf has fallen,
and how large it is!
Kigo: 病葉 【わくらば】 wakuraba, weak/sickly/pale leaves [losing the colors of their prime] (late summer).
Notes: 箱庭 (hakoniwa) = miniature garden. A blighted leaf falls into the miniature garden—disproportionately large.

Poem: 蝶低し葵の花の低ければ
Romaji:
chō hikushi 
aoi no hana no 
hikukereba
My translation:
Butterflies fly low
because the hollyhock
flowers are low.
Kigo: 葵 【あおい】 aoi, （あおひ）, hollyhock / althea [Alcea rosea; not to be confused with 木槿【むくげ】 mukuge, rose of Sharon / shrub althea, Hybiscus syriacus], and autumn kidai (mid summer).
Notes: 蝶低し (chō hikushi) = the butterfly flies low. The butterfly flies as low as the hollyhock flowers.

Poem: よろこべばしきりに落つる木の実かな
Romaji:
yorokobeba 
shikirini otsuru
ko no mi kana
My translation:
As I rejoice
they fall time and time again
nuts from the tree.
Kigo: 木の実 【このみ】 konomi, nut/fruit/berry [or plurals; of a tree or shrub; note that the common vernacular pronunciation きのみ ki no mi, is not used for this term in haikai] (all autumn).
Notes: よろこべば (yorokobeba) = when one rejoices. When happy, nuts fall one after another.

Poem: 樫の実を掃くばかりなり墓掃除
Romaji:
kashi no mi wo
haku bakari nari
haka sōji
My translation:
Sweeping off the acorns
is all I need to do, when
cleaning the graves.
Kigo: 樫の実 【かしのみ】 kashi no mi, acorn (all autumn).
Notes: Sweeping graves, only acorns to sweep—quiet, meditative labor.

Poem: ハンケチ振って別れも愉し少女等は
Romaji:
hankechi futte 
wakare mo tanoshi 
otome-ra wa
My translation:
Waving handkerchiefs,
they even enjoy a parting:
the young maidens.
Kigo: 夏 【なつ】 natsu, summer.
Notes: ハンケチ振って (hankachi futte) = waving handkerchiefs. Girls waving handkerchiefs at parting—joyful and carefree.

Poem: 望月のふと歪みしと見しはいかに
Romaji:
mochizuki no 
futo yugamishi to 
mishi wa ikani
My translation:
The full moon, for
a moment, looked misshapen
and I wonder why.
Kigo: 望月 【もちつき】 mochizuki, full moon (mid autumn).
Notes: Did the full moon warp for just an instant?—questioning the reliability of perception.

Poem: 本読めば本の中より虫の声
Romaji:
hon yomeba 
hon no naka yori 
mushi no koe
My translation:
I read a book—
somewhere within the book
An insect chirps.
Kigo: 虫の声 【むしのこえ】 mushi no koe, insect voices (all autumn).
Notes: 本読めば (hon yomeba) = when I read a book. Reading: an insect's voice emerges from between the pages.

Poem: ガソリンの真赤き天馬春の雨
Romaji:
gasorin no 
ma-akaki tenba 
haru no ame
My translation:
At the gas station
a bright red Pegasus—
spring rain.
Kigo: 春の雨 【はるのあめ】 haru no ame, spring rain (all spring).
Notes: A red gasoline truck as a heavenly horse in the spring rain—modernity and myth.

Poem: 一めんの落花の水に蛙の眼
Romaji:
ichimen no 
rakka no mizu ni 
kaeru no me
My translation:
All over the water
fallen blossoms spread, and amongst them
a frog’s eyes.
Kigo: 落花 【らっか】 rakka, （らくくわ）, falling (cherry) blossoms (late spring).
Notes: A frog's eye in a sea of floating petals—the frog's perspective.

Poem: 多勢の眼に一片の散紅葉
Romaji:
ōnei no 
me ni hitohira no 
chiri momiji
My translation:
Before a great many 
people’s eyes a solitary 
tinted leaf falls.
Kigo: 散紅葉 【ちりもみじ】 chiri-momiji, scattering autumn leaves (late autumn).
Notes: 多勢の眼 (ōzei no me) = many eyes. Many watching; a single autumn leaf catches all eyes as it falls.

Poem: よろぼへる蛾も林中の閑かさに
Romaji:
yoroboeru ga 
mo rinchū no 
shizukasa ni
My translation:
It totters too—
a moth, under the stillness
of the grove.
Kigo: 蛾 【が】 ga, moth (all summer).
Notes: Even a stumbling moth partakes of the forest's stillness.

Poem: 一茎の百合の全力一蕾に
Romaji:
ikkei no 
yuri no zenryoku 
ichirai ni
My translation:
A lily stalk
concentration all its might
into one flower bud.
Kigo: 百合 【ゆり】 yuri, lily (all summer).
Notes: 一茎の百合の全力 (ikkei no yuri no zenryoku) = all the lily's force. A single lily stalk's entire power concentrated in one bud.

Poem: 父のごとまた母のごと大夏木
Romaji:
chichi no goto 
mata haha no goto 
ō-natsuki
My translation:
Like a father
and also like a mother,
The huge summer tree.
Kigo: 夏木 【なつき】 natsuki, summer tree (all summer).
Notes: 父のごとまた母のごと (chichi no goto mata haha no goto) = like a father, and like a mother. A great summer tree as both father and mother.

Poem: 満月を生みし湖山の息づかひ
Romaji:
mangetsu wo 
umishi kozan no 
ikizukai
My translation:
After giving birth
to a full moon, lakeside mountains
breathe in and out.
Kigo: 満月 【まんげつ】 mangetsu, full moon (mid autumn).
Notes: The mountain and lake's breath giving birth to the full moon.

Poem: 春暁や水車の落す夜の水
Romaji:
shungyō ya
suisha no otosu
yoru no mizu
My translation:
spring dawnー
the waterwheel dropping
night water
Kigo:
Spring dawn
春暁 shungyō

Romaji:
sabishisa ni
mata dora utsu ya
kabiya mori
My translation:
In his loneliness
Once again he strikes the gong—
The deer-fire watchmen.

Romaji:
kaei basa to
fumu beku arinu
soba no tsuki
My translation:
Blossom shadows blur—
I might have stepped on them!
Moon of the mountain path.

Romaji:
chōjō ya
koto ni nogiku no
fukareori
My translation:
The crest of the hill—
The camomiles especially
Are blown by the wind.

Poem: 鮒売や春めく笊を打ち重ね
Romaji:
funa uri ya
haru-meku zaru wo
uchi kasane
My translation:
carp peddler―
vernal bamboo baskes
piled up
Kigo:
Vernal signs
春めくharu-meku

Poem: 貧しけれどもクリスマスの夜の父ありぬ
Romaji:
mazushi keredo
kurisumasu no yo no
chichi arinu
My translation:
we may be poor,
but on Chirstmas Eve
Dad is home
Kigo: Christmas

Poem: 五色に塗る餅柔かしお命講
Romaji:
goshiki ni 
nuru mochi yawarakashi 
o-meikoo
My translation:
the mochi cakes
in five colors and so soft ...
memorial for Saint Nichiren
Kigo: 餅 【もち】 mochi, rice cake (New Year).
Notes: 五色に塗る餅 (goshiki ni nuru mochi) = five-colored rice cakes. Soft five-colored mochi for the お命講 (o-inochi-kō) longevity assembly.

Poem: 摩利支天の露店の上や春の月
Romaji:
marishiten no
roten no ue ya
haru no tsuki
My translation:
above the shops
at the Marishiten Festival -
the spring moon
Kigo: 春の月 【はるのつき】 haru no tsuki, spring moon (all spring).
Notes: 摩利支天 (Marishiten) = Marici, deity of the sun and moon. A roadside stand beneath the spring moon at Marishiten shrine.

Poem: 大橋を恵方へ渡り詣りけり
Romaji:
oohashi wo 
ehoo e watari 
mairi keri
My translation:
crossing the Great Bridge
in the auspicious direction
for the New Year
Kigo: 恵方参り 【えほうまいり】 ehōmairi, New Year's directional pilgrimage (New Year).
Notes: 大橋を恵方へ渡り (ōhashi wo ehō e watari) = crossing the great bridge toward the auspicious direction. Crossing the great bridge in the auspicious direction for the New Year pilgrimage.

Poem: 重陽や椀の蒔絵のことごとし
Romaji:
chooyoo ya 
wan no makie no 
koto gotoshi
My translation:
Chrysanthemum Festival -
in the bowl this laquer image
almost the same
Kigo: 重陽 【ちょうよう】 chōyō, Double Nine Festival [9th day of 9th month] (mid autumn).
Notes: 椀の蒔絵のことごとし (wan no makie no kotogotoshi) = the lacquerwork on the bowl is elaborate. Elaborate lacquerwork bowls at the chrysanthemum festival.

Romaji:
Musashino no 
tori kuru matsu no 
shin mugen
My translation:
birds of Musashino plain
coming to the pine candles -
infinity

Poem: 御所人形の稚児輪ふくらむ牡丹の芽
Romaji:
gosho ningyoo 
no chigowa fukuramu 
botan no me
My translation:
the fluffy hairdo
of this Gosho doll -
bud of a peony
Kigo: 牡丹の芽 【ぼたんのめ】 botan no me, peony bud (early spring).
Notes: 御所人形 (gosho-ningyō) = court doll. A court doll's childlike topknot swelling like a peony bud.

Poem: 西鶴の女みな死ぬ夜の秋
Romaji:
Saikaku no 
onna mina shinu 
yoru no aki
My translation:
the heroines of Saikaku
all die in the end
autumn night
Kigo: 夜の秋 【よるのあき】 yoru no aki, autumn night (early autumn).
Notes: 西鶴の女みな死ぬ (Saikaku no onna mina shinu) = all Saikaku's women die. All the women in Ihara Saikaku's novels die on this autumn night.

Poem: 初夏や路の一本がつくる陰
Romaji:
hatsu natsu ya
michi no ippon ga
tsukuru kage
My translation:
early summer-
the road's one tree
makes a shadow
Kigo: 初夏 shoka Early summer

Poem: 山鴉春立つ空に乱れけり
Romaji:
yama-garasu
haru tatsu sora ni
midare keri
My translation:
mountain crows
in the early spring sky
disordered
Kigo: Beginning of spring

Poem: 春の山らくだのごとくならびけり
Romaji:
haru no yama
rakuda no gotoku
narabi keri
My translation:
spring mountains
lined up
just line a camel
Kigo: Spring mountain

Poem: 春暁や雨のあらひし松の幹
Romaji:
shungyō ya
ame no araishi
matsu no miki
My translation:
spring dawnー
trunk of the pine
washed by rain
Kigo:
Spring dawn
春暁 shungyō

Poem: 東風吹くや耳あらわるるうなひ髪
Romaji:
kochi fuku ya
mimi arawaruru
nai-gami
My translation:
the east wind blows一
her ears show through
nape-length hair
Kigo:
East wind
東風 kochi

Poem: 春暁や水のみに来る鳥の声
Romaji:
shungyō ya
mizu nomi ni kuru
tori no koe
My translation:
spring dawnー
songs of birds come
to drink water
Kigo:
Spring dawn
春暁 shungyō

Poem: 元日や手を洗ひをる夕ごころ
Romaji:
ganjitsu ya
te wo arai-oru
yū-gokoro
My translation:
New Years Day
washing my hands
evening heart
Kigo: New Years Day
Notes: yugokoro: gloomy feeling at the end of the day. New Years Day is a bright happy day, but at the end of it the author feels the sadness of it ending while washing his hands in the bathroom

Poem: 秋立つ日うろ歯に銀をうづめけり
Romaji:
aki tatsu hi 
uroba ni gin wo
uzume-keri
My translation:
The day autumn began
I had a cavity in my tooth
filled with silver.
Kigo: 秋立つ 【あきたつ】 aki tatsu, autumn begins (early autumn).
Notes: 虫歯に銀をうづめけり (mushiba ni gin wo uzumekeri) = silver filled into a decayed tooth. On the first day of autumn, silver packed into a cavity — precise, comic, wry.

Poem: 白菊や匂にもある影日なた
Romaji:
shiragiku ya
nioi ni mo aru
kage hinata
My translation:
White chrysanthemums:
in the fragrance, too, there are
light and shade.
Kigo: 白菊 【しらぎく】 shiragiku, white chrysanthemum (mid autumn).
Notes: 匂にもある影日なた (nioi ni mo aru kage hinata) = even in the fragrance there is shade and sun. The white chrysanthemum's fragrance itself has shadow and sunlight.

Poem: 木がらしや目刺にのこる海のいろ
Romaji:
kogarashi ya
mezashi ni nokoru
umi no iro
My translation:
Wintry gusts:
on the sardine still lingers
the ocean’s colour.
Kigo: 木がらし 【こがらし】 kogarashi, wintry gust (early winter).
Notes: 目刺にのこる海のいろ (mezashi ni nokoru umi no iro) = the sea's color remaining in the dried sardine. A wintry gust; the sea's color still lives in the eye of a dried sardine.

Poem: 蝶の舌ゼンマイに似る暑さかな
Romaji:
chō no shita
zenmai ni niru
atsusa kana
My translation:
The butterfly’s tongue
resembles a steel spring—
what a hot day!
Kigo: 暑さ 【あつさ】 atsusa, heat (all summer).
Notes: 蝶の舌ゼンマイに似る (chō no shita zenmai ni niru) = a butterfly's tongue resembles a coiled spring. In the heat, a butterfly's proboscis coiled like a watch spring — precise entomological observation.

Poem: 青蛙おのれもペンキ塗りたてか
Romaji:
aogaeru
onoree mo penki
nuritate ka
My translation:
Green frog,
have you also had your body
freshly painted?
Kigo: 青蛙 【あおがえる】 aogaeru, （あおがへる）, green frog [hyla species] (all summer).
Notes: 自身もペンキ塗りたてか (jishin mo penki nuritare ka) = have you yourself just been freshly painted? The green frog: have you too just been freshly painted? — comic modernity.

Poem: 蟻地獄陰して牡丹花赤き
Romaji:
arijigoku 
kage shite botan
hana akaki
My translation:
An ant lion’s pit
is hidden underneath a peony
blossoming in red.
Kigo: 牡丹 【ぼたん】 botan, tree peony (early summer).
Notes: 蟻地獄陰して (ari-jigoku kageshite) = an antlion pit giving shade. An antlion pit shading the brilliantly red peony — predation beside beauty.

Poem: 熱を病んで桜明りに震へゐる
Romaji:
netsu wo yande
sakura akari ni
furue iru
My translation:
Sick and feverish
in the gleam of cherry blossoms
I keep shivering.
Kigo: 桜明り 【さくらあかり】 sakura-akari, cherry-blossom glow (mid spring).
Notes: Fevered, trembling in the cherry-blossom light — illness illuminated by spring beauty.

Poem: 山の月冴えて落葉の匂かな
Romaji:
yama no tsuki
saete ochiba no
nioi kana
My translation:
The moon above the hill
is serene; under it the smell
of fallen leaves.
Kigo: 落葉 【おちば】 ochiba, fallen leaves (all autumn).
Notes: 山の月冴えて (yama no tsuki saete) = the mountain moon sharp and clear. A sharp mountain moon; fallen leaves fragrant — autumn at its clearest.

Poem: 赤百合の蕋黒む暑さ極りぬ
Romaji:
akayuri no
shibe kuromu atsusa
kiwamarinu
My translation:
The red lily’s pistil
darkens as the hot spell
reaches its peak.
Kigo: 暑さ極まる 【あつさきわまる】 atsusa kiwamaru, heat at its peak / great heat (late summer).
Notes: 赤百合の蕋黒む (aka-yuri no shibe kuramu) = the red lily's stamens blacken. The red lily's stamens blackening in the peak heat — excess of summer.

Poem: 秋風や黒子に生えし毛一根
Romaji:
akikaze ya
hokuro ni haeshi
ke ikkon
My translation:
The wind of autumn:
a hair has begun to grow
on my mole.
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn).
Notes: 黒子に生えし毛一根 (hokuro ni haeshi ke ichi ne) = a single hair growing from a mole. Autumn wind; a single hair grown from a mole — microscopic, wry observation.

Poem: 松風や人は月下に松露を掘る
Romaji:
matsukaze ya
hito wa gekka ni
shōro wo horu
My translation:
Wind through the pine trees:
in the moonlight someone 
digs truffles.
Kigo: 松露 【しょうろ】 shōro, pine mushroom / truffle (all autumn).
Notes: 松風や人は月下に松露を掘る (matsukaze ya hito wa gekkka ni shōro wo horu) — pine wind; people dig for pine truffles in the moonlight.

Poem: 炎天に上りて消える箕の埃
Romaji:
enten ni
noborite kieru 
mi no hokori
My translation:
The the sweltering sky
it rises and disappears:
dust from the winnowing.
Kigo: 炎天 【えんてん】 enten, blazing sky (late summer).
Notes: 箕の埃 (mi no hokori) = dust from a winnowing basket. Dust from a winnowing basket rising into the blazing sky and vanishing.

Poem: 石の垢ものうき水の目ざしかな
Romaji:
ishi no aka
monouki mizu no
hizashi kana
My translation:
Slime on the stones—
gloomily through the water
the rays of the sun.
Kigo: 水の目ざし 【みずのめざし】 mizu no mezashi, the gaze of water (summer).
Notes: 石の垢ものうき (ishi no aka mono uki) = algae on stones lazily floating. The stones' algae and the water's languid gaze — enervating summer stillness.

Poem: 木の枝の瓦にさはる暑さかな
Romaji:
ki no eda no
kawara ni sawaru
atsusa kana
My translation:
Branches of a tree
touching the tiles of the roof—
how hot it is!
Kigo: 暑さ 【あつさ】 atsusa, heat (all summer).
Notes: 木の枝の瓦にさはる (ko no eda no kawara ni sawaru) = a branch touching the roof tile. A branch touching the roof tile in the heat — everything in contact, sweltering.

Poem: 静かさに堪えず散りけり夏椿
Romaji:
shizukasa ni
taezu chiri-keri
natsu tsubaki
My translation:
Unable to stand
with the stillness, it falls—
summer camellia.
Kigo: 夏椿 【なつつばき】 natsu-tsubaki, summer camellia (early summer).
Notes: 静かさに堪えず散りけり (shizukasa ni taedzu chirikeri) = unable to bear the silence, it scattered. Unable to endure the quiet, the summer camellia falls.

Poem: 初秋の蝗つかめば柔かき
Romaji:
hatsu aki no
inago tsukameba
yawarakaki
My translation:
Early autumn—
as I grab a grasshopper,
how soft it feels!
Kigo: 初秋 【しょしゅう】 shoshu, early autumn. / 蝗 【いなご】 inago, grasshopper/locust [small, green grasshoppers in the Acrididae (short-horned) family, sometimes cooked and eaten] (all autumn).
Notes: 初秋の蝗つかめば柔かき (shoshu no inago tsukameba yawarakaki) = locusts of early autumn are soft when grasped. Early-autumn locusts: soft in the hand — their bodies not yet hardened.

Poem: 秋風や甲羅をあます膳の蟹
Romaji:
akikaze ya
kōra wo amasu
zen no kani
My translation:
The wind of autumn:
only the carapace remains
of a crab on the tray.
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn). / 蟹 【かに】 kani, crab [note: these are all small crabs, generally not eaten] (all summer).
Notes: 甲羅をあます膳の蟹 (kōra wo amasu zen no kani) = crab on the tray with leftover shell. Autumn wind; the crab's shell left over on the tray — the feast and its remnants.

Poem: 兎も片耳垂るる大暑かな
Romaji:
usagi mo 
kata-mimi taruru
taisho kana
My translation:
Even the rabbit
droops one of her ears—
midsummer heat!
Kigo: 大暑 【たいしょ】 taisho, great heat (late summer).
Notes: 兎も片耳垂るる (usagi mo kataimi taruru) = even the rabbit droops one ear. In the great heat, even the rabbit droops one ear — the whole world wilting.

Poem: うららかに毛虫わたるや松の枝
Romaji:
uraranani 
kemushi wataru ya
matsu no eda
My translation:
Under the bright sky
a hairy caterpillar crawls
on the pine tree’s branch.
Kigo: 毛虫 【けむし】 kemushi, woolybear / hairy caterpillar [distinguish 尺取【しゃくとり shakutori, inchworm / looper, also an all-summer season word] (all summer).
Notes: うらゝかに (uraraka ni) = brightly, serenely. A caterpillar crossing a pine branch in the bright spring light — unhurried beauty.

Poem: 水洟や鼻の先だけ暮れ残る
Romaji:
mizubana ya
hana no saki dake 
kure nokoru
My translation:
My runny nose:
everywhere, except on that spot,
evening dusk falls.
Kigo: 水洟 【みずはな】 mizu-hana, runny nose / watery mucus (all winter).
Notes: 鼻の先だけ暮れ残る (hana no saki dake kure nokoru) = only the tip of the nose remains in the light. Only the tip of the nose still catching the last light — winter dusk.

Poem: 海の空まだ春暁をわかつなし
Romaji:
umi to sora
mada shungyo wo
wakatsu nashi
My translation:
sea and sky
by the spring dawn
not yet separated
Kigo:
Spring dawn
春暁 shungyō

Poem: 見あぐるや山躑躅燃ゆ熔岩の上
Kigo: 山躑躅 【やまつつじ】 yama-tsutsuji, mountain azalea (mid spring/early summer).
Notes: 見あぐるや (miaguru ya) = looking up at. Looking up at mountain azaleas blazing on the lava — the raw volcanic landscape and spring fire.

Poem: 見るかぎり蘆花ゆらぎゐて暮るるかな
Romaji:
miru kagiri 
roka yuragiite 
kururu kana
My translation:
Everywhere in sight
reed tassels waver, as
night begins to fall.
Kigo: 蘆花 【ろか】 roka, reed-plume / reed flower (mid autumn).
Notes: 見るかぎり蘆花ゆらぎゐて (miru kagiri roka yuragite) = as far as the eye can see, reed plumes swaying. Reed plumes swaying to the horizon at dusk.

Poem: 春愁のかぎりを躑躅燃えにけり
Romaji:
shunshū no
kagiri wo tsutsuji
moenikeri
My translation:
the limits of 
spring melencoly, azaleas
are burning
Kigo: azaleas (躑躅)・春
Notes: Spring azalea (躑躅) at its limit — spring grief burning out.

Poem: 綺羅星の中の青きが流れけり
Romaji:
kiraboshi no
naka no aoki ga
nagarekeri
My translation:
the glitering galaxy
within blue star 
flows
Kigo: Shooting star (流れ星)・秋
Notes: A blue shooting star among glittering stars — the one that moves.

Poem: 冬ざれやころゝとなける檻の鶴
Romaji:
fuyu zareya
kokoro to nakeru
ori no tsuru
My translation:
dead of winter—
crying ko, ro, ro
the caged crane
Kigo: dead of winter (冬ざれ)・冬
Notes: 冬ざれ (dead of winter): a caged crane calling softly — captive bird in bleak season.

Poem: 日輪や蝌蚪の水輪の只中に
Romaji:
nichirin ya
kato no minowa no
tada naka ni
My translation:
helos—
exactly in the middle of
tadpoles' ripples
Kigo: tadpole (蝌蚪)・春
Notes: The sun-disc; tadpole water-rings — the cosmic and the microscopic.

Poem: 沈丁の葉ごもる花も濡れし雨
Romaji:
jinchō no
hagomoru hana mo 
nureshi ame
My translation:
the rain moistens
even the clove flowers
covered with leaves
Kigo: clove flowers (沈丁花)・春
Notes: 沈丁花 (daphne) hidden in leaves, wet in rain — fragrant concealment.

Poem: 遠泳や高浪越ゆる一の列
Romaji:
enei ya
takanami koyuru
ichi no retsu
My translation:
long distance swimmers—
going over a high wave
a single line
Kigo: swimming (水泳)・夏
Notes: Open-water swimming: a file of swimmers cresting high waves.

Poem: 高嶺星蚕飼の村は寝しづまり
Romaji:
takaneboshi
kai no mura wa
ne shizumari
My translation:
star of the high peak
the magnanery village
settles down to sleep
Kigo: sericulture (蚕飼)・春
Notes: High-peak stars; a silkworm-rearing village asleep.

Poem: 焼岳のよひも燃ゆる新樹かな
Romaji:
yakedake no
koyohimo moyuru
shinjū kana
My translation:
Burning Peak
burning again tonight
sprouting trees
Kigo: new tree (新樹)・夏
Notes: 焼岳 (Mt. Yakeyama) glowing at dusk; new summer foliage burning.

Poem: 海贏打や灯ともり給ふ観世音
Romaji:
bai utchi ya
hi tomori-tamau
kanzeon
My translation:
kids playing caps
the sacred lights come on
Kanseon
Kigo: playing caps (海贏打)・秋
Notes: 海贏打 (shell-game): the goddess Kannon lights the lamp.

Poem: 多摩川や堤焼きゐるわたし守
Romaji:
Tamagawa ya
tsutsumi yakiiru
watarimori
My translation:
Tamagawa River—
the ferry men
burning the banks
Kigo: bank burning (堤焼く)・春
Notes: Tama River; a ferryman burning the bank in spring.

Poem: ふるさとや馬追なける風の中
Romaji:
furusato ya
umaoi nakeru
kaze no naka
My translation:
hometown—
the grasshoppers crip
in the wind
Kigo: grasshopper (馬追)・秋
Notes: Hometown; a katydid crying in the autumn wind.

Poem: 桑の葉の照るに堪へゆく帰省かな
Romaji:
kuwa no ha no
teru ni taeyuku
kisei kana
My translation:
enduring
the shining on mulberry  leaves
returning home
Kigo: homecoming (帰省)・夏
Notes: Mulberry leaves gleaming; enduring the heat on the way home.
Other translation:
How the mulberry leaves
shine, as I trudge along the way
towards my parents’ home! (Ueda, Modern)

Poem: 葛飾や桃の籬も水田べり
Romaji:
katsushika ya
momo no magaki mo
mizutaberi
My translation:
at Katsushika—
peach fence also
edge of paddy water
Kigo: peach (桃) ・春
Notes: Katsushika district; peach hedges beside the paddies.

Poem: 青春のすぎにしこころ苺喰ふ
Romaji:
seisyun no
suginishi kokoro
ichigo kuu
My translation:
the heart of
youth now passed
eating straberries
Kigo: straberry (苺)・夏
Notes: Youth past; eating summer strawberries in memory.

Poem: なく雲雀松風立ちて落ちにけむ
Romaji:
naku hibari
matsu kaze tachite
ochi ni kemu
My translation:
crying skylark
pine wind rose
then fell
Kigo: skylark (雲雀)・春
Notes: A calling skylark; pine wind rises then falls.

Poem: 春惜しむおんすがたこそとこしなへ
Romaji:
haru oshimu
on sugata koso
tokoshinae
My translation:
in its lament for the passing spring
the honored form becomes
Eternal
Kigo: passing spring (春惜しむ)・春
Notes: Lamenting departing spring — the figure's form eternal.

Poem: 人が焼く天の山火を奪ふもの
Romaji:
hito ga yaku
ame no yamabi wo
ubau mono
My translation:
the one who steals
Heaven mountains fire
that people burn
Kigo: burning mountain (山焼)・春
Notes: Mountain burning: something steals fire from the sky.

Poem: 啄木鳥や落葉をいそぐ牧の木々
Romaji:
kitsutsuki ya
ochiba wo isogu
maki no kigi
My translation:
woodpecker—
speeding the falling leaves
pasture's trees
Kigo: falling leaves (落葉)・冬
Notes: A woodpecker; pasture trees hurrying to shed leaves.

Poem: 天平のをとめぞ立てる雛かな
Romaji:
tenpō no
tome zo tateru
hina kana
My translation:
a Tempō
maiden! Standing 
doll
Kigo: doll (雛)・春
Notes: A Nara-period maiden stands up — the Dolls' Festival.

Poem: 馬酔木咲く金堂の扉にわが触れぬ
Romaji:
ashibi saku
kondō no to ni
waga furenu
My translation:
my hand touches
the door of the Golden Hall
where andomeda bloom
Kigo: andomeda (馬酔木)・春
Notes: Andromeda (馬酔木 pieris) blooms; touching the golden hall's door.

Poem: 蟇ないて唐招提寺春いづこ
Romaji:
hiki naite
tōshōdaiji
haru izuko
My translation:
toads croak
Tōshōdaiji Temple
where is spring
Kigo: where is spring (春いづこ)・春
Notes: A toad calls at Tōshōdaiji — where is spring?

Poem: 厨子の前望のひかりの来てゐたり
Romaji:
zushi no mae
mochi no hikari
kiteitari
My translation:
in front of the alter box
the light of the harvest moon
has come
Kigo: harvest moon (望) ・秋
Notes: Moonlight (望) before the shrine cabinet — harvest moon light.

Poem: 馬酔木より低き門なり浄瑠璃寺
Romaji:
ashibi yori
hikuki kado nari
jōruriji
My translation:
its gate shorter
than the andromeda
Jōruri Temple
Kigo: andomeda (馬酔木)・春
Notes: The gate at Jōruji temple lower than the andromeda blooms.

Poem: 或る門のくづれて居るに馬酔木かな
Romaji:
aru mon no
kuzurete oru ni
ashibi kana
My translation:
where there is a 
crumbling gate
andomeda
Kigo: andomeda (馬酔木)・春
Notes: A crumbling gate with andromeda — ruin and bloom.

Poem: 唐黍の影を横たふ舟路かな
Romaji:
tōkibi no
kage wo yokotau
funa ji kana
My translation:
the shadow of the corn
leans across
the boat road
Kigo: corn (唐黍)・秋
Notes: Corn shadows laid across the boat-path in autumn.

Poem: 柴漬や古利根けふの日を沈む
Romaji:
fushizuke ya
furutone kyō no
hi wo shizumu
My translation:
fish trap—
at Old lake Tobe the sun
of today sets
Kigo: fish trap (柴漬)・冬
Notes: Fish trap (柴漬) in the old Tonegawa; the day sinking.

Poem: ぜすきりしと踏まれ踏まれて失せたまへり
Romaji:
zesu kirishito
fumare fumarete
usetamaeri
My translation:
Jesu Christo
stepped on and steped on
until honorably lost
Kigo: stepping on the image (踏絵)・春
Notes: The fumie (踏絵): trampled and trampled until gone — spring faith erased.

Poem: 草籠に一人静も刈られたる
Romaji:
kusa kago ni
hitori shizuka mo
kararetaru
My translation:
in the grass basket
Shizuka Alone also
is cut by mistake
Kigo: Chloranthus (一人静)・春
Notes: Chloranthus (一人静) mown into the grass basket.

Poem: 天使魚もいさかひすなりさびしくて
Romaji:
tenshigyo mo
isakai sunari
sabishikute
My translation:
angel fish also
fight
sadly
Kigo: angel fish (天使魚)・夏
Notes: Angel fish (天使魚) quarreling too — loneliness.

Poem: をとめ立てり跳躍台にライト照り
Romaji:
otome tateri
chōyakudai ni
raito trri
My translation:
the maiden stands
on the divingboard 
light glows
Kigo: divingboard (跳躍台)・夏
Notes: A girl stands on the diving platform, light shining.

Poem: 寒鯉を真白しとみれば鰭の藍
Romaji:
kangoe wo
mashiroshi to mireba
hire no ai
My translation:
cold carp
appears pure white by
indigo fins
Kigo: cold card (寒鯉)・冬
Notes: 寒鯉 (cold-season carp): pure white — then the blue of the fins.

Poem: 鮫揚ぐる人々鯖を踏みしだき
Romaji:
same aguru
hitobito saba wo
fumi shi daki
My translation:
lifting a shark
people trample
the markel
Kigo: markel (鯖)・夏
Notes: Hauling sharks; mackerel trampled underfoot.

Poem: 浄連の瀧とて冬木うちふるふ
Romaji:
jōren no
taki tote fuyuki
uchifuruu
My translation:
pure lotus falls 
shakes the 
winter trees
Kigo: winter trees (冬木)・冬
Notes: Jōren Falls: winter trees shaking in the cold.

Poem: 山焼けば鬼形の雲の天に在り
Romaji:
yama yakeba
kigyō no kumo no
ten ni ari
My translation:
when the moutnains burned
there are ogre-shaped clouds
in the heavens
Kigo: burn mountains (山焼)・春
Notes: Mountain burning: demon-shaped clouds over the sky.

Poem: 日光佛春あけぼのの香を焚けり
Romaji:
nikkōbutsu
haru akebono no
kō wo takeri
My translation:
Sun Light Buddha
in spring dawn
burning incents
Kigo: spring dawn (春曙)・春
Notes: The Nikkō Buddha; incense at spring dawn.

Poem: 選手知るや跳躍台に月のぼる
Romaji:
senshu shiru ya
chōyakudai ni
tsuki noboru
My translation:
knowing the compedater
on the diving board
the moonlight
Kigo: diving board (跳躍台)・夏
Notes: Athletes know: the moon rising over the diving platform.

Poem: 先生の手に炭火映え掌ぞあかき
Romaji:
sensei no 
te ni sumibi hae
te zo akaki
My translation:
teacher's hands
aglow in the charcoal fire
the plams red
Kigo: charcoal fire(炭火)・冬
Notes: Teacher's hands reddened in the glow of charcoal fire.

Poem: 術なきか春あけぼのを脈ほそり
Romaji:
sube naki ka
haru akebono wo
myaku hosori
My translation:
not knowing what to do
spring dawn
weak pulse
Kigo: spring dawn (春曙)・春
Notes: Helpless — spring dawn, pulse weakening.

Poem: 巴里の繪のこゝに冴え返り並ぶあはれ
Romaji:
pari no e no
koko ni sae kaeri
narabu aware
My translation:
painting of Paris
here the cold returns
lined up are moving
Kigo: cold snap (冴え返り)・春
Notes: Parisian paintings here in the cold snap — poignant.

Poem: 瑠璃（琉璃）沼に 滝落ちきたり 瑠璃となる
Romaji:
ruri numa ni
taki ochi kitari
ruri to naru
My translation:
into Turquoise  pond 
drops the waterfall
and becomes turquoise
Kigo: waterfall (滝)・夏
Notes: A waterfall falls into a lapis pool — becoming lapis.

Poem: 梅雨の羊歯金堂をめぐり真青なり
Romaji:
tsuyu no shida
kondō wo meguri
masao nari
My translation:
ferns in the rainy season
around the Golden Hall
turn deep blue
Kigo: rainy season (梅雨)・夏
Notes: Rainy-season ferns surrounding the golden hall — vivid green.

Poem: 火口壁まなかひに失せて霧吹けり
Romaji:
kakōheki
manakahi ni usete
kiri fukeri
My translation:
the creater 
before my eyes disappears
bellowing mist
Kigo: mist (霧)・秋
Notes: The crater wall lost; mist blowing.

Poem: 翡翆の淵あり瀬々は秋の風
Romaji:
kawasemi no
fuchi ari seze wa
aki no kaze
My translation:
kingfisher's
there is a pool, rapids
the autumn wind
Kigo: autumn wind (秋風)・秋
Notes: Kingfisher's pool; the shallows full of autumn wind.

Poem: 氷る畦ゆるゝと見るや鶫居り
Romaji:
kooru aze
yururu to miru ya
tsugumi ori
My translation:
frozen path
looks to be thawing
there is a thrush
Kigo: ice (氷)・冬
Notes: Frozen ridge path — a fieldfare sits, barely moving.

Poem: 窯中の炎金色に春の雨
Romaji:
yōchū no
honoo konjiki ni
haru no ame
My translation:
on the flames of
gloden color in the liln
rain of spring
Kigo: spring rain (春雨)
Notes: Kiln flame gold; spring rain falling.

Poem: 門とぢて良夜の石と我は居り
Romaji:
kado tojite
ryōya no ishi to
ware wa ori
My translation:
close the gate
on the good night; the stones
and I are
Kigo: good night (良夜)・秋
Notes: Gate closed; good night (良夜) — sitting with the stone.

Poem: 柿干して今日の独り居雲もなし
Romaji:
kaki hoshite
kyō no hitori i
kumo mo nashi
My translation:
drying persimmons
alone today in the house
no cloud either
Kigo: persimmon (柿)・秋
Notes: Persimmons hung to dry; today alone, no clouds.

Poem: 涸川や波を曳きゐる杭ひとつ
Romaji:
karekawa ya
nami wo hikiiru
kui hitotsu
My translation:
low river
pulling waves
a single ridgepole
Kigo: low river (涸川)・冬
Notes: A dried-up river — one post still trailing a wave.

Poem: 水仙に光微塵の渚あり
Romaji:
suisen ni
hikari mijin no
nagisa ari
My translation:
there is a shore
where particles of light
fall on daffodils
Kigo: daffodils (水仙)・冬
Notes: Narcissus; a shore of tiny sparkling light.

Poem: 暗き灯やされど炭火に立つ焔
Romaji:
kuraki hi ya
saredo sumibi ni
tatsu honoo
My translation:
a dark light—
and yet in the coalfire
a flame stands
Kigo: coalfire (炭)・冬
Notes: Dim lamp; yet charcoal flame rises.

Poem: 落葉踏む今日の明るさ明日もあれ
Romaji:
ochiba fumu
kyō no akarosa
asu mo are
My translation:
stepping on fallen leaves
may tomorrow be
as bright as today
Kigo: fallen leaves (落葉)・冬
Notes: Treading fallen leaves; today's brightness — may tomorrow have it too.

Poem: 麦生より鶫があふぐ梅咲けり
Romaji:
mugiu yori
tsugumi ga afugu
ume sakeri
My translation:
from the sprouting wheat
the thrush looks up
blooming plum
Kigo: plum (梅)・春
Notes: From the wheat field, a fieldfare looks up at the plum.

Poem: 臈たけて紅の菓子あり弥生尽
Romaji:
rō takete
beni no kashi ari
yayoijin
My translation:
elegantly
there is a crimson sweet
end of the verdant month
Kigo: end of the verdant month (弥生尽)・春
Notes: 弥生尽 (end of the Third Month): elegant red confections.

Poem: 雨追ひて春日さしわたる殿の簷
Romaji:
ame oite
haru hisashi wataru
tono no noki
My translation:
chasing the rain
spring light shines across
eaves of the lord
Kigo: spring light (春日)・春
Notes: Rain chased away; spring light crossing the palace eave.

Poem: うらゝにて雲雀はしれる墳の前
Romaji:
urara nite
hibari hashireru
tsuka no mae
My translation:
on a beautiful day
skylark runs
in front of the mound
Kigo: skylark (雲雀)・春
Notes: Brightly; skylarks racing before an old burial mound.

Poem: 木瓜の朱は匂ひ石棺の朱は失せぬ
Romaji:
boke no shu wa
nioi sekikan no
shu wa aseru
My translation:
the vermillion of quince
is fragrant the vermillion of the
stone coffin has faded
Kigo: 木瓜 (quince)・春
Notes: 木瓜 (quince) fragrance; the stone coffin's red is gone.

Poem: 時鳥野に甘藍の渦みだれ
Romaji:
hototogisu
no ni kanran no
uzu midare
My translation:
cuckoo
in the field the cabbage
vortex disorder
Kigo: 時鳥 (cuckoo)・夏
Notes: Cuckoo over cabbage-patch swirling.

Poem: 芥子咲くやけふの心の夕映に
Romaji:
keshi saku ya 
kyō no kokoro no 
yūbae ni
My translation:
poppies bloom—
in the evening glow
of my feelings today
Kigo: 芥子 (poppies)・夏
Notes: Poppies bloom; the heart this evening gilded.

Poem: 朝は憂し机上臘燭と柿一顆
Romaji:
asa wa ushi 
kijō rōsaku to
kaki ikka
My translation:
gloomy morning
on my desk a candle
and one persimmon
Kigo: 柿 【かき】 kaki, persimmon(s) [fruit of Diospyros kaki or related species] (late autumn).
Notes: Morning is dark; candle and one persimmon on the desk.

Poem: 冬菊のまとふはおのがひかりのみ
Romaji:
fuyugiku no
motou wa ono ga
hikari nomi
My translation:
winter chrysanthemum
wear only their 
own light
Kigo: 冬菊(winter chrysanthemum)・冬
Notes: 冬菊 (winter chrysanthemum): wrapped only in its own light.

Poem: わが齢夜番勤めよと触れきたる
Romaji:
waga yowai
yoban tsutome yo
furekitaru
My translation:
even at my age
they come to tell me 
its my turn for nightwatch
Kigo: 夜番 (nightwatch)・冬
Notes: My age: told to do night-watch duty.

Poem: 峽の日はたかしスケートの線みだれ
Romaji:
kai no hi wa
takashi sukeeto no
sen midare
My translation:
the sun over the gorge
is high; the lines of the skates
are wild
Kigo: スケート (skates)・冬
Notes: Gorge sun high; skate-lines crossing on the ice.

Poem: 雹のあと蘂眞青に梅こぼれ
Romaji:
hyō no ato
shibe massao ni
ume kobore
My translation:
after the hail
the deep blue pistil
plum spils
Kigo: 梅 【うめ】 ume, （sometimes むめ mume）, plum (blossoms) [technically, the "Japanese apricot", Prunus mume; but this has almost always been translated "plum" for literary purposes] (early spring).
Notes: After hail; stamens vivid blue; plum scattered.

Poem: 水掻の朱がひた濡れて春の鴨
Romaji:
mizugaki no
shu ga hita nurete
haru no kamo
My translation:
the vermillion of the webed foot
just wet
duck of spring
Kigo: 春の鴨 (duck of spring)・春
Notes: Spring duck's vermilion webbing soaking wet.

Poem: 浮雲の影あまた過ぎ木瓜ひらく
Romaji:
ukigumo no
kage amata sugi
boke hiraku
My translation:
floating clouds
many shadows pass
quince flowers open
Kigo: 木瓜 (quince)・春
Notes: Many cloud-shadows passing; quince opens.

Poem: べたべたに田も菜の花も照りみだる
Romaji:
betabeta ni
ta mo na no hana mo
teri midaru
My translation:
stickely
in the pattaies & on the rape flowers
shining scattered
Kigo: 菜の花 【なのはな】 na-no-hana, rape flowers / mustard flowers [technically, Brassica rapa, the plant from which canola oil derives; one may prefer to translate with the closely related "mustard" in English; the image is of a field covered with the yellow flowers] (late spring).
Notes: Paddies and rape flowers shining everywhere.

Poem: きりぎりす見るは巌のみ又波のみ
Romaji:
kirigirisu
miru wa iwa nomi
mata nami nomi
My translation:
cricket
all that is seen is rocks
and waves
Kigo: きりぎりす(cricket)・夏
Notes: Cricket: sees only rock, sees only wave.

Poem: 青き鴨波翔けめぐり初日いづ
Romaji:
aoki kamo
nami kagemeguri
hatsuhi izu
My translation:
emerald duck
waves winging up
sun rise first dawn
Kigo: 初日(first dawn)・新年
Notes: Green ducks skimming waves; the New Year's first sunrise.

Poem: 廃運河何に波立つ雪の中
Romaji:
haiunga
nan ni nami tatsu
yuki no naka
My translation:
abandonded canal 
what makes the waves raise?
In the snow
Kigo: 雪(snow)・冬
Notes: Abandoned canal; snow — why do waves form?

Poem: 鷽の来てあけぼのの庭に胸赤し
Romaji:
uso no kite
akebono no niwa ni
mune akashi
My translation:
bullfinch comes
to dawn garden
its chest red
Kigo: 鷽(bullfinch)・春
Notes: A bullfinch (鷺) comes; red breast in the dawn garden.

Poem: 谿二つ雷火立ちては相照す
Romaji:
tani futatsu
raika tachite wa
aiterasu
My translation:
two valleys
lighting flashes
shine back & forth
Kigo: 雷(lighting)・夏
Notes: Two ravines; lightning fires answering each other.

Poem: 夢さめておどろく闇 や 秋 の 暮
Romaji:
yume samete
odoroku yami ya
aki no kure
My translation:
waking from a dream
shocking darkness—
end of autumn
Kigo: 秋 の 暮(end of autumn)・ 秋
Notes: Waking startled from a dream — dark; autumn dusk.

Poem: 田掻牛観世音寺の前を曳く
Romaji:
tagaki ushi
kanzeon-ji no
mae wo hiku
My translation:
field turning ox
pulling in front of
Kanzeon Temple
Kigo: 田掻牛(field turning ox)・春
Notes: Field-plowing ox led before Kanzeonji temple.

Poem: 薔薇喰ふ虫聖母見たまふ高きより
Romaji:
bara kuu mushi
seibo mitamau
takaki yori
My translation:
rose eating bugs
view the holy mother
from on high
Kigo: 薔薇 rose)・夏
Notes: A rose-eating insect; the Madonna looks down.

Poem: 素朴なる卓に秋風の聖書あり
Romaji:
sobokunaru
taku ni aki kaze no
seisyo ari
My translation:
on the rustic 
table there is the Bible
of the autumn wind
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn).
Notes: On the plain table — an autumn-wind Bible.

Poem: 龍の角落ちて土筆の生ひにける
Romaji:
ryū no tsuno
ochite tsukushi no
oinikeru
My translation:
the dragon horns
fall to earth and 
field horsetail sprout
Kigo: 土筆 【つくし】 tsukushi, horsetail shoot(s) [the reproductive shoots of Equisetum arvense] (mid spring).
Notes: Dragon horns (土筆 horsetail shoots) sprouting where the horns fell.

Poem: 春深し紫髯（しぜん）の胡人あそぶ壺
Romaji:
haru fukashi
shizen nokojin
asobu tsubo
My translation:
spring deepens
purple breaded foreigner
frolk on the jar
Kigo: 春深し(spring deepens)・春
Notes: 春深し (spring deepens): a purple-bearded foreigner at play with a jar.

Poem: 落葉聴く豊頬陶土観世音
Romaji:
ochiba kiku
hōkyō tōdo
kanzeon
My translation:
hearing leaves fall
ample clay cheecks
of Kanon
Kigo: 落葉 ( leaves fall)・冬
Notes: Listening to fallen leaves; a round-cheeked earthen Kannon.

Poem: 大雪の都電とどまる旧居前
Romaji:
ōyuki no
toden todomaru
kyūkyo mae
My translation:
great snow fall
the street car stops
in frontof my old house
Kigo: 雪 (snow)・冬
Notes: Heavy snow; the city tram stopped before the old house.

Poem: 瀧落ちて群青世界とどろけり
Romaji:
taki ochite
gunjyō sekai
todorokeri
My translation:
cataract falls
ultramarine world
resounds
Kigo: 瀧 (cataract)・夏
Notes: A waterfall plunges — the ultramarine world thunders.

Poem: 蛙つぶやく輪塔大空放哉居士
Romaji:
kawazu tsubuyaku
rintō daiku
hōsai koshi
My translation:
the frogs mutter
pagoda "Big Sky"
blessed Hōsai
Kigo: 蛙 【かわず】 kawazu, （かはづ）, frog(s) [note that this is a literary word] (all spring).
Notes: A frog mutters; the pagoda — Hōsai's great sky.

Poem: 蕎麦咲けり雲水峡をいできたる
Romaji:
soba sakeri
unsui kai wo
idekitaru
My translation:
buckwheat flowers bloom
an itinerant monk from the valley
coming on
Kigo: 蕎麦の花 (buckwheat flowers)・秋
Notes: Buckwheat blooming; a monk-wanderer emerges from the gorge.

Poem: 菓子買ひに妻をいざなふ地虫の夜
Romaji:
kashii kai ni
tsuma wo izanau
jimushi no yo
My translation:
inviting the wife
to buy sweets
night of the grubs
Kigo: 地虫 (grubs)・春
Notes: Grubs at night; coaxing wife to buy sweets.

Poem: 曇り来て諸佛面伏す雨蛙
Romaji:
kumori kite
shobutsu omofusu
ama-gaeru
My translation:
cloudness comes and 
the various buddhas looking down 
rain frogs
Kigo: 雨蛙 (rain frogs)・春
Notes: Cloud coming; all the Buddhas bow their heads — rain frogs.

Poem: 鳥寄せに寄りきてかなし巣立鳥
Romaji:
toriyose ni
yorikite kanashi
sudachidori
My translation:
fledgling 
how sad for them to be lured
by a bird lure
Kigo: 巣立鳥 【すだちどり】 sudachidori, fledgeling (late spring).
Notes: Called to the bird-summons, a fledgling comes — sadly.

Poem: 啄木鳥に泉の水輪絶ゆるなし
Romaji:
kitsutsuki ni
izumi no minowa 
tayuru nashi
My translation:
the woodpeaker
the ripples in the sprig
do not stop
Kigo: 啄木鳥 (woodpeaker)・秋
Notes: Woodpecker; the spring's water-rings never stop.

Poem: 残る雪月黄なる夜を失せにけり
Romaji:
nokoru yuki
tuski kinaru wo
usenikeri
My translation:
lingering snow
night of yellow moon
dissappears
Kigo: 残雪 【ざんせつ】 zansetsu, remaining snow (mid spring).
