Notes: Lingering snow; the yellow moon night vanishes.

Poem: 何菩薩春愁華岳ゑがきける
Romaji:
nani bosatsu
shunshū kagaku
wegakikeru
My translation:
what bosatsu?
Shuka depects 
gloom in spring
Kigo: 春愁 【しゅんしゅう】 shunshū, （しゅんしう）, spring melancholy (mid spring).
Notes: What bodhisattva painted spring gloom on Huashan?

Poem: 稲架照らす提灯の紋ぞ揚羽蝶
Romaji:
haza terasu
chōchin no mon zo
agehachō
My translation:
lighting the rice drying
the lantern's design
raised wing butterfly
Kigo: 稲架 (lighting)・秋
Notes: Rice-rack lantern crest: a swallowtail butterfly.

Poem: 色鳥の来て佛敵の名の悲し
Romaji:
irodori no
kite butsu teki no
na no kanashi
My translation:
the colored birds
come, enemy of the Buddha
name is sad
Kigo: 色鳥 【いろどり】 irodori, colorful (small) birds [in autumn migration] (all autumn).
Notes: Colored birds come; the name of the Buddha-enemy is sad.

Poem: 雨蛙石となつたる墓は黙す
Romaji:
amagaeru
ishi to nattaru
haka wa modasu
My translation:
rain frogs
the grave that has turned to stone
fall silent
Kigo: 雨蛙 (rain frogs)・春
Notes: A rain frog turned to stone; the grave is silent.

Poem: 黒百合や星帰りたる高き空.
Romaji:
kuroyuri ya
hoshi kaeritaru
takaki sora
My translation:
black lily—
the stars return
to the high heavens
Kigo: 黒百合 (black lily)・夏
Notes: Black lily; stars have returned to the high sky.

Poem: 木の実降り鵯鳴き天平観世音
Romaji:
ko no mi furi
hyo naki tenpyō
kanzeon
My translation:
seeds of trees falling
a bulbul cries, Tenpyō
Kanon statue
Kigo: 木の実 【このみ】 konomi, nut/fruit/berry [or plurals; of a tree or shrub; note that the common vernacular pronunciation きのみ ki no mi, is not used for this term in haikai] (all autumn).
Notes: Tree nuts falling; bulbul calling; Nara-period Kannon.

Poem: おもひきや春月のぼる藪のひま
Romaji:
omoiki ya
shungetsu noboru
yabu no hima
My translation:
how unexpected!
spring moon rises in between
cracks in the groove
Kigo: spring moon (春月)・春
Notes: I didn't expect — the spring moon rising in the bamboo grove.

Poem: 行春や娘首の髪の艶
Romaji:
yuku haru ya
musume-gashira no
kami no en
My translation:
departing spring—
a girl's head
hair elegance
Kigo: 行春 (departing spring)・春
Notes: 行春 (departing spring): gloss of a daughter's nape hair.

Poem: 硝煙や兜捨てたる鎧武者
Romaji:
shōen ya
kabuto sutetaru
yoroimusha
My translation:
powder smoke—
tossing away their helmets
armored warriors
Kigo: 裸 【はだか】 hadaka, naked / nude (late summer).
Notes: Gunsmoke; a warrior has cast off his helmet.

Poem: 散紅葉鳥獣絵巻かくれなし
Romaji:
chiri momiji
chōjū emaki
kakure nashi
My translation:
scattering autumn leaves on
frolicing birds & anmials scrolls
nothing is hidden
Kigo: 散紅葉 (scattering autumn leaves)・冬
Notes: Scattering autumn leaves; the animal scrolls unhidden.

Poem: 蕪村忌や画中酔歩の李太白
Romaji:
busonki ya
gachū suiho no
ritaihaku
My translation:
Buson memorial—
stumbleing drunk through the picture
Ritahaku
Kigo: 蕪村忌 (Buson memorial)・冬
Notes: Buson memorial: Li Bai drunk-walking in a painted world.

Poem: 遊蝶花 春は素朴に 始まれり
Romaji:
yūchōka
haru wa soboku ni 
hajimareri
My translation:
playing butterfly flowers
very plain is the start
of spring
Kigo: 遊蝶花 (playing butterfly flowers)・春
Notes: 遊蝶花 (butterfly flower/pansies): spring begins simply.

Poem: 月いでて薔薇のたそがれなほつづく
Romaji:
tsuki idete
bara no tasogare
nao tsuduku
My translation:
moon riseing 
rose evening 
continues yet still
Kigo: 薔薇 (rose)・夏
Notes: The moon rises; twilight of roses still continues.

Poem: 葛咲くや濁流わたる熊野犬
Romaji:
kuzu saku ya
dakuryū wataru
kumanoken
My translation:
kudzu flowers bloom—
crossing the muddy stream
a kumano breed
Kigo: 葛の花　(kudzu flowers)・秋
Notes: Kudzu flowers; a Kumano dog crossing the muddy current.

Poem: 琴弾けば緑陰深くむせぶ声
Romaji:
koto hikeba
ryokuin fukaku
musebu koe
My translation:
plucking the harp
the emerald shade deep
clouded voice
Kigo: 緑陰 【りょくいん】 ryokuin, green shade (all summer).
Notes: Playing the koto; from the green shade, a choking voice.

Poem: 鯊釣や不二暮れそめて手を洗ふ
Romaji:
haze tsuri ya
fuji kure somete
te wo arau
My translation:
goby fishing—
sunset stains Fuji
washing their hands
Kigo: goby (鯊)・秋
Notes: Fishing for goby; Fuji darkening, washing hands.

Poem: 琴責めの琴よこたへぬ初芝居
Romaji:
koto-zeme no
koto yokotaenu
hatsu shibai
My translation:
the lute of the 
tormenting lute laid out
opening performance
Kigo: 初芝居 (opening performance)・新年
Notes: 初芝居 (New Year kabuki): the koto laid across the stage.

Poem: 月幾夜照らせし鴟尾に今日の月
Romaji:
tsukiyo
teraseshi shibi ni
kyō no tuski
My translation:
the moon which has shone
on many generations t the ridge end tile
today's moon
Kigo: 今日の月 (today's moon)・秋
Notes: How many nights has the moon lit this ridge-tile — today's moon.

Poem: 古雛は着ぶれたまふ佳かりけり
Romaji:
furu hina wa
kibure tamau
yokarikeri
My translation:
the old dolls
bundled in warm robes
it is good
Kigo: 雛 【ひな】 hina, （ひいな）, (ceremonial) doll(s) [specifically, dolls representing the Heian court, typically displayed in homes with female children during the "Doll Festival", 3 March (formerly observed on the third day of third lunar month, late spring)] (mid spring).
Notes: An old doll (古雛) worn with age — still beautiful.

Poem: 寄生木やしづかに移る火事の雲
Romaji:
yadorigi ya
shizukani utusru
kaji no kumo
My translation:
mistletoe—
quietly relecting 
the cloud of fire
Kigo: fire (火事)・冬
Notes: Mistletoe (寄生木): quietly, the fire-cloud moves.

Poem: 蜻蛉生れ緑眼煌とすきけり
Romaji:
tanbo umare
ryokugankō to
sugiyukeri
My translation:
dragonfly is born
glint of its green eyes and
off it goes
Kigo: 蜻蛉生る (dragonfly is born)・夏
Notes: A dragonfly hatches; green eyes flashing.

Poem: 鰻掻き去りたるあとのいなびかり
Romaji:
unagi kaki
saritaru ato no
inabikari
My translation:
eel hook
after having left
lighting
Kigo: いなびかり (lighting)・秋
Notes: An eel slips away; lightning in its wake.

Poem: 馬追や月をよこぎる萩一枝
Romaji:
uma oi ya 
tsuki wo yokogiru
hagi isshi
My translation:
katydid—
crosscuting the moon
single branch of bushclover
Kigo: 馬追 (katydid)・秋
Notes: Katydid (馬追); a branch of bush-clover crossing the moon.

Poem: 追羽根に舁きゆく鮫の潮垂りぬ
Romaji:
oibane ni
kaki yuku same no 
shio tarinu
My translation:
shuttlecocks 
sholdering sharks
the tide drops
Kigo: shuttlecocks (追羽根)・新年
Notes: New Year battledore game (追羽根); a shark dripping seawater.

Poem: 梨咲くと葛飾の野はとの曇り
Romaji:
nashi saku
ka no no wa
tono kumori
My translation:
pear tree blooms
and Katsushika feild
clouds up
Kigo: pear blooms (梨咲く)・春
Notes: Pear blossoms; Katsushika fields hazy as pigeons.

Poem: 影ならぶむかしながらの月の下
Romaji:
kage narabu
mukashi nagara no
tuki no shita
My translation:
the shadows lined up
just like in the past
under the moon
Kigo: 月 (moon)・秋
Notes: Shadows side by side — the same old moon above.

Poem: 消ゆる灯の命を惜しみ牡蛎を食ふ
Romaji:
kiyuru hi no
inochi wo oshimi
kaki wo kuu
My translation:
regreting the fading
light of life
eating oysters
Kigo: 牡蛎 【かき】 kaki, oyster(s) (all winter).
Notes: Mourning the dying lamp; eating oysters.

Poem: 年越蕎麦待てばしきりに救急車
Romaji:
toshikoshi soba
materi shikirini
kyūkyūsha
My translation:
waiting for new year's soba
incessantly come
the ambulances
Kigo: 年越蕎麦 (new year's soba)・冬
Notes: Waiting for year-crossing soba; ambulances keep coming.

Poem: 仰臥せり鰹の角煮舌に載せ
Romaji:
gyōgaseri
katsuo no kakuni
shita ni nose
My translation:
laying on my back
carefully placing
sweet-stewed banito
Kigo: 甘露煮 (sweet-stewed banito)・冬
Notes: Lying down; boiled bonito placed on the tongue.

Poem: 琴冴えてのこる虫の音冴えにけり
Romaji:
koto saete
nokoru mushi no ne
saenikeri
My translation:
the harp is clear
the sound of lingering insects
is clear
Kigo: 虫 【むし】 mushi, insect(s) [usually plural, for their singing] (all autumn).
Notes: Koto clear; remaining insect voices also clear.

Poem: ひかり飛ぶものあまたゐて末枯るる
Romaji:
hikari tobu
mono amataite
uragaruru
My translation:
so many of them
glowing in flight
tip withering
Kigo: tip withering (末枯)・秋
Notes: Light things flying everywhere; branch-tips withering.

Poem: 垣の薔薇白きがちりて径しろし
Romaji:
kaki no bara
shiroki ga chirite
michi shiroshi
My translation:
rose covered fence
the whitness scatters
and the road is white
Kigo: rose (薔薇)・夏
Notes: White roses on the fence scatter; the path turns white.

Poem: 競べ馬逸りつ踏めり苜蓿
Romaji:
kurabe uma
hayaritsu fumeri
umagoyashi
My translation:
the race horse 
excited, it steps on
alfalfa
Kigo: alfalfa (苜蓿)・春
Notes: Race horse rearing and stamping on alfalfa.

Poem: むさしのの空真青なる落葉かな
Romaji:
musashino no
sora masaonaru
ochiba kana
My translation:
the sky over
Musashi Plain is pure blue
fallen leaves
Kigo: fallen leaves (落葉)・冬
Notes: Musashino sky deep blue; fallen leaves on the ground.

Poem: 夏めくや素足の裏に庭の土
Romaji:
natsu meku ya
suashi no ura ni
niwa no tsuchi
My translation:
summery-
on the bottom of bear feet
garden soil
Kigo:
夏めくnatsu meku 
Summery or summer-like

Poem: 花冷の闇にあらはれ篝守
Romaji:
hana-bie no 
yami ni araware 
kagari mori
My translation:
from flower chill
darkness appeared
the lamp-lighter
Kigo:
Flower chill
花冷 hana-bie

Poem: 花舗の日覆みどりに夏きたる
Romaji:
hana mise no
hioi midori ni
natsu kitaru
My translation:
to the flower shop
with green sunshade
summer has come
Kigo: 立夏  Rikka  [Summer / Season]

Poem: はしための葱の香しみし濡手かな
Romaji:
hashi tame no
negi no ka shimishi
nure te kana
My translation:
maid servant,
with green onion’s scent soaked,
her wet hands
Kigo: 葱 【ねぎ】 negi, stone leek(s) [Allium fistulosum, also known as "Welch onions"] (all winter).
Notes: 濡手 (nurete) = wet hands. A servant's hands fragrant and wet from chopping leeks.

Poem: 院々の肉煮ゆる香や夕紅葉
Romaji:
in’in no 
niku niyuru ka ya 
yū momiji
My translation:
From the monks’ cells
a smell of cooking meat:
autumn leaves at nightfall.
Kigo: 夕紅葉 【ゆうもみじ】 yū-momiji, autumn leaves at dusk (all autumn).
Notes: 肉煮ゆる香 (niku ni yuru ka) = the scent of meat cooking. Temple kitchens with cooking smells and evening autumn leaves.

Poem: 金剛の露ひとつぶや石の上
Romaji:
kongō no 
tsuyu hitotsubu ya 
ishi no ue
My translation:
Like a diamond 
a drop of dew, all alone 
on a stone.
Kigo: 露 【つゆ】 tsuyu, dew (mid autumn).
Notes: 金剛の露 (kongō no tsuyu) = diamond-like dew. A single diamond-like dewdrop on a stone—the entire universe in miniature.

Poem: 虎杖を啣へて沙弥や墓掃除
Romaji:
itadori wo 
kuwaete shami ya 
haka sōji
My translation:
A stem of knotweed 
in his mouth, a young acolyte 
sweeps the graveyard.
Kigo: 墓掃除 【はかそうじ】 haka-sōji, grave-cleaning (all autumn).
Notes: 虎杖 (itadori) = Japanese knotweed. A novice monk carrying knotweed while cleaning graves.

Poem: 水晶の念珠に映る若葉かな
Romaji:
suishō no 
nenju ni utsuru 
wakaba kana
My translation:
In the crystal beads 
of my rosary young leaves 
are mirrored.
Kigo: 若葉 【わかば】 wakaba, young leaves/ new leaves / fresh verdure (early summer).
Notes: 水晶の念珠 (suishō no juzu) = crystal rosary beads. Young leaves reflected in crystal rosary beads.

Poem: 蝶の空七堂伽藍さかしまに
Romaji:
chō no sora 
shichidō-garan 
sakashima ni
My translation:
To the butterfly in the sky 
all buildings on the temple ground 
are upside down.
Kigo: 蝶 【ちょう】 chō, （てふ）, butterfly [the spring butterfly image is typically a cabbage white, white members of the family Pieridae; see also "summer butterfly", etc.] (all spring).
Notes: Butterflies flying above the temple compound; the seven halls reflected upside down in their wings.

Poem: 大根馬菩薩面して眼になみだ
Romaji:
daikon uma 
bosatsu-zura shite 
me ni namida
My translation:
The horse loaded with turnips 
has a Bodhisattva’s face, 
with tears in his eyes.
Kigo: 大根 【だいこん】 daikon, daikon [the Japanese white radish, Raphanus sativas, much used in cooking] (all winter).
Notes: 大根馬 (daikon uma) = daikon-horse. A horse made of daikon for the altar; tears in its bodhisattva-like eyes.

Poem: 春の夜や寝れば恋しき観世音
Romaji:
haru no yo ya 
nereba koishiki 
kanzeon
My translation:
Nightfall on a spring day: 
in bed, I think longingly 
of the gentle Bodhisattva.
Kigo: 春の夜 【はるのよ】 haru no yo, spring night (all spring).
Notes: 観世音 (Kanzeon) = Kannon. On a spring night, even in sleep one yearns for Kannon.

Poem: 僧酔うて友の頭撫づる月の縁
Romaji:
sō yōte 
tomo no zu nazuru 
tsuki no en
My translation:
The monk, a little 
drunk, pats a friend on the head— 
terrace in the moonlight.
Kigo: 月 【つき】 tsuki, moon (mid autumn).
Notes: A monk drunk and stroking a friend's head in moonlight on the veranda.

Poem: 月の雪あをあを闇を染めのけり
Romaji:
tsuki no yuki 
aoao yami wo 
somenokeri
My translation:
Snow under the moon 
is blue, dyeing with its blue 
the darkness of night.
Kigo: 月の雪 【つきのゆき】 tsuki no yuki, moonlit snow (winter).
Notes: Moonlit snow staining the darkness a vivid blue.

Poem: 氷る夜の文殊に燭をたてまつる
Romaji:
kōru yo no 
monju ni shoku wo 
tatematsuru
My translation:
On a freezing night 
to the Bodhisattva of Wisdom 
I offer a candle.
Kigo: 氷る夜 【こおるよ】 kōru yo, freezing night (all winter).
Notes: 文殊 (Monju) = Mañjuśrī. Offering a candle to Mañjuśrī on a freezing night.

Poem: まひまひや雨後の円光とりもどし
Romaji:
maimai ya 
ugo no enkō 
torimodoshi
My translation:
Now that the shower 
has passed, the water spider 
regains its halo.
Kigo: 雨後 【うご】 ugo, after the rain (summer).
Notes: まひまひ (mahimai) = water snail. After the rain, the snail's concentric ripples restore the halo.

Poem: まひまひの水輪に鐘の響かな
Romaji:
maimai no 
minawa ni kane no 
hibiki kana
My translation:
The water spider 
draws rings on the water, wherein 
echoes a temple bell.
Kigo: 蝸牛 【かたつむり】 katatsumuri, snail / land snail (all summer).
Notes: Snail making water rings; the bell's sound resonates within them.

Poem: 光輪を負ひて貧しき田螺かな
Romaji:
kōrin wo 
oite mazushiki 
tanishi kana
My translation:
Carrying a halo 
on its back, how impoverished 
a mud snail!
Kigo: 田螺 【たにし】 tanishi, mud-snail(s)/paddy-snail(s) (all spring).
Notes: 光輪 (kōrin) = halo. The pond snail bearing a halo—every humble creature has sacred light.

Poem: 葱の花ふと金色の仏かな
Romaji:
negi no hana 
futo konjiki no 
hotoke kana
My translation:
Green onions flowering— 
for a moment golden 
Buddha was there.
Kigo: 葱の花 【ねぎのはな】 negi no hana, onion flower (mid spring).
Notes: The sudden association of an onion flower with a golden Buddha.

Poem: 月光に深雪の創のかくれなし
Romaji:
gekkō ni 
miyuki no kizu no 
kakure nashi
My translation:
In the moonlight 
how clearly the deep snow 
shows its scars!
Kigo: 深雪 【みゆき】 miyuki, deep snow (all winter).
Notes: In moonlight, even the wound in the deep snow is unhidden.

Poem: 眼前に蜘の巣かかり夕山河
Romaji:
ganzen ni 
kumo no su kakari 
yū sanga
My translation:
A spider web 
hanging before my eyes, evening 
mountains and rivers.
Kigo: 蜘の巣 【くものす】 kumo no su, spider web (all autumn).
Notes: A spider web appears before the eyes in the evening landscape.

Poem: 緑陰に黒猫の目のかつと金
Romaji:
ryokuin ni 
kuroneko no me no 
katto kin
My translation:
In the shade of green 
leaves the eyes of a black cat 
glaring in gold.
Kigo: 緑陰 【りょくいん】 ryokuin, green shade (all summer).
Notes: In the green shade, a black cat's eyes flash golden.

Poem: 火の玉の如くに咳きて隠れ栖む
Romaji:
hi no tama no 
gotoku ni sekite 
kakure sumu
My translation:
Like a fireball, I
fall into a fit of coughing 
in this hideout of mine.
Kigo: 咳 【せき】 seki, cough (all winter).
Notes: 火の玉の如くに咳きて (hi no tama no gotoku ni sekite) = coughing like a fireball. Coughing like a ball of fire, then hiding away.

Poem: 我が魂のごとく朴咲き病よし
Romaji:
waga tama no 
gotoku hō saki 
yamai yoshi
My translation:
As if it were my soul 
a magnolia blooms out— 
ailing, I feel better.
Kigo: 朴の花 【ほおのはな】 hō no hana, magnolia flower (early summer).
Notes: The magnolia blooms like the poet's soul; the illness lifts.

Poem: 石枕してわれ蟬か泣き時雨
Romaji:
ishi makura 
shite ware semi ka 
naki shigure
My translation:
My head on a pillow 
of stone, am I a cicada? 
The weeping of rain...
Kigo: 蝉 【せみ】 semi, cicada (late summer/early autumn).
Notes: Lying with a stone pillow, weeping like a cicada—or is the cicada weeping with him?

Poem: 袖かろし夏めく水仕はげまされ
Romaji:
sode karoshi
natsu meku minashi
hagemasare
My translation:
feeling buoyed by 
airy sleeves doing
summery kitchen chores
Kigo:
夏めくnatsu meku 
Summery or summer-like

Poem: 咳の子のなぞなぞあそびきりもなや
Romaji:
seki no ko no
nazonazo asobi
kiri mo naya
My translation:
there’s no end
playing riddles with 
coughing child
Kigo: cough

Poem: 右の眼に大河左の眼に騎兵
Romaji:
migi no me ni
taiga hidari no
me ni kihei
My translation:
In the right eye,
an immense river: in the left
eye, a horseman.
Kigo: 大河 【たいが】 taiga, great river (summer).
Notes: Cavalry in one eye, a great river in the other—war landscape fractured.

Poem: 算術の少年しのびなけり夏
Romaji:
sanjutsu no 
shōnen shinoni
nakeri natsu
My translation:
Over arithmetic 
a youngster voicelessly
weeps—summer.
Kigo: 夏 【なつ】 natsu, summer.
Notes: 算術の少年 (sanjutsu no shōnen) = the arithmetic boy. A boy weeping secretly over arithmetic in the summer—the loneliness of being clever.

Poem: 機関銃眉間に赤き花が咲く
Romaji:
kikanjū
miken ni akaki 
hana ga saku
My translation:
A machine gun—
in the middle of the forehead
red blossoms bloom.
Kigo: 花 【はな】 hana, (cherry) blossoms [in haiku and haikai the simple word hana 花 refers to cherry blossoms, as do all kigo listed here; but note that in Manyōshū and some other early poetry hana was understood as referring to ume 梅【うめ】plum blossoms, an early spring topic] (late spring).
Notes: 機関銃花ヨリ赤ク闇ニ咲ク

Poem: 雄鶏や落葉の下に何もなき
Romaji:
ondori ya
ochiba no shita ni
nani mo naki
My translation:
A rooster: 
beneath the fallen leaves
there is not a thing:
Kigo: 落葉 【おちば】 ochiba, fallen leaves (all autumn).
Notes: A rooster standing over fallen leaves covering nothing—existential emptiness.

Poem: 倒れたる案山子の顔の上に天
Romaji:
taore taru
kakashi no kao no
ue ni ten
My translation:
Lying collapsed.
a scarecrow, and high above
its face, the heavens.
Kigo: 案山子 【かかし】 kakashi, scarecrow (all autumn).
Notes: A fallen scarecrow, sky above its face—the sky as final witness.

Poem: 限りなく降る雪何をもたらすや
Romaji:
kagirinaku
furu yuki nani wo
motarasu ya
My translation:
The endlessly 
falling snow—I wonder what 
it is bringing to me.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: 限りなく降る雪 (kagiri naku furu yuki) = endlessly falling snow. The snow falls without limit—what will it bring?

Poem: クリスマス馬小屋ありて馬が住む
Romaji:
kurisumasu
uma-goya arite
uma ga sumu
My translation:
Christmas Day—
there stands a stable, and
a horse is in it.
Kigo: クリスマス kurisumasu, Christmas (all winter).
Notes: Christmas: a stable with a real horse—deflating the sacred with the mundane.

Poem: 鯨食って始まる孤児と医者の野球
Romaji:
kujira kutte
hajimaru koji to
ishi no yakyū
My translation:
After eating whalemeat
orphans and a doctor start
a baseball game.
Kigo: 鯨 【くじら】 kujira, whale (all winter).
Notes: After eating whale, an orphan and a doctor play baseball—absurdist post-war scene.

Poem: おつまでも笑ふ枯野の遠くにて
Romaji:
itsumademo
warau kareno no
tōku nite
My translation:
The laughter lasts
forever in the distance
on the withered moor.
Kigo: 枯野 【かれの】 kareno, withered field (all winter).
Notes: Something laughing endlessly far away in the withered field—eerie, unresolved.

Poem: 病者起ち冬が汚せる硝子拭く
Romaji:
byōsha tachi
fuyu ga yogoseru
garasu fuku
My translation:
A patient rises
and wipes the window pane
soiled by winter.
Kigo: 冬 【ふゆ】 fuyu, winter.
Notes: A sick person gets up to wipe winter grime from the glass—the body asserting itself.

Poem: 五月の地面犬はいよいよ犬臭く
Romaji:
gogatsu no
jimen inu wa iyoiyo
inu kusaku
My translation:
On the ground of May
the dog ever increasingly
smells of dog.
Kigo: 五月 【ごがつ】 gogatsu, May (early summer).
Notes: In May, the dog becomes emphatically itself—animality in the season.

Poem: 対岸の人と寒風もてつながる
Romaji:
taigan no
hito to kanpū mote
tsunagaru
My translation:
On the other shore,
a person; the cold wind
connects me to him.
Kigo: 寒風 【かんぷう】 kanpū, cold wind (all winter).
Notes: The people on opposite banks connected only by cold wind—bitter intimacy of winter.

Poem: 石工若し散る石片が秋の花
Romaji:
ishiku wakashi
chiru sekihen ga
aki no hana
My translation:
The stonemason is young,
scattering fragments of stone
like blooms of autumn.
Kigo: 秋の花 【あきのはな】 aki no hana, autumn flower (all autumn).
Notes: 石工若し (sekikō wakashi) = the stonemason is young. Stone chips flying from the young stonemason—each chip an autumn flower.

Poem: 鴉飛び立てり羽ばたく枯野男
Romaji:
karasu tobi
tateri habataku
kareno otoko
My translation:
The raven has flown
away: flapping his wings
on the moor, a man.
Kigo: 枯野 【かれの】 kareno, withered field (all winter).
Notes: A crow flies; in the withered field, a man beats his wings—the human become bird-like.

Poem: 病む顔の前の硝子に雪張りつく
Romaji:
yamu kao no
mae no garasu ni
yuki haritsuku
My translation:
On the window pane
in front of an ailing face
snowflakes have stuck.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: Snow plastered on the glass before the sick face—enclosure and cold.

Poem: 向日葵播く雲の上なる日を探す
Romaji:
himawari maki
kumo no ue naru
hi wo sagasu
My translation:
I sow sunflower seeds
and look up above the clouds
to locate the sun.
Kigo: 向日葵 【ひまわり】 himawari, （ひまはり）, sunflower [Helianthus annuus] (late summer).
Notes: Planting sunflowers: searching for the sun above the clouds.

Poem: 身に貯へん金山の蝉の声
Romaji:
mi ni takuwaen
zenzan no
semi no koe
My translation:
Could I store it
in myself: a mountainful 
of cicadas’ screech!
Kigo: 蝉の声 【せみのこえ】 semi no koe, cicada voices (late summer).
Notes: Storing cicada voices in the body like gold in a mine.

Poem: 荒園の力あつまり向日葵立つ
Romaji:
kōen no
chikara atsumari
himawari tatsu
My translation:
Concentrating the strength
of the abandoned garden,
a sunflower stands.
Kigo: 向日葵 【ひまわり】 himawari, （ひまはり）, sunflower [Helianthus annuus] (late summer).
Notes: The rough garden's power gathered into the standing sunflower.

Poem: 秋の暮大魚の骨を海が引く
Romaji:
aki no kure
taigyo no hone wo
umi ga hiku
My translation:
Autumn nightfall—
the skeleton of a huge fish
is drawn out to the sea.
Kigo: 秋の暮 【あきのくれ】 aki no kure, autumn dusk (all autumn).
Notes: The sea drags the large fish's bones away at autumn dusk—vast indifference.

Poem: 海に足浸る三日月に首吊らば
Romaji:
umi ni ashi 
hitaru mikazuki ni 
kubi tsuraba
My translation:
The ocean would soak
my feet, if the crescent moon
hanged me by the neck.
Kigo: 三日月 【みかづき】 mikazuki, crescent moon (all autumn).
Notes: Dipping feet in the sea under a crescent moon—Sanki's dark surrealism.

Poem: いづかたも水行く途中春の暮
Romaji:
izukata mo
muzu yuku tochū
haru no kure
My translation:
everywhere
water in the midst of going
the end of spring day
Kigo: 春の暮
Notes: ここからは、二つの見解が可能です。一つ目は、中七で切って読む場合です。森羅万象の活動は、人も含めて全て「途中」なのだという見解で、水行きには終点がないということです。水は循環しているから常に「途中」です。 二つ目は、中七で切らない場合です。そうすると、「春の暮」が句の主眼になってきて、冬を過ぎて暮春になったから、水行きは活発なんだという見解になります。どちらを選ぶかは、各人の好みになるでしょうが、句から驚きを得られるのは、前者です。なぜなら、無常観を「途中」という俗語で言い表しているからです。『永田耕衣五百句』

Poem: 啓蟄や光り流るる厨水
Romaji:
keichitsu ya
hikari nagaruru
kuriya-mizu
My translation:
insects awake―
luster flows in
kitchen’s water
Kigo:
Insects awake
啓蟄 keichitsu

Poem: 冬すでに路標にまがふ墓一基
Romaji:
fuyu sudeni
rohyō ni magau 
haka ikki
My translation:
Winter already—
Too much like a signpost,
A gravestone.
Kigo: 冬 【ふゆ】 fuyu, winter.
Notes: 路標 (michishirube) = road marker. A single grave resembling a road marker in winter.

Poem: 空瓶と老いし盲の冬日向
Romaji:
akibin to 
oishi mekura no 
fuyu hinata
My translation:
An empty bottle 
and an aged blind man 
in the winter sunshine
Kigo: 冬日向 【ふゆひなた】 fuyu hinata, winter sunshine (all winter).
Notes: An old blind man and an empty bottle in the winter sunshine—quiet desolation.

Poem: 万緑の中や吾子の歯生え初むる
Romaji:
banryoku no 
naka ya ako no ha
hae somuru
My translation:
Myriad green leaves— 
in their midst my baby
begins to cut his teeth.
Kigo: 万緑 【ばんりょく】 banryoku, myriad green leaves [literally "myriad green"] (all summer).
Notes: In the sea of summer green, the child's first white tooth—a celebrated poem of life.

Poem: 夜の蟻迷えるものは孤を描く
Romaji:
yoru no ari
mayoeru mono wa
ko wo egaku
My translation:
Ants in the nighttime:
the one that has lost its way
crawls in a circle
Kigo: 蟻 【あり】 ari, ant (all summer).
Notes: 孤を描く (ko wo egaku) = drawing a circle of isolation. A lost ant traces a circle—existential isolation.

Poem: 記憶を持たざるもの新雪と跳ぶ栗鼠と
Romaji:
kioku wo motazaru 
mono shinsetsu to 
tobu risu to
My translation:
Things that do not possess
memories: freshly fallen snow
and a leaping squirrel.
Kigo: 新雪 【しんせつ】 shinsetsu, new snow (all winter).
Notes: New snow and a squirrel leaping—both without memory, pure present.

Poem: 耕せばうごき憩えばしづかな土
Romaji:
tagayaseba 
ugoki ikoeba 
shizukana tsuchi
My translation:
When I plough
it moves; when I pause to rest
it is still—the earth.
Kigo: 耕す 【たがやす】 tagayasu, plowing / tilling (all spring).
Notes: When tilled the soil moves; when resting it is quiet—the earth responsive.

Poem: 永久に生きたし女の声と蟬の音と
Romaji:
towa ni ikitashi 
onna no koe to 
semi no ne to
My translation:
How I wish to live
forever! A woman’s voice
and a cicada’s cry.
Kigo: 蝉 【せみ】 semi, cicada (late summer).
Notes: Wanting to live forever: a woman's voice and cicada song.

Poem: 空は太初の青き妻より林檎うく
Romaji:
sora wa taisho no 
aosa tsuma yori 
ringo uku
My translation:
In the sky there is 
primeval blue, and from my wife
I receive an apple.
Kigo: 林檎 【りんご】 ringo, apple(s) [fruit of Malus pumila] (late autumn).
Notes: The sky a primordial blue; a wife offers an apple—Eden imagery.

Poem: 比喩もろとも信仰消えて枯野の日
Romaji:
hiyu morotomo 
shinkō kiete 
kareno no hi
My translation:
The metaphors are 
gone, and so is my faith…
sun over a moor.
Kigo: 枯野 【かれの】 kareno, withered field (all winter).
Notes: Faith dissolving with metaphor, into the winter field's sunlight.

Poem: 炎熱や勝利の如き地の明るさ
Romaji:
ennetsu ya 
shōri no no gotoki 
chi no akarusa
My translation:
Scorching heat: 
like a victory, the brightness 
of the earth.
Kigo: 炎熱 【えんねつ】 ennetsu, scorching heat (all summer).
Notes: The scorching heat gives the earth a brightness like victory.

Poem: 葡萄食ふ一語一語の如くにて
Romaji:
budō kū 
ichigo ichigo no 
gotoku nite
My translation:
Eating grapes— 
like one word, another word, 
and still another.
Kigo: 葡萄 【ぶどう】 budō, （ぶだう）, grapes [eminent haiku masters have placed this kidai in early, mid, and late autumn, apparently according to geographical latitude and local grape production; we follow Inahata Teiko's Hototogisu New Saijiki with an all-autumn designation, leaning toward mid autumn] (all autumn).
Notes: Eating grapes one by one as if each were a word—the grape as unit of language.

Poem: 何事もなかりし如き日盛なり
Romaji:
nanigoto mo 
nakarishi gotoki 
hizakari nari
My translation:
Appearing as if 
nothing had happened, the brightness 
of the midday sun.
Kigo: 日盛 【ひざかり】 hizakari, blazing midday sun (all summer).
Notes: As if nothing happened—the blazing midday continues indifferent.

Poem: 睡蓮や死ならぬもの以て肉浄めよ
Romaji:
suiren ya 
shi naranu mono mote 
niku kiyome yo
My translation:
A water lily: 
may something other than death 
cleanse my body!
Kigo: 睡蓮 【すいれん】 suiren, （すゐれん）, water lily/lilies [white-flowered; Nymphaea species; see also 河骨【こうほね】 kōhone] (late summer).
Notes: The water lily—purify the flesh with what is not death.

Poem: 梅一連踏まれて大地の紋章たり
Romaji:
ume ichirin 
fumarete daichi no 
monshō tari
My translation:
A plum blossom, 
trampled, has become the insignia 
of the earth.
Kigo: 梅 【うめ】 ume, （sometimes むめ mume）, plum (blossoms) [technically, the "Japanese apricot", Prunus mume; but this has almost always been translated "plum" for literary purposes] (early spring).
Notes: A fallen plum blossom trampled becomes the earth's emblem.

Poem: 頭を伏せし蜥蜴と聴けり日の言葉
Romaji:
zu wo fuseshi 
tokage to kikeri 
hi no kotoba
My translation:
With a lizard 
the droops its head, I listen 
to the words of the sun.
Kigo: 蜥蜴 【とかげ】 tokage, lizard (all summer).
Notes: A lizard with bowed head listens to the sun's words.

Poem: 生れて十日生命が赤し風がまぶし
Romaji:
arete tōka 
inochi ga akashi 
kaze ga mabushi
My translation:
Ten days after birth 
the baby’s life is reddish, 
the wind is dazzling.
Kigo: 風 【かぜ】 kaze, wind (all spring).
Notes: 生れて十日 (umarete tōka) = ten days after birth. Ten days old, life is red; the wind dazzling.

Poem: 覇王樹立ち夕蟹走りわれ生れし
Romaji:
saboten tachi 
yūkani hashiri 
ware areshi
My translation:
A cactus stood,
an evening crab scurried, 
and I was born.
Kigo: 覇王樹 【はおうじゅ】 haōju, cactus (all summer).
Notes: Cactus standing, crabs running at dusk—birth as elemental event.

Poem: 三日月のせた水輪こちらへ来たがるよ
Romaji:
mikazuki nosete 
mizuwa kochira e 
kitagaru yo
My translation:
Each carrying a crescent 
moon, water rings are anxious 
to reach me!
Kigo: 三日月 【みかづき】 mikazuki, crescent moon (all autumn).
Notes: The moon's reflection in water rings drifting toward the viewer.

Poem: 玉菜の芯から微かな鶏鳴広漠たり
Romaji:
tamana no shin kara 
kasukana keimei
 kōbaku tari
My translation:
From inside a cabbage 
the faint crow of a rooster— 
vast and desolate.
Kigo: 玉菜 【たまな】 tamana, cabbage (all winter).
Notes: From the cabbage's heart, a faint cock-crow in the vast landscape.

Poem: 旧景が闇を脱ぎゆく大旦
Romaji:
kyūkei ga 
yami wo nugi-yuku 
ō-ashita
My translation:
The familiar scene 
slowly strips off its darkness 
as the New Year dawns.
Kigo: 大旦 【おおあした】 ōashita, New Year's morning (New Year).
Notes: The old landscape shedding its darkness into the New Year morning.

Poem: 夕がすみ灯台ともること早し
Romaji:
yūgasumi 
tōdai tomoru 
koto hayashi
My translation:
evening mist
the lighthouse lights up
a bit early
Kigo: 霞 【かすみ】 kasumi, (spring) mist [frequently translated "haze"; see note "On Haze, Mist, Fog"] (all spring).
Notes: Lighthouse lit early in the spring evening haze—dusk arriving before expected.
Other translation:
evening mist
the lighthouse lights up
a bit early  (UVA)

Poem: 春暁や人こそ知らね木々の雨
Romaji:
shungyō ya
hito koso shirane 
kigi no ame
My translation:
spring dawnー
rain on the trees that
on one knows
Kigo: Spring
Notes: 人こそ知らね (hito koso shirane) = though people may not know. Spring dawn; people unaware while the trees are drenched in rain.

Poem: 春の灯や女は持たぬのどぼとけ
Romaji:
haru no hi ya 
onna wa motanu 
nodobotoke
My translation:
Spring evening’s lamplight: 
a woman; she does not have 
an Adam’s apple.
Kigo: 春の灯 【はるのひ】 haru no hi, spring lamp / spring light (all spring).
Notes: Spring lamplight; a woman—she has no Adam's apple.

Poem: ものの種握ぎれば生命ひしめける
Romaji:
mono-dane wo 
nigireba inochi 
hishimekeru
My translation:
Seeds of some sort一
grasping them, I feel the jostle
of lives against my palm.
Kigo: 種 【たね】 tane, seed(s) (spring).
Notes: Holding seeds in the fist—life pressing and jostling inside.

Poem: 春暁や人こそ知らね木々の雨
Romaji:
shungyō ya
hito koso shirane
kigi no ame
My translation:
Early spring dawn: 
nobody else would know of
this rain on the trees.
Kigo: 春暁 【しゅんぎょう】 shungyō, （しゅんげう）, spring dawn (all spring).
Notes: Duplicate of Row 477.

Poem: 凩や堕胎草煮たれども
Romaji:
kogarashi ya 
oroshi-gusa ni wa 
nitare domo
My translation:
Wintry gusts:
abortion-herb is boiling
and yet … and yet …
Kigo: 木枯らし 【こがらし】 kogarashi, wintry gust (early winter).
Notes: 堕胎草 (datai-gusa) = abortifacient herb. The cold wind; herbs to cause miscarriage are boiled but seem useless.

Poem: 朝寒や歯磨匂ふ妻の口
Romaji:
asa samu ya 
hamigaki niou 
tsuma no kuchi
My translation:
The morning cold:
smelling of tooth power,
my wife’s mouth.
Kigo: 朝寒 【あさざむ】 asazamu, morning cold (late autumn).
Notes: Morning cold; the wife's mouth fragrant with toothpaste—marital intimacy.

Poem: わが思ひ月かげとなり空に満つ
Romaji:
waga omoi 
tsuki kage to nari 
sora ni mitsu
My translation:
My pondering
turns into the moonlight
filling the sky.
Kigo: 月 【つき】 tsuki, moon (mid autumn).
Notes: My thoughts become moonlight filling the sky.

Poem: かいつぶりさびしくなればくぐりけり
Romaji:
kairsuburi 
sabishiku nareba 
kuguri-keri
My translation:
The grebe
when it becomes lonely
dives into the water.
Kigo: 鳰 【にお】 niō, grebe (all autumn).
Notes: When it grows lonely, the grebe dives under—evasion as emotional response.

Poem: 眼をとぢてむかしの恋にあたたまる
Romaji:
me wo tojite 
mukashi no koi ni 
atatamaru
My translation:
I close my eyes
and bask in the warmth of love
that is long past.
Kigo: 冬 【ふゆ】 fuyu, winter.
Notes: Closing the eyes and warming oneself in an old love—winter introspection.

Poem: いなづまにまばたきしたる枯木達
Romaji:
inazuma ni 
mabataki shi taru 
kareki tachi
My translation:
At a flash of lighting
they blinked their eyes一
the leafless trees.
Kigo: 稲妻 【いなずま】 inazuma, lightning (all autumn).
Notes: 枯木達 (kareki-tachi) = bare trees. Lightning; the bare trees seem to blink.

Poem: ひと拗ねてものいはず白き薔薇となる
Romaji:
At a flash of lighting
they blinked their eyes一
the leafless trees.
My translation:
She sulks,
says nothing, and becomes
a white rose.
Kigo: 白き薔薇 【しろきばら】 shiroki bara, white rose (summer).
Notes: Someone sulking and silent—becoming a white rose.

Poem: 熱退きぬ空漠として黄の疲弊
Romaji:
netsu hikinu 
kūbaku to shite 
ki no tsukare
My translation:
The fever is gone.
in the immeasurable void,
yellow weariness.
Kigo: 熱退く 【ねつひく】 netsu hiku, fever breaking (summer).
Notes: After the fever breaks: a vast, yellow exhaustion.

Poem: 朝顔やおもひを遂げしごとしぼむ
Romaji:
asagao ya
omoi wo togeshi
goto shibomu
My translation:
The morning-glory:
like fulfilled desire
it withers away.
Kigo: 朝顔 【あさがお】 asagao, morning glory (late summer/autumn).
Notes: The morning glory wilts as if having gotten what it wanted.

Poem: 十六夜や溲瓶かがやく縁の端
Romaji:
izayoi ya
shubin kagayaku
en no hashi
My translation:
Moon sixteen nights old:
my urine glass glitters
at the veranda’s edge.
Kigo: 十六夜 【いざよい】 izayoi, the sixteenth night / moon (mid autumn).
Notes: 溲瓶 (shōbin) = urinal. The sixteenth-night moon glittering on the bedpan—sick-room poetry.

Poem: 夜番柝を打つ月光にひび走る
Romaji:
yoban ki wo
utsu gekkō ni
hibi hashiru
My translation:
A night watch
strikes his clappers一at the sound
cracks run up the moonlight.
Kigo: 月光 【げっこう】 gekkō, moonlight (mid autumn).
Notes: The night watchman's clapper: moonlight cracks.

Poem: 妻が持つ薊の棘を手に感ず
Romaji:
tsuma ga
motsu azami no toge wo 
te ni kanzu
My translation:
My wife holds
a thistle一I feel its prickles
in my hand.
Kigo: 薊 【あざみ】 azami, thistle (late spring).
Notes: Sensing the thistle's thorn through the wife's hand—domestic tenderness and pain.

Poem: 夏の闇高熱のわれ発光す
Romaji:
natsu no yami 
kōnetsu no ware 
hakkō-su
My translation:
Dark summer night一
sick and feverish, I
emit a gleam.
Kigo: 夏の闇 【なつのやみ】 natsu no yami, summer darkness (all summer).
Notes: 高熱のわれ発光す = I with high fever emit light. In the summer dark, the feverish poet glows.

Poem: 荒草の今は枯れつつ安らかに
Romaji:
arakusa no 
ima wa kare tsutsu 
yasurakani
My translation:
The weeds
are now beginning to wither,
and in peace, too.
Kigo: 枯草 【かれくさ】 karekusa, withered plants [includes more than grasses] (all winter).
Notes: Withered grass withering peacefully now—acceptance of decay.

Poem: 秋の道日かげに入りて日に出でて
Romaji:
aki no michi 
hikage ni irite 
hi ni idete
My translation:
The autumn road
enters the shade一and emerges
into the sunshine.
Kigo: 秋の道 【あきのみち】 aki no michi, autumn road (all autumn).
Notes: Walking the autumn road in and out of sunlight.

Poem: 見えぬ目の方の眼鏡の玉も拭く
Romaji:
mienu me no 
hō no megane no 
tama mo fuku
My translation:
Its sight has been lost
and yet, for that eye also
I polish the eyeglass.
Kigo: 眼鏡 【めがね】 megane, eyeglasses.
Notes: Polishing both lenses even though one eye can't see—compulsive care.

Poem: リラの香と気づきて昼寝さめにけり
Romaji:
rira no ka to 
kizukite hirune 
same ni keri
My translation:
It’s the lilac’s scent一
So I notice, and wake
From my noonday nap.
Kigo: リラ rira, lilac (early summer).
Notes: Waking from a midday nap, suddenly aware of lilac scent.

Poem: 雨はれてふたたび寒し根深汁
Romaji:
ame harete
futatabi samushi
nebuke-jiru
My translation:
the rain cleared
again it’s cold
green onion soup
Kigo: 根深汁 【ねぶかじる】 nebukajiru, leek soup (all winter).
Notes: Rain clearing; cold again; leek soup—winter's simple comforts.

Poem: スケートの紐むすぶ間も逸りつつ
Romaji:
sukeeto no
himo musubu ma mo
hayari tsutsu
My translation:
while lacing up
my skates
growing
Kigo: skate

Poem: 七月の青嶺まぢかく溶鉱炉
Romaji:
shichigatsu no 
aone majikaku 
yōkōro
My translation:
On a July day 
near the green mountains, 
a smelting furnace.
Kigo: 七月 【しちがつ】 shichigatsu, July (mid summer).
Notes: A blast furnace and the blue mountain peak in July—industrial and natural sublime.

Poem: かりかりと蟷螂蜂の皃を食むとは
Romaji:
karikari to
tōrō hachi no 
kao wo hamu
My translation:
With a crunching sound 
the praying mantis devours 
the face of a bee.
Kigo: 蟷螂 【かまきり】 kamakiri, praying mantis (all autumn).
Notes: かりかりと (karikari to) = crunchily. A praying mantis crunching a wasp's face.

Poem: 夏草に気罐車の車輪来て止る
Romaji:
natsu kusa ni 
kikansha no sharin 
kite tomaru
My translation:
Amid the summer grass 
the wheels of a steam engine 
come to a standstill.
Kigo: 夏草 【なつくさ】 natsukusa, summer grasses (all summer).
Notes: A steam engine wheel coming to rest in the summer grass.

Poem: 春潮やわが総身に船の汽笛
Romaji:
shunchō ya 
waga sōshin ni 
fune no fue
My translation:
The spring tide: 
piercing my entire body, 
the whistle from a boat.
Kigo: 春潮 【はるしお】 harushio, spring tide (all spring).
Notes: 船の汽笛 (fune no kiteki) = a ship's steam whistle. The spring tide; a ship's whistle resonates through the whole body.

Poem: 夏の河赤き鉄鎖のはし浸る
Romaji:
natsu no kawa 
akaki tessa no 
hashi hitaru
My translation:
River in summer一 
a red iron chain, its end 
soaking in the water.
Kigo: 夏の河 【なつのかわ】 natsu no kawa, summer river (all summer).
Notes: 赤き鉄鎖 (akaki tessho) = a red iron chain. A red iron chain's end submerged in the summer river.

Poem: 秋風が通るに嬰児片眼をあき
Romaji:
aki kaze ga 
tōru ni eiji 
katame wo aki
My translation:
An autumnal wind 
passes by, and a little baby 
opens an eye.
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn).
Notes: The autumn wind passing; an infant opens one eye.

Poem: ひとり膝を抱けば秋風また秋風
Romaji:
hitori hiza wo 
dakeba aki kaze 
mata aki kaze
My translation:
All alone, I hug 
my knees...an autumnal wind, 
again, autumnal wind.
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn).
Notes: Sitting alone, knees hugged: autumn wind, and again autumn wind.

Poem: 水甕に浮べる蟻の影はなく
Romaji:
mizugame ni 
ukaberu ari no 
kage wa naku
My translation:
In the water jar 
floats an ant, and its shadow 
is not.
Kigo: 蟻 【あり】 ari, ant (all summer).
Notes: An ant's shadow floating in the water jar—but no actual ant; only shadow.

Poem: 声なりしやと炎天を顧みる
Romaji:
koe narishi ya 
to enten wo 
kaerimiru
My translation:
Was that a voice? 
Back toward the sweltering sky 
I turn my face.
Kigo: 炎天 【えんてん】 enten, blazing sky (late summer).
Notes: 声なりしや (koe nari shi ya) = was that a voice? Looking back at the blazing sky.

Poem: 炎天の遠き帆やわがこころの帆
Romaji:
enten no 
tōki ho ya waga 
kokoro no ho
My translation:
Under the flaming sky, 
a distant sail: in my 
heart, a sail.
Kigo: 炎天 【えんてん】 enten, blazing sky (late summer).
Notes: A distant sail in the blazing sky—the sail of my own heart.

Poem: 夕焼や思ひかへして貝拾ふ
Romaji:
yūyake ya 
omoi kaeshite 
kai hirou
My translation:
The sunset glow: 
changing my mind, I pick up 
a seashell.
Kigo: 夕焼 【ゆうやけ】 yūyake, （ゆふやけ）, afterglow (late summer).
Notes: Reconsidering at the sunset—picking up a shell after all.

Poem: 昼見たる蟻を暗夜に思ひ出づ
Romaji:
hiru mitaru 
ari wo anya ni 
omoi-izu
My translation:
In the daytime I saw 
an ant, and it haunts my mind 
in this darkness of night.
Kigo: 蟻 【あり】 ari, ant (all summer).
Notes: An ant seen in daytime, recalled in the dark night.

Poem: 少女たるよろこび春の日に瞑る
Romaji:
shōjo taru 
yorokobi haru no 
hi ni metsumuru
My translation:
Delighted to be born 
a girl, in the spring sun 
she closes her eyes.
Kigo: 春の日 【はるのひ】 haru no hi, spring day (all spring).
Notes: The joy of being a girl, closing eyes in the spring sunlight.

Poem: やさしさは殻透くばかり蝸牛
Romaji:
yasashisa wa 
kara suku bakari 
katatsumuri
My translation:
The gentleness 
pervades its shell一 
a snail.
Kigo: 蝸牛 【かたつむり】 katatsumuri, snail / land snail (all summer).
Notes: The snail's shell nearly transparent with gentleness.

Poem: 行く雁の啼くとき宙の感ぜられ
Romaji:
yuku kari no 
naku toki chū no 
kanzerare
My translation:
Passing in the sky 
wild geese call; that instant 
a feel of the mid-air.
Kigo: 春

Poem: 昼寝の中しばしば釘を打ち込まる
Romaji:
hirune no naka 
shibashiba kugi wo 
uchikomaru
My translation:
Into my midday nap, 
again and again, someone 
hammers a nail.
Kigo: 昼寝 【ひるね】 hirune, midday nap / siesta (all summer).
Notes: Nails driven in during the nap—the body registering sound as sensation.

Poem: 秋の暮水中もまた暗くなる
Romaji:
aki no kure 
suichū mo mata 
kuraku naru
My translation:
Evening in autumn一 
under the water also 
it becomes dark.
Kigo: 秋の暮 【あきのくれ】 aki no kure, autumn dusk (all autumn).
Notes: Autumn dusk: the underwater world darkening too.

Poem: 浪にあとかたもなし女と泳ぎしが
Romaji:
nami ni atokata 
mo nashi onna to 
oyogishi ga
My translation:
In the waves no trace 
remains, though I have swum there 
with a woman.
Kigo: 泳ぎ 【およぎ】 oyogi, swimming (all summer).
Notes: After swimming with a woman, the waves leave no trace.

Poem: 死にければ闇たちこむる蛍籠
Romaji:
shi ni kereba 
yami tachikomuru 
hotaru kago
My translation:
Since they died 
darkness fills up the space 
in the firefly cage.
Kigo: 蛍籠 【ほたるかご】 hotaru-kago, firefly cage (mid summer).
Notes: When the firefly died, the cage filled with darkness.

Poem: 冬河に新聞全紙浸り浮く
Romaji:
fuyu kawa ni 
shinbun zenshi
tsukari uku
My translation:
In the winter river 
a whole sheet of newspaper, 
soaked through, floating.
Kigo: 冬河 【ふゆかわ】 fuyukawa, winter river (all winter).
Notes: The entire newspaper soaking and floating in the winter river—information dissolved.

Poem: 枯葦を瞳につめこんでたちもどる
Romaji:
kareashi o 
me ni tsumekonde
tachimodoru
My translation:
Withered reeds—
I stuff them into my eyes
and trudge towards home.
Kigo: 枯葦 【かれあし】 kare-ashi, withered reeds (all autumn).
Notes: Withered reeds crammed into the pupils—intense, surrealist vision.

Poem: 蝶墜ちて大音響の結氷期
Romaji:
chō ochite
daionkyō no
keppyōki
My translation:
As a butterfly
plummets, a thunderous crash
in the freezing season.
Kigo: 結氷期
Notes: 結氷期 (kekkyōki) = the freezing period. A butterfly falls; a vast sound of freezing fills the world—surrealist scale contrast.

Poem: 彷徨へる馬郷愁となりて消えぬ
Romaji:
samayoeru
uma kyōshū to
narite kienu
My translation:
A wandering horse,
turning in a longing
for home, vanishes.
Kigo: 馬 【うま】 uma, horse.
Notes: The wandering horse becomes homesickness and vanishes—surrealist metamorphosis.

Poem: 冬天に牡丹のやうなひとの舌
Romaji:
tōten ni
botan no yōna
hito no shita
My translation:
Under the winter sky
it looks like a peony:
the woman's tongue.
Kigo: 冬天 【ふゆてん】 fuyuten, winter sky (all winter).
Notes: In the winter sky, a person's tongue like a peony—erotic surrealism.

Poem: 椿散るああなまぬるき昼の火事
Romaji:
tsubaki chiru
aa namanuruki
hiru no kaji
My translation:
Camellias fall.
Ah, what a lukewarm
fire in the daytime!
Kigo: 椿 【つばき】 tsubaki, camellia(s) (all spring).
Notes: Camellias falling—a fire spreading in tepid midday.

Poem: 豹の檻一滴の水天になし
Romaji:
hyō no ori
itteki no mizu
ten ni nashi
My translation:
The leopard's cage:
not a drop of water
in heaven.
Kigo: 豹 【ひょう】 hyō, leopard (summer).
Notes: A leopard in its cage—not a drop of water in the sky above.

Poem: 岩黝く憂愁の牡蠣うすびかる
Romaji:
iwa kuroku
yūshū no kaki
usubikaru
My translation:
The rocks are dark
and a melancholy oyster
faintly gleams.
Kigo: 牡蠣 【かき】 kaki, oyster (all winter).
Notes: Melancholy oysters glimmering faintly on dark rocks.

Poem: 秋風は蛇のぬけがらより白し
Romaji:
akikaze wa
hibe no nukegara
yori shiroshi
My translation:
The autumnal wind
surpasses an empty snakeskin
in whiteness.
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn).
Notes: The autumn wind whiter than the shed snakeskin.

Poem: 咳けば枯木の天も咳けり
Romaji:
shiwabukeba
kareki no ten mo
shiwabukeri
My translation:
As I cough
heaven above the leafless trees
coughs too.
Kigo: 咳 【せき】 seki, cough (all winter).
Notes: Coughing; the bare-tree sky coughs too—the world sharing the illness.

Poem: 炎天に跫音きえて哄笑はのこる
Romaji:
enten ni 
ashioto kiete 
kōshō wa nokoru
My translation:
In the sweltering sky
the sound of footsteps fades
and the laughter remains.
Kigo: 炎天 【えんてん】 enten, blazing sky (late summer).
Notes: Footsteps vanish in the blazing sky; loud laughter remains.

Poem: 嘘吐いて光彩うつくしきつららかな
Romaji:
uso tsuite
iro utsukushiki
tsurara kana
My translation:
Uttering a lie 
with beautiful colours,
an icicle.
Kigo: つらら 【つらら】 tsurara, icicle(s) (all winter).
Notes: An icicle beautiful as a told lie—the aesthetics of deception.

Poem: 黄昏の喪章黒犬がうづくまる
Romaji:
tasogare no
moshō kuroinu ga
uzukumaru
My translation:
In the evening dusk
a mourning badge: a black dog
crouches.
Kigo: 喪章 【もしょう】 moshō, mourning band.
Notes: A mourning armband at dusk; a black dog crouches—images of grief.

Poem: 葡萄一粒一粒の弾力と雲
Romaji:
būdō hitotsubu
hitotsubu no
danryoku to kumo
My translation:
Grapes, each one of them with
resilience, and clouds
Kigo: 葡萄 【ぶどう】 budō, （ぶだう）, grapes [eminent haiku masters have placed this kidai in early, mid, and late autumn, apparently according to geographical latitude and local grape production; we follow Inahata Teiko's Hototogisu New Saijiki with an all-autumn designation, leaning toward mid autumn] (all autumn).
Notes: Each grape's elasticity against the clouds.

Poem: 錐をもむ暗澹として錐をもむ
Romaji:
kiri wo momu
antan to shite 
kiri wo momu
My translation:
I keep rubbing an awl,
in the darkness of despair
I keep rubbing an awl.
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 錐をもむ (kiri wo momu) = turning an awl. Grinding an awl in dark despair—endless, mechanical repetition.

Poem: 雲にあるあかるさ葦にあるくらさ
Romaji:
kumo ni aru
akarusa ashi ni
aru kurasa
My translation:
Brightness that lies
in the clouds: darkness
that lies in the reeds
Kigo: 葦 【あし】 ashi, reed (all autumn).
Notes: The sky bright; the reeds dark—visual contrast.

Poem: ひとの瞳の中の蟻蟻蟻蟻蟻
Romaji:
hito no me no
naka ni ari ari
ari ari ari
My translation:
Within her eyes
ant, ant, ant, ant, ant.
Kigo: 蟻 【あり】 ari, ant (all summer).
Notes: Surrealist multiplication of ants in the human eye.

Poem: 春は白い卵と白い卵の影と
Romaji:
haru wa shiroi
tamago to shiroi
tamago no kage to
My translation:
Spring:
white eggs
and white eggs' shadows.
Kigo: 卵 【たまご】 tamago, egg (spring).
Notes: Spring as white eggs and their shadows—pure, minimal.

Poem: 善意？どこまでつづく零の環よ
Romaji:
zen'i?
doko made tsuzuku
zero no wa you
My translation:
Good will?
How far do the rings
of zeros extend?
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 善意 (zen'i) = goodwill. How far does goodwill extend?—a zero ring without end.

Poem: 結論のごとく地に跼し蟇
Romaji:
ketsuron no
gotoku chi ni kyoshi
hikigaeru
My translation:
Like a conclusion
it crouches on the ground—
a toad.
Kigo: 蟇 【ひきがえる】 hikigaeru, （ひきがへる）, toad [Bufo vulgaris] (all summer).
Notes: A toad crouching like a conclusion on the ground—philosophical finality.

Romaji:
gunkan ga 
shizundaumi no
oitaru kamome
My translation:
An aged seagull
over waters where a warship foundered.

Poem: 初夏の一日一日と庭のさま
Romaji:
hatsu natsu no
hito hi hito hi to
niwa no sama
My translation:
early summer
day by day
the garden's appearance
Kigo: 初夏 shoka Early summer

Poem: うごけば、寒い
Romaji:
ugokeba,
samui
My translation:
if you move,
its cold
Kigo: 寒い
Notes: normally when you move, you feel warm, but if it is very cold moving makes you feel colder

Poem: 子の髪の風に流るる五月来ぬ
Romaji:
ko no kami no
kaze ni nagaruru
satsuki kinu
My translation:
a child's hair
flows in the wind and
the fifth month has come
Kigo: 夏  Natsu  [Summer / Season]

Poem: かなしめば鵙金色の目を負ひ来
Romaji:
kanashimeba
mozu konjiki no 
hi wo oi ku
My translation:
I grieve, and there comes 
a shrike, with golden sunbeams
on its back.
Kigo: 鵙 【もず】 mozu, shrike [Lanius species] (all autumn).
Notes: When I grieve, the shrike comes with golden eyes—the bird as witness of sorrow.

Poem: 枯るるもの枯れゆき林しづかなり
Romaji:
karuru mono
kare yuki hayashi 
shizukanari
My translation:
All that withers
has withered away, and the grove
reposes in calm.
Kigo: 枯れゆく 【かれゆく】 kareyuku, withering (all autumn).
Notes: As withering things wither, the forest grows quiet—acceptance.

Poem: 木木霞み遠ひかるもの鷺となりぬ
Romaji:
kigi kasumi
tōhikaru mono
sagi to narinu
My translation:
Trees are in a hazeー
something gleaming in the distance
has become a heron.
Kigo: 霞 【かすみ】 kasumi, (spring) mist [frequently translated "haze"; see note "On Haze, Mist, Fog"] (all spring).
Notes: Trees and mist in the distance; the shining thing became a heron—metamorphosis.

Poem: わが凭りし冬木戦車の音となる
Romaji:
waga yorishi
fuyuki sensha no
oto to naru
My translation:
The winter tree
I am leaning on has turned
into a tank’s roar.
Kigo: 冬木 【ふゆき】 fuyuki, bare winter tree(s) (all winter).
Notes: Leaning against a winter tree; the sound becomes that of a tank—war trauma in the landscape.

Poem: 坂くだる寒き夕焼に腕を振り
Romaji:
saka kudaru
samuki yūyake ni
ude wo furi
Kigo: 寒き夕焼 【さむきゆうやけ】 samuki yūyake, cold evening glow (winter).
Notes: Descending a slope into the cold sunset, swinging the arms.

Poem: 蟻殺すわれを三人の子に見られぬ
Romaji:
ari korosu
ware wo sannin no 
ko ni mirarenu
My translation:
I kill an ant
and realize my three children
have been watching.
Kigo: 蟻 【あり】 ari, ant (all summer).
Notes: Killing an ant; caught in the act by three children—unexpected moral witness.

Poem: 屋上に見し朝焼のながからず
Romaji:
okujō ni
mishi asayake no
nagakarazu
My translation:
From atop the roof
I gaze at the morning glow
that does not last long.
Kigo: 朝焼 【あさやけ】 asayake, morning glow (all autumn).
Notes: A rooftop dawn that didn't last long—the brief beauty of early morning.

Poem: 蟷螂に蟷螂のごとくわが手を立つ
Romaji:
tōrō ni 
tōrō no gotoku
waga te wo tatsu
My translation:
At a mantis
I brandish my hand--like
a mantis.
Kigo: 蟷螂 【かまきり】 kamakiri, praying mantis (all autumn).
Notes: Raising a hand like a praying mantis—to face a praying mantis as an equal.

Poem: 火を消すや心崖なす月の前
Romaji:
hi wo kesu ya
kokoro gake nasu
tsuki no mae
My translation:
I put out the light.
In my heart a precipice
before the moon.
Kigo: 月 【つき】 tsuki, moon (mid autumn).
Notes: The heart a cliff-face before the moon.

Poem: 灼け砂に果てにしものの形ただし
Romaji:
yakezuna ni 
hatenishi mono no
katachi tadashi
My translation:
On the scorching sand
lies a lost life, with its shape
impeccably preserved.
Kigo: 灼け砂 【やけすな】 yake-suna, scorched sand (all summer).
Notes: Something that ended on the scorched sand—its shape is still exact.

Poem: 雉子の眸のかうかうとして売られけり
Romaji:
From the hydrangea’s
shade a pair of eyes watch:
as I look, nothing.
My translation:
A pheasant, with eyes
defiantly glaring,
is being sold.
Kigo: 雉子 【きじ】 kiji, pheasant (all spring).
Notes: The pheasant's blazing eyes as it is sold—defiant life.

Poem: 紫陽花の蔭に目があり見ればなし
Romaji:
ajisai no
kage ni me ga ari
mireba nashi
My translation:
From the hydrangea’s
shade a pair of eyes watch:
as I look, nothing.
Kigo: 紫陽花 【あじさい】 ajisai, （あぢさゐ）, hydrangea (blossoms) [Hydrangea macrophylla] (mid summer).
Notes: Eyes in the shadow of the hydrangea—only to find nothing there.

Poem: 寒雷や今は亡き目を負ひて生く
Romaji:
kanrai ya
Ima wa naki me wo
oite iku
My translation:
Thunder in midwinter:
the eyes of a dead friend
looking on, I live.
Kigo: 寒雷 【かんらい】 kanrai, winter thunder (all winter).
Notes: One of Shūson's most celebrated poems—living with the eyes of the now-dead.

Poem: 猫と生れ人間と生れ露に歩す
Romaji:
neko to umare
nengen to umare
tsuyu ni hosu
My translation:
She was born a cat
and I was born a man一
we walk in the dew.
Kigo: 露 【つゆ】 tsuyu, dew (mid autumn).
Notes: Born a cat, born a human, all walking in autumn dew.

Poem: 霜夜子は泣く父母よりはるかなるものを呼ぶ
Romaji:
shimoyo ko wa 
naku fubo yori harukanaru 
mono wo yobi
My translation:
This frosty night a baby
cries, craving for something 
far more than its parents.
Kigo: 霜夜 【しもよ】 shimoyo, frosty night (all winter).
Notes: The baby's cry calling something beyond parents—the numinous.

Poem: 雪の中鴉のむくろ目をあけゑゐる
Romaji:
yuki no naka 
karasu no mukuro 
me wo akeiru
My translation:
Amid the snow 
lies the corpse of a crow 
with its eyes open.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: A dead crow in the snow, eyes open—austere winter image.

Poem: 見つつ過ぐ秋風が松の傷吹くを
Romaji:
mitsutsu sugu 
akikaze ga matsu no 
kizu fuku wo
My translation:
Passing by, I see 
an autumnal wind blowing 
at a pine tree’s wound.
Kigo: 秋風 【あきかぜ】 akikaze, autumn breeze / autumn wind [carries with it the sound of rustling leaves] (all autumn).
Notes: The autumn wind blowing the pine's wound—the tree's scar as mouth.

Poem: 落葉地にとどくや時間ゆるみけり
Romaji:
ochiba chi ni 
todoku ya jikan 
yurumi-keri
My translation:
A falling leaf:
the moment it reaches the ground
time slows down.
Kigo: 落葉 【おちば】 ochiba, fallen leaves (all autumn).
Notes: The fallen leaf taking so long to land that time seems to slow.

Poem: 秋の風鶏の見るもの我に見えぬ
Romaji:
aki no kaze 
tori no miru mono 
ware ni mienu
My translation:
The wind of autumn一
a chicken gazes at something
I cannot see.
Kigo: 秋の風 【あきのかぜ】 aki no kaze, autumn wind (all autumn).
Notes: The chicken sees something I cannot—multiple worlds in the autumn wind.

Poem: 柚子匂ふすぐそこ死に目ひらけば
Romaji:
yuzu niou 
sugu soko no shi ni 
me hirakeba
My translation:
The scent of citron 
as i open my eyes to death 
right beside me.
Kigo: 柚子 【ゆず】 yuzu, citron [a small citrus fruit, Citrus medica (late autumn).
Notes: Yuzu fragrance; if the dying eyes open—the last sense.

Poem: 鮟鱇の骨までいててぶちきらる
Romaji:
ankō no
hone made itete
buchikiraru
My translation:
the anglerfish
split open
as if frozen to the bone
Kigo: 鮟鱇
Notes: Anglerfish are ugly fish that live on the bottom of the ocean, you cut them while they are hanging

Poem: 春暮るる花なき庭の落花かな
Romaji:
haru kururu
hana naki niwa no
rakka kana
My translation:
spring comes to an end…
in a garden without flowers,
some fallen petals
Kigo:
Spring dusk 
春の暮 haru no kure

Poem: ひさびさの杖を手にして春めきし
Romaji:
hisabisa no
tsue wo te ni shite
haru-mekishi
My translation:
taking in hand 
my old walking stick
as spring grows vernal
Kigo:
Vernal signs
春めくharu-meku

Poem: 冬薔薇紅く咲かんと黒みもつ
Romaji:
fuyu sōbi
akaku sakan to
kuromi motsu
My translation:
winter rose
with enough black
to bloom with red
Kigo: 冬薔薇

Poem: 夏浅きゆうべの空のいろなりけり
Romaji:
natsu asaki
yūbe no sora no
iro narikeri
My translation:
slightly summery
the color of 
the dusk sky
Kigo:
夏めくnatsu meku 
Summery or summer-like

Poem: 夏あさきゆふべの空のいろなりけり
Romaji:
natsu asaki
yube no sora no
iro nari keri
My translation:
shallow summer
the evening sky
becomes colored
Kigo:
Shallow summer
夏浅し natsu asashi

Poem: しぐるるや駅に西口東口
Romaji:
shigururu ya
eki ni nishi-guchi
higashi-guchi
My translation:
winter drizzle falling--
outside the train station's west enterence, 
east enterence
Kigo: しぐる

Poem: 花の冷えと花の重たさの下をゆく
Romaji:
hana no hie to 
hana no omotasa no 
shita wo yuki
My translation:
from blossom chill
darkness appeared
the lamp-lighter
Kigo:
Blossom chill
花冷 hana-bie

Poem: 立春の米こぼれをり葛西橋
Romaji:
risshun no
kome kobore-ori
kasai-bashi
My translation:
beginning of spring
rice is spilt
on the Kasai Bridge
Kigo: Beginning of spring

Poem: 花冷の顔ばかりなり雲の中
Romaji:
hana-bie no 
kao bakari nari 
kumo no naka
My translation:
blossom chill
they are only faces 
in clouds
Kigo: 花冷え 【はなびえ】 hanabie, (cherry) blossom chill [chilly late spring weather] (late spring).
Notes: In the flower chill, only faces visible in the clouds.

Poem: 檻の鷲さびしくなれば羽つかも
Romaji:
ori no washi 
sabishiku nareba 
ha utsu mako
My translation:
The caged eagle,
beginning to feel lonely, 
flaps his wings.
Kigo: 鷲 【わし】 washi, eagle (all autumn).
Notes: A caged eagle—when lonely, it preens. Dignity in captivity.

Poem: 秋の暮業火となりて秬は燃ゆ
Romaji:
aki no kure 
gōka to narite 
kibi wa moyu
My translation:
Nightfall in autumn— 
turning into flames of hellfire, 
cornhusks burn.
Kigo: 秋の暮 【あきのくれ】 aki no kure, autumn dusk (all autumn).
Notes: At autumn dusk, barley burns into hellfire.

Poem: さくらの芽のはげしさ仰ぎ蹌めける
Romaji:
sakura no me 
no hageshisa aogi 
yoromekeru
My translation:
In the cherry tree’s buds 
an intense force; looking upward 
at them, I stagger.
Kigo: 桜の芽 【さくらのめ】 sakura no me, cherry bud (early spring).
Notes: Looking up at the fierce cherry buds, stumbling—overcome by the violence of spring.

Poem: 蟬の朝愛憎は悉く我に還る
Romaji:
semi no asa 
aizō wa kotogotoshiku 
ware ni kaeru
My translation:
Cicadas’ morning— 
all my loves and hatreds 
have come back to me.
Kigo: 蝉 【せみ】 semi, cicada (late summer).
Notes: On a cicada morning, all love and hatred return to the self.

Poem: 霜の道馬糞その他をうべなへり
Romaji:
shimo no michi 
bafun sono ta wo 
ubenari
My translation:
On the frosty road 
horse dung lies—I accept it, 
and everything else.
Kigo: 霜の道 【しものみち】 shimo no michi, frosted road (mid winter).
Notes: The frosted road accepts horse dung and everything else—equanimity.

Poem: 朝寒の市電兵馬と別れたり
Romaji:
asa samu no 
shiden heiba to 
wakaretari
My translation:
In the morning cold 
a streetcar begins to part 
from soldiers and horses.
Kigo: 朝寒 【あさざむ】 asazamu, morning cold (late autumn).
Notes: A morning-cold street car; separating from a soldier going to war—wartime farewell.

Poem: 朝顔の紺の彼方の月日かな
Romaji:
asagao no 
kon no kanata no 
tsukihi kana
My translation:
The morning-glory—
far beyond its dark blue,
months and days to come.
Kigo: 朝顔 【あさがお】 asagao, morning glory (late summer/autumn).
Notes: The deep blue of morning glory; time stretching beyond.

Poem: 貨車寒し百千の墓うちふるひ
Romaji:
kasha samushi 
hyaku sen no haka 
uchifurui
My translation:
Freight trains, cold. 
Hundreds and thousands of tombstones 
trembling with them.
Kigo: 寒し 【さむし】 samushi, cold [of weather, air, and the like] (all winter).
Notes: A freight car; hundreds of graves shaking in the cold—wartime displacement.

Poem: 蝶死にて流るる水を今も踰ゆ
Romaji:
chō shinite 
nagaruru mizu wo 
ima mo koyu
My translation:
The butterfly, now dead, 
floats across the flowing water 
once again.
Kigo: 蝶 【ちょう】 chō, （てふ）, butterfly [the spring butterfly image is typically a cabbage white, white members of the family Pieridae; see also "summer butterfly", etc.] (all spring).
Notes: A dead butterfly; still crossing the flowing water—life persisting after death.

Poem: 焼跡に透きとほりけり寒の水
Romaji:
yakeato ni 
sukitōri keri 
kan no mizu
My translation:
Amid the debris 
perfectly transparent 
midwinter water.
Kigo: 寒の水 【かんのみず】 kan no mizu, cold-season water (mid winter).
Notes: Cold water transparent in the bomb ruins—clarity after destruction.

Poem: 稲妻す妻の来し方我行く方
Romaji:
inazuma su 
tsuma no koshi kata 
waga yuku kata
My translation:
Lightning flashes 
where my wife has come from, 
whither I go.
Kigo: 稲妻 【いなずま】 inazuma, lightning (all autumn).
Notes: Lightning: the direction my wife came from and I am going to.

Poem: 蛼赤しほのぼの熱の上るとき
Romaji:
kōrogi akashi 
honobono netsu no 
agaru toki
My translation:
A red cricket. 
My fever, glimmering, 
reaches a peak.
Kigo: 蛼 【こおろぎ】 kōrogi, cricket (all autumn).
Notes: The cricket red; the fever rising—autumn insects and illness intertwined.

Poem: 栗咲く香血を喀く前もその後も
Romaji:
kuri saku ka 
chi wo haku mae mo 
sono ato mo
My translation:
Chestnut blossoms were fragrant 
before I vomited blood— 
and they are still.
Kigo: 栗の花 【くりのはな】 kuri no hana, chestnut blossom (early summer).
Notes: The chestnut blooms before and after the poet coughs blood—life surrounding illness.

Poem: 麻薬うてば十三夜月遁走す
Romaji:
mayaku uteba 
jūsanya-zuki 
tonsōsu
My translation:
As the drug takes hold, 
the moon of the thirteenth night
scampers away from me.
Kigo: 十三夜 【じゅうさんや】 jūsanya, thirteenth night moon (mid autumn).
Notes: Injected with narcotics; the thirteenth-night moon flees—hallucinatory beauty.

Poem: 春嵐屍は敢えて出でゆくも
Romaji:
haru arashi 
kabane wa aete 
ide yuku mo
My translation:
Spring storm— 
a corpse courageously 
leaves the hospital.
Kigo: 春嵐 【はるあらし】 haruarashi, spring storm (all spring).
Notes: In the spring storm, even a corpse dares to emerge—desperate vitality.

Poem: 力なく降る雪なればなぐさまず
Romaji:
chikara naku 
furu yuki nareba 
nagusamazu
My translation:
So languidly 
snowflakes fall, offering no 
consolation to me.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: Snow falling without force—no consolation in its weakness.

Poem: 雪はしづかにゆたかのはやし屍室
Romaji:
yuki wa shizukani 
yutakani hayashi 
kabaneshitsu
My translation:
It snows quietly, 
abundantly, and fast— 
a mortuary.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: 屍室 (shikabane shitsu) = morgue. Snow quiet and rich in the morgue.

Poem: 泉への道後れゆく安けさよ
Romaji:
izumi e no 
michi okure yuku 
yasukesa yo
My translation:
On the way towards 
the fountain I lag behind, 
and how calm I feel!
Kigo: 泉 【いずみ】 izumi, spring / fountain (all summer).
Notes: Falling behind on the path to the spring—ease in being last.

Poem: 百千の土管口あけ雪降れり
Romaji:
hyaku sen no 
dokan kuchi ake 
yuki fureri
My translation:
Hundreds and thousands 
of earthen pipes, with their mouths 
open, the snow falls.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: Snow falling into thousands of open pipe mouths—surreal geometry of winter.

Poem: 起ち上らざるもの胸に萩起す
Romaji:
tachiagarazaru 
mono mune ni 
hagi okosu
My translation:
With something in my heart 
that will not stand up, I help 
the bush clover to stand up.
Kigo: 萩 【はぎ】 hagi, bush clover (mid autumn).
Notes: Something in the chest that cannot rise—bush clover raised to meet it.

Poem: 白き手の病者ばかり落葉焚
Romaji:
shiroki te no
byōsha bakari
ochiba-taki
My translation:
all whites hands of
ill patiants 
above the pile of burning leaves
Kigo: 落葉焚
Notes: writen after the auther had surgery for tuberculosis

Poem: 春分の日なり雨なり草の上
Romaji:
shunbun no
hi nari ame nari
kusa no ue
My translation:
the vernal equinox
some sun, some rain
over the grass
Kigo:
Vernal equinox
春分 shunbun

Poem: 人体冷えて東北白い花盛り
Romaji:
jintai hiete 
touhoku shiroi 
Hanazakari
My translation:
my body feels the chill
Tohoku covered in white
masses of flowers
Kigo: 花盛り 【はなざかり】 hanazakari, flowers in full bloom (mid spring).
Notes: The human body cold; in the Tōhoku region, white flowers in full bloom—post-war alienation.
Other translation:
my body feels the chill
Tohoku covered in white　Dhugal J.Lindsay
masses of flowers

Poem: 蛾のまなこ赤光なれば海を戀う
Romaji:
ga-no manako 
sekkou nareba 
umi-o kou
My translation:
the moth's eyes
glow red, yes the ocean
is the place for me
Kigo: 蛾 【が】 ga, moth (all summer).
Notes: A moth's red-lit eye yearning for the sea.
Other translation:
the moth's eyes
glow red, yes the ocean
is the place for me

Poem: 彎曲し火傷し爆心地のマラソン
Romaji:
wankyoku shi 
yakedo shi bakushinchi-no 
marason
My translation:
over the once twisted 
and charred ground zero
a marathon
Kigo: 炎熱 【えんねつ】 ennetsu, scorching heat (all summer).
Notes: Bent, burned, a marathon runner at the hypocenter—atomic bomb poem.
Other translation:
urned into a curve
turned into a blackened scar
hypocentre marathon

Poem: 梅咲いて庭中に青鮫が来ている
Romaji:
ume saite 
niwajuh-ni aozame-ga 
kite iru
My translation:
the plum in bloom
blue sharks have come right in
into the garden
Kigo: 梅 【うめ】 ume, （sometimes むめ mume）, plum (blossoms) [technically, the "Japanese apricot", Prunus mume; but this has almost always been translated "plum" for literary purposes] (early spring).
Notes: Plum blooming; a blue shark in the garden—surrealist intrusion of the oceanic.
Other translation:
the plum in bloom
blue sharks have come right in
into the garden

Poem: おおかみに螢が一つ付いていた
Romaji:
ookami-ni 
hotaru-ga hitotsu 
tsuite ita
My translation:
on the wolf
a firefly
attached itself
Kigo: 蛍 【ほたる】 hotaru, firefly (mid summer).
Notes: A wolf with one firefly attached—the predator and the small light.
Other translation:
on the wolf
a firefly
attached itself

Poem: 手が長くだるし赤茶けた製鋼煙
Romaji:
te ga nagaku 
darushi akachaketa
seikōen
My translation:
Like an arm overstretched
and tired, reddish brow smoke
rising from a steel mill.
Kigo: 製鋼煙 【せいこうけむり】 seikō kemuri, steelworks smoke.
Notes: Long slack hands; reddish-brown steelworks smoke—industrial exhaustion.

Poem: なめくじり寂光を負ひ鶏のそば
Romaji:
namekujiri 
jakkō wo oi
tori no soba
My translation:
A slug
bathed in an ethereal glow
near a chicken
Kigo: なめくじり namekujiri, slug (all summer).
Notes: A slug bearing the light of nirvana beside the chicken.
Other translation: Ueda

Poem: 中学生神語りおり雪積む藁
Romaji:
chūgakusei 
kami katari ori 
yuki tsumu wara
My translation:
High school boys
are talking of God, while the snow
keeps piling up on the ricks.
Kigo: 雪 【ゆき】 yuki, snow (all winter).
Notes: A student talks of God; snow accumulates on straw.
Other translation: Ueda

Poem: 死にし骨は海に捨つべし沢庵嚙む
Romaji:
shinishi hone wa
umi ni sutsu beshi
takuan kamu
My translation:
Dead bones
must be dumped into the sea!
I chew a piece of takuan.
Kigo: 沢庵 【たくあん】 takuan, pickled daikon (all winter).
Notes: Eating pickled daikon; the dead should be thrown to the sea—blunt mortality.

Poem: 墓地も焼跡蝉肉片のごと樹々に
Romaji:
bochi mo
yakeato semi nikuhen no 
goto kigi ni
My translation:
The graveyard is burnt too:
cicadas, like pieces of fleash
on the trees.
Kigo: 蝉 【せみ】 semi, cicada (late summer).
Notes: Cicadas like flesh-pieces on the trees; graveyard and bomb-site.
Other translation:
The graveyard is burnt too:
cicadas, like pieces of fleash
on the trees. Ueda

Poem: 崩れ煉瓦に蝶執着すここスラム
Romaji:
kuzure renga ni
chō shūjakisu
koko suramu
My translation:
Above the crumbled brick
a butterfly, its heart attached
here to the slums.
Kigo: 蝶 【ちょう】 chō, （てふ）, butterfly [the spring butterfly image is typically a cabbage white, white members of the family Pieridae; see also "summer butterfly", etc.] (all spring).
Notes: A butterfly obsessively clinging to rubble in a slum.
Other translation:
Above the crumbled brick
a butterfly, its heart attached
here to the slums. Ueda

Poem: 山には枯畑谷には思惟なくただ澄む水
Romaji:
yama ni wa
karehata tani niwa shii naku 
tada sumu mizu
Kigo: 澄む水 【すむみず】 sumu mizu, clear water (all summer).
Notes: Mountain: withered fields. Valley: clear, thoughtless water.

Poem: 奴隷の自由という語寒卵皿に澄み
Romaji:
dorei-no 
jiyū to iu go kantamago
sara ni sumi
My translation:
A slave's freedom' –so says
the phrase: an egg in midwinter
serene on the plate.
Kigo: 寒卵 【かんたまご】 kan-tamago, winter egg (all winter).
Notes: Slave freedom as empty language; a cold egg clear on a plate.

Poem: 異質のごと新しき松かさ草に正座
Romaji:
ishitsu no goto 
atarashiki matsukasa
kusa ni seiza
My translation:
Like something totally
alien, a fresh pine cone
sits upright on the grass.
Kigo: 松かさ 【まつかさ】 matsukasa, pine cone (all autumn).
Notes: A new pine cone in the grass, sitting formally—as if alien to its surroundings.

Poem: 蜉蝣むらがる橋燈に来て影を得る
Romaji:
kagerō muragaru
kyōtō ni kite
kage wo uru
My translation:
Ephemerae swarming
At a bridge lamp— I arrive
And gain a shadow.
Kigo: 蜉蝣 【かげろう】 kagerō, mayfly (all summer).
Notes: Mayflies clustering around the bridge lamp; finally gaining a shadow.

Poem: あまたの街角街娼争い蜜柑乾く
Romaji:
amata no machikado 
gaishō arasoi 
mikan kawaku
My translation:
Factory dismissing the workers—
it vomits cloudy autumn water
into the canal.
Kigo: 蜜柑 【みかん】 mikan, mikan / mandarin orange [fruit of the Citrus reticulata] (all winter).
Notes: At many street corners, prostitutes fight; a mandarin dries out.

Poem: 群に入る目高素早く幸福に
Romaji:
mure ni iru
medaka subayaku
kōfuku ni
My translation:
It joins a group—
a killfish, swiftly
and happily.
Kigo: 目高 【めだか】 medaka, killifish (all summer).
Notes: A killifish darting into the school—quick happiness.

Poem: 平和おそれるや夏の石石炭蓆かぶり
Romaji:
heiwa osoreru ya
natsu no sekitan
mushiro kaburi
My translation:
Is it afraid
Of peace? Coal in summertime
Covered with straw mats.
Kigo: 夏 【なつ】 natsu, summer.
Notes: Fearing peace; summer stones in a coal basket.

Poem: 首切る工場秋雲の水を運河に吐き
Romaji:
kubi kiru kōba
shūdon no mizu wo
unga ni haki
My translation:
Factory dismissing the workers—
it vomits cloudy autumn water
into the canal.
Kigo: 秋雲 【あきぐも】 akigumo, autumn clouds (all autumn).
Notes: A factory spitting water into a canal under autumn clouds.

Poem: 白い人影はるばる田をゆく消えぬために
Romaji:
shiroi hitokage 
harubaru ta wo yuku
kienu tame ni
My translation:
A white human figure
far, far away, walks on the farm
in order not to fade.
Kigo: 白き人影 【しろきひとかげ】 shiroki hitokage, white human figure (summer).
Notes: A white figure moving far away across the fields—not to disappear.

Poem: ガット下にはりつく反吐が冬の華
Romaji:
gādo shita ni
haritsuku hedo ga
fuyu no hana
My translation:
Under the girders of the bridge
vomit is stuck, blooming
as winter's blossoms.
Kigo: 冬 【ふゆ】 fuyu, winter.
Notes: Clinging to the gut beneath—the winter's flower.

Poem: 激論つくし街ゆきオートバイと化す
Romaji:
gekiron 
tsukushi machi yuki 
ōtobai to kasu
My translation:
After a heated argument
I go out to the street 
and become a motorcycle.
Kigo: オートバイ ōtobai, motorcycle.
Notes: After fierce debate, transforming into a motorcycle in the street.

Poem: どれも口美し晩夏のジャズ一団
Romaji:
dore mo kuchi 
utsukushi banka no
jazu ichidan
My translation:
Every one of the mouths
is beautiful—late in summer
a jazz group.
Kigo: 晩夏 【ばんか】 banka, late summer (late summer).
Notes: Every mouth beautiful in a late-summer jazz band.

Poem: 銀行員等朝より螢光す烏賊のごとく
Romaji:
ginkoin-ra 
asa yori keikō su 
ika no-gotoku
My translation:
bank clerks
from the morning glowing
fluorescent as squid
Kigo: 螢光 【けいこう】 keikō, fluorescent light (summer).
Notes: Bank employees fluorescent since morning like squid—sardonic image of white-collar labor.

Poem: 強し青年干潟に玉葱腐る日も
Romaji:
tsuyoshi seinen
higata ni tamanegi
kusaru hi mo
My translation:
Strong are the youngsters
even on a day when onions
rot at the dry beach
Kigo: 玉葱腐る 【たまねぎくさる】 tamanegi kusaru, onion rotting (summer).
Notes: A strong young man; onions rotting on the tidal flat—youth and decay.

Poem: 鉛筆の遺書ならば忘れ易からむ
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: 鉛筆の遺書 (enpitsu no isho) = a pencil suicide note. A pencil note is easily forgotten — dark, laconic.

Poem: 黄の青の赤の雨傘誰から死ぬ
Kigo: 雨傘 【あまがさ】 amagasa, umbrella (rainy season/spring).
Notes: Yellow, blue, red umbrellas — who dies first?

Poem: ピアノは音のくらがり髪に星を沈め
Kigo: (no fixed kigo — jiyūritsu/free verse)
Notes: ピアノは音のくらがり (piano wa oto no kuragari) = the piano is a darkness of sound. The piano as dark abyss of sound; stars sink into hair.

Poem: 春の雪誰かに電話したくなり
Romaji:
haru no yuki
dare ka ni denwa 
Shitakunari
My translation:
spring snow
makes me want to
call someone
Kigo: 春の雪 【はるのゆき】 haru no yuki, spring snow (early spring).
Notes: Spring snow; the sudden urge to call someone.

Poem: うちの子でない子がいてる昼寝覚め
Romaji:
uchi no ko 
denai ko ga iteru
Hironezame
My translation:
waking from a nap
there is a kid
not from our family
Kigo: 昼寝 【ひるね】 hirune, midday nap / siesta (all summer).
Notes: Waking from a nap to find an unfamiliar child—quiet uncanny.

Poem: 矢車の音に角力の初日かな
Romaji:
yaguruma no
oto ni kakuryoku no
hatsuhi kana
My translation:
to the sound of 
an arrow cart, amateur sumo
first day:
Kigo: 矢車 【やぐるま】 yaguruma, arrow-wheel / pinwheel (New Year).
Notes: Pinwheel sound; sumo's opening day—New Year festivity.

Poem: 春分のおどけ雀と目覚めけり
Romaji:
shunbun no
odoke suzume to
me-zame keri
My translation:
awakening with
the comical sparrows
of the vernal equinox
Kigo:
Vernal equinox
春分 shunbun

Poem: 顔泛けるごと春分の京にをり
Romaji:
kao ukeru
goto shunbun no
kyo ni ori
My translation:
flitting across every 
face, vernal equinox
in Kyoto
Kigo:
Vernal equinox
春分 shunbun

Poem: 臍の緒を家のどこかに春惜しむ
Kigo: 春惜しむ 【はるおしむ】 haru oshimu, lamenting the passing of spring (late spring).
Notes: 臍の緒 (heso no o) = umbilical cord. The umbilical cord kept somewhere in the house—spring passing, attachment to origin.

Poem: 白葱のひかりの棒をいま刻む
Romaji:
shironegi no
hikari no bō wo
ima kizamu
My translation:
the glow of
the long white onion
marks this moment
Kigo: 白葱 【しろねぎ】 shironegi, white leek (all winter).
Notes: 光の棒をいま刻む (hikari no bō wo ima kizamu) = now cutting a rod of light. The white leek—a rod of light being cut now.

Poem: 薔薇咲くや生涯に割る皿の数
Romaji:
bara saku ya
shōgai ni waru
sara no kazu
My translation:
roses bloom
the number of plates
broken over a lifetime
Kigo: 薔薇 【ばら】 bara, rose (summer).
Notes: Roses blooming; how many plates will a life break.

Poem: 九官鳥同士は無口うららけし
Romaji:
kyūkanchō
dōshi wa muguchi
Urarakeshi
My translation:
myna  birds have 
nothing to say to each other
in the bright spring
Kigo: 麗か 【うららか】 uraraka, bright (and clear) / splendid [of weather] (all spring).

Poem: 人間の智慧ゆらゆらと誘蛾燈
Romaji:
ningen no
chie yurayura to
yūgatō
My translation:
Man's wisdom
flickers, flickers—
a light trap.
Kigo: 誘蛾燈 【ゆうがとう】 yūgatō, （いうがとう）, insect light-trap / moth lantern (late summer).
Notes: Human wisdom swaying in the moth-trap light.

Poem: 肉白き病体に世もかすみたる
Romaji:
niku shiroki 
byōtai ni yo mo 
kasumitaru
Kigo: 霞 【かすみ】 kasumi, (spring) mist [frequently translated "haze"; see note "On Haze, Mist, Fog"] (all spring).
Notes: The white body ill; the world seen through spring mist—dissolution.
Other translation:
flesh white
in my sick body too
the world is misty (UVA)

Poem: 春の山重りゆきて富士となる
Romaji:
haru no yama
kasanari yukite
fuji to naru
My translation:
spring mountains
piled one on the other
then Mt. Fuji
Kigo: Spring mountain

Poem: 馬借りてかはるがはるに霞みけり
Romaji:
uma karite 
kawarugawaru ni 
kasumikeri
Kigo: mist
Notes: Passing through the mist on a borrowed horse in turn.
Other translation:
taking turns
on a borrowed horse
mist-shrouded  (UVA)

Poem: 口あけて顔のなくなる燕の子
Romaji:
kuchi akete
kao no nakunaru
suzume no ko
My translation:
swallow chicks
their faces disappear
when they open their beaks
Kigo: 燕の子 【つばめのこ】 tsubame no ko, baby swallow (all summer).
Notes: A baby swallow opening its beak—its face gone, all mouth.

Poem: ハイヒール山に突き刺し夏に入る
Romaji:
haihiiru
yama ni tsukisashi
natsu ni hairu
My translation:
high heels 
jab into the mountain
entering summer
Kigo: 夏に入る 【なつにいる】 natsu ni iru, entering summer (early summer).
Notes: High heels plunged into the mountain, entering summer.

Poem: 夏浅きまだ水張らず湖畔の田
Romaji:
natsu asashi
mada mizu harazu
kohan no ta
My translation:
shallow summer
not yet watered
lakeside rice patty
Kigo:
Shallow summer
夏浅し natsu asashi

Poem: 昨日漉きし紙春分の日を過ごす
Romaji:
kino sukishi
kami shunbun no
hi wo sugosu
My translation:
passing the day
of the vernal equinox with 
paper made yesterday
Kigo:
Vernal equinox
春分 shunbun

Poem: 夏浅き草花店や種も売る
Romaji:
natsu asaki
kusa-bana mise ya
tane mo uru
My translation:
the arboretum
in shallow summerー
seed are also for sale
Kigo: 夏浅し natsu asashi

Poem: 初夏のこの森に蝶のおびただし
Romaji:
shoka no kono
mori ni cho no
obitadashi
My translation:
early summer
in these woods butterflies
are abundant
Kigo: 初夏 shoka

Poem: 我とともに老いたる牛や麦の秋
Romaji:
ware to tomo ni
oi taru ushi ya
mugi no aki
My translation:
togeather with me
this ox has grown old-
wheat's autumn
Kigo: 麦の秋 mugi no aki

Poem: 夏の日や薄苔つける木々の枝
Romaji:
natsu no hi ya
usu-goke tsukeru
kigi no eda
My translation:
summer daysー
tree boughs covered
with a thin layer of moss
Kigo: 夏の日　natsu no hi

Poem: 夏の日を或る児は泣いてばかりかな
Romaji:
natsu no hi wo
aru ko wa naite
bakari kana
My translation:
one a summer day
a child cries
incessantly:
Kigo: 夏の日　natsu no hi

Poem: 堅きまで乾きしタオル夏日にほふ
Romaji:
kataki made
kawakishi taoru
natsu-bi niou
My translation:
so dried they stiffen
towels
fragrant with the summer sun
Kigo: 夏の日　natsu no hi

Poem: 夏の夜の湖白し松の間
Romaji:
natsu no yo no
mizuumi shiroshi
matsu no ai
My translation:
summer night
the lake is white
between the pines
Kigo: 夏の夜 natsu no yo

Poem: 月の輪をゆり去る舟や夜半の夏
Romaji:
tsuki no wa wo
yuri saru fune ya
yowa no natsu
My translation:
from the moon’s corona
the boat drifts awayー
summer midnight
Kigo: 夏の夜 natsu no yo

Poem: みじか夜の浮藻うごかす小蝦かな
Romaji:
mijika yo no
uki mo ugokasu
ko ebi kana
My translation:
a short night
floating duckweed stirs
a small shrimp.
Kigo: 短夜 mijika yo

Poem: 明けやすき欅にしるす生死かな
Romaji:
ake yasiki
keyaki ni shirusu
shoji kana
My translation:
quick to dawn
on a zelkova tree marked
life and death
This poem was written in 1940 after an American air raid on Tokyo.  The poet's house and the surrounding neighborhood were completely demolished, so the poet carved a message in the tree to tell anyone who might come looking for him before seeking shelter.
Kigo: 短夜 mijika yo

Poem: 鹿の子の人慕ひ来てためらへり
Romaji:
Shika no ko no
hito shitai kite
tamerae ri
My translation:
A fawn
came following a man,
and hesitated.
Kigo: 鹿の子 Kanoko — Fawn [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 芽楓の雨をさむがる鹿の子かな
Romaji:
Me kaede no
ame wo samugaru
kanoko kana
My translation:
A budding maple’s
rain makes the fawn
shiver.
Kigo: 鹿の子 Kanoko — Fawn [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 苑日々に草深うなる鹿の子かな
Romaji:
Sono hibi ni
kusa fuko naru
kanoko kana
My translation:
The park each day
deeper in grasses,
fawns.
Kigo: 鹿の子 Kanoko — Fawn [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 金の月へ遠き蝙蝠とんで消ゆ
Romaji:
Kin no tsuki e
toki komori
tonde kiyu
My translation:
All the way to
a golden moon, the bat
flew and faded.
Kigo: 蝙蝠 Komori — Bat [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 河鹿鳴いて石ころ多き小川かな
Romaji:
Kajika naite
ishikoro oki
ogawa kana
My translation:
River frogs sing —
a many-pebbled
little brook.
Kigo: 河鹿 Kajika — River Frog [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 眦を波にしづめし河鹿かな
Romaji:
Manajiri wo
nami ni shizumeshi
kajika kana
My translation:
The tail of its eye
sunk under a wave,
river frog.
Kigo: 河鹿 Kajika — River Frog [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 河鹿の声の水を流るる昼餉かな
Romaji:
Kajika no koe no
mizu wo nagaruru
hiruge kana
My translation:
Where river frog
voices flow over the water,
eat lunch.
Kigo: 河鹿 Kajika — River Frog [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 河鹿鳴く我一塊の岩となり
Romaji:
Kajika naku
ware ikkon no
iwa to nari
My translation:
A river frog cries —
and I turn into
a boulder.
Kigo: 河鹿 Kajika — River Frog [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 老鶯や青嶺折々雲の上
Romaji:
Ro-o ya
seirei oriori
kumo no ue
My translation:
An old warbler —
green peaks sometimes appear
above the clouds.
Kigo: 老鶯 Oi uguisu — Old Bush Warbler [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 老鶯や珠のごとくに一湖あり
Romaji:
Ro-o ya
tama no gotoku ni
ikke ari
My translation:
An old warbler —
and a lake there,
like a jewel.
Kigo: 老鶯 Oi uguisu — Old Bush Warbler [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 老鶯や出湯のあまりが谷に落つ
Romaji:
Ro-o ya
deyu no amari ga
tani ni otsu
My translation:
Old warbler —
the excess of the hot spring
falls into valley.
Kigo: 老鶯 Oi uguisu — Old Bush Warbler [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 芦原の中に家あり行々子
Romaji:
Ashihara no
naka ni ie ari
gyogyoshi
My translation:
In the middle
of a reed plain, a house —
reed warblers.
Kigo: 葦切 Yoshikiri — Reed Warbler [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 信濃川は分流多し行々子
Romaji:
Shinanogawa wa
bunryu oshi
gyogyoshi
My translation:
Shinano river
has many tributaries —
reed warblers.
Kigo: 葦切 Yoshikiri — Reed Warbler [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 葦切のをちの鋭声朝曇り
Romaji:
Yoshikiri no
ochi no eisei
asa gumori
My translation:
A reed warbler’s
distant, shrill voice —
morning cloudiness.
Kigo: 葦切 Yoshikiri — Reed Warbler [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 翡翠とぶその四五秒の天地かな
Romaji:
Hisui tobu
sono shigo byo no
tenchi kana
My translation:
A kingfisher flies —
those four, five seconds
of a world.
Kigo: 翡翠 Kawasemi — Kingfisher [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 山の色釣りあげし鮎に動くかな
Romaji:
Yama no iro
tsuri ageshi ayu ni
ugoku kana
My translation:
The mountain’s colour
on the hooked ayu
moves.
Kigo: 鮎 Ayu — Sweet-Fish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 鮎釣の腰を真白に水たぎつ
Romaji:
Ayutsuri no
koshi wo mashiro ni
mizu tagitsu
My translation:
On the ayu fisherman’s
hips, pure white
water foams.
Kigo: 鮎 Ayu — Sweet-Fish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 上流は曲りて見えず鮎の川
Romaji:
Joryu wa
magarite miezu
ayu no kawa
My translation:
Upstream, with the bend, not in sight —
ayu river.
Kigo: 鮎 Ayu — Sweet-Fish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 底を行く金魚に動く真砂かな
Romaji:
Soko wo yuku
kingyo ni ugoku
masago kana
My translation:
Going along the bottom,
the goldfish stirs
the white sand.
Kigo: 金魚 Kingyo — Goldfish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 生涯の今の心や金魚見る
Romaji:
Shogai no
ima no kokoro ya
kingyo miru
Kigo: 金魚 Kingyo — Goldfish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 女たちおしゃべり金魚浮き沈み
Romaji:
Onna tachi
oshaberi kingyo
uki shizumi
My translation:
The ladies
prattle, goldfish
float and sink.
Kigo: 金魚 Kingyo — Goldfish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: しだり尾の錦ぞ動く金魚かな
Romaji:
Shidari o no
nishiki zo ugoku
kingyo kana
My translation:
The drooping
tail’s brocade moves —
goldfish.
Kigo: 金魚 Kingyo — Goldfish [Summer Dobutsu]

Poem: 滝落ちて群青世界とどろけり
Romaji:
Taki ochite gunjo sekai
todorokeri
My translation: The waterfall flows —
Kigo: 滝 Taki
Notes:
a dark-green world
vibrates
At Nachi waterfall; gunjo is one of the basic colours in Japanese painting. The dark green world is that of the cedar trees that surround the falls.

Poem: 滝の上に水現われて落ちにけり
Romaji:
Taki no ue ni
mizu arawarete
ochi ni keri
My translation: Over the waterfall
Kigo: 滝 Taki
Notes:
the water appears
then falls.

Poem: 半ばより煙の如く滝落つる
Romaji:
Nakaba yori
kemuri no gotoku
taki otsuru
My translation: Half-way down,
Kigo: 滝 Taki
Notes:
like smoke —
the waterfall falls.

Poem: 夏山の大木倒す谺かな
Romaji:
Natsu yama no
taiboku taosu
kodama kana
My translation:
Summer mountain —
a huge tree being felled,
the echoes.
Kigo: 夏の山 Natsu no yama — Summer Mountain [Summer Kigo]

Poem: 夏山の樵たのもしく思はずや
Romaji:
Natsu yama no
kikori tanomoshiku
omowazu ya
My translation:
A summer mountain’s
lumberjack — lucky,
don’t you think?
Kigo: 夏の山 Natsu no yama — Summer Mountain [Summer Kigo]

Poem: 青野ゆき馬は片眼に人を見る
Romaji:
Ao no yuki
uma wa kata me ni
hito wo miru
My translation:
