Going the green field,
the horse with one eye
looks at you.
Kigo: 夏野  Natsuno  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 汽車一刻青野より乗り青野に降る
Romaji:
Kisha ikkoku
ao no yori nori
ao no ni oriru
My translation:
Short train ride —
I got on in green fields,
off to green fields.
Kigo: 夏野  Natsuno  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 朝霞の小松はなれし夏野かな
Romaji:
Asa moya no
komatsu hanareshi
natsu no kana
My translation:
The morning haze
has left the little pines,
summer fields.
Kigo: 夏野  Natsuno  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 夏川の美しき村又訪はん
Romaji:
Natsu gawa no
utsukushiki mura
mata towan
My translation:
A village with
a beautiful summer river —
must come again.
Kigo: 夏の川  Natsu no kawa  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 刻々と真珠は育つ夏の海
Romaji:
Kokokuhuto
shinju wa sodatsu
natsu no umi
My translation:
Each moment
the pearls grow —
summer ocean.
Kigo: 夏の海  Natsu no umi  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 夏浪を桶にす尚も揺よこぼるる
Romaji:
Natsu nami wo
oke ni su nao mo
yure koboruru
My translation:
Summer waves
scooped in a bucket, still
sway and spill.
Kigo: 夏の海  Natsu no umi  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 夕風の鷺吹き飛ばす青田かな
Romaji:
Yukage no
sagi fukitobasu
aota kana
My translation:
The dusk wind
sends herons flying,
green ricefields.
Kigo: 青田  Aota  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 広き葉のかさなり映る泉かな
Romaji:
Hiroki ha no
kasanari utsuru
izumi kana
My translation:
Broad leaves
reflect in layers —
a spring.
Kigo: 泉  Izumi  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 其底に木葉散ふる清水かな
Romaji:
Sono soko ni
konoha toshifuru
shimizu kana
My translation:
At the bottom,
tree leaves spend the years —
pure water.
Kigo: 清水  Shimizu  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 五月富士水車は高き水玉を
Romaji:
Satsuki Fuji
suisha wa takaki
mizudama wo
My translation:
Fifth month Fuji —
the water-wheel throws up
its sprays.
Kigo: 五月富士  Satsuki Fuji  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 展望の一舟一鷹五月富士
Romaji:
Tenbo no
isshu ichien
satsuki Fuji
My translation:
From the look-out,
one boat, one black kite —
Fifth month Fuji.
Kigo: 五月富士  Satsuki Fuji  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 立つ鷺にあらわれてをり五月富士
Romaji:
Tatsu sagi ni
arawarete ori
Satsuki Fuji
My translation:
By a standing heron
appeared —
Fifth month Fuji.
Kigo: 五月富士  Satsuki Fuji  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 大雨に濁りかへせし植田哉
Romaji:
Oame ni
nigori kaeseshi
ueta kana
My translation:
With a downpour
their muddiness returned,
planted ricefields.
Kigo: 植田  Ueta  [Summer / Chiri]

Poem: 更衣爪はするどき山の鳥
Romaji:
Koromogae
tsume wa surudoki
yama no tori
My translation:
Change of garments —
their claws are sharp,
the mountain bird.
Kigo: 更衣  Koromogae  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 人にややおくれて衣更へにけり
Romaji:
Hito ni yaya
okurete koromo
kae ni keri
My translation:
Somewhat later
than others, I changed
my garments.
Kigo: 更衣  Koromogae  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 羅をゆるやかに着て崩れざる
Romaji:
Usumono wo
yuruyaka ni kite
kuzurezaru
My translation:
A thin silk
kimono worn casually,
her propriety.
Kigo: 羅  Usumono  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 羅に汗さへ見せぬ女かな
Romaji:
Usumono ni
ase sao misenu
onna kana
My translation:
In thin silk
no sign of sweat
does the woman show.
Kigo: 羅  Usumono  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 爽かな汗へ上着る浴衣かな
Romaji:
Sawayakana
ase no ue kiru
yukata kana
My translation:
On fresh sweat,
put on
a yukata.
Kigo: 浴衣  Yukata  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 月影のふところにさす浴衣かな
Romaji:
Tsukikage no
futokoro ni sasu
yukata kana
My translation:
Moonlight
falls on the chest —
yukata.
Kigo: 浴衣  Yukata  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 雑巾となるまではわが浴衣
Romaji:
Zokin to naru made wa waga
furu yukata
My translation:
Till it's reduced
to a floor rag, my
old yukata.
Kigo: 浴衣  Yukata  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 浴衣あたらしく夜の川漕ぎくだる
Romaji:
Yukata atarashiku
yoru no kawa
kogi kudaru
My translation:
New yukatas —
going down
the night river.
Kigo: 浴衣  Yukata  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 夏帽や今年銀座に柳無し
Romaji:
Natsuba ya
kotoshi Ginza ni
yanagi nashi
My translation:
Summer hats —
this year on the Ginza,
no willows.
Kigo: 夏帽子  Natsuboshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 夏帽の日を照り返す渚かな
Romaji:
Natsubo no
hi wo teri kaesu
nagisa kana
My translation:
Summer hats —
on a strand that
reflects the sun.
Kigo: 夏帽子  Natsuboshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 麦藁帽たたよふ海の紺のなか
Romaji:
Mugiwarabo
tadayou umi no
kon no naka
My translation:
A wheat straw hat
floats, on the ocean's
deep blue.
Kigo: 夏帽子  Natsuboshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: カンカン帽ゆゑに目に立つ頬骨なる
Romaji:
Kankambo
yue ni me ni tatsu
hobone naru
My translation:
A hard straw hat —
and so, prominent,
the cheek bones.
Kigo: 夏帽子  Natsuboshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 匙なめて童たのしも夏氷
Romaji:
Saji namete
warabe tanoshi mo
natsu gori
My translation:
Licking their spoons,
happy children!
summer ice.
Kigo: 氷水  Korimizu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 日焼顔見合ひてうまし氷水
Romaji:
Hiyakegao
miaite umashi
kori mizu
My translation:
Sunburnt faces
across the table, delicious!
shaved ice.
Kigo: 氷水  Korimizu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 水捨る音の夜深し氷店
Romaji:
Mizu suteru
oto no yo fukashi
kori mise
My translation:
The sound of water
being thrown out, late at night —
ice shop.
Kigo: 氷水  Korimizu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 氷店より見てゐたる人通り
Romaji:
Kori mise
yori mite itaru
hito dori
My translation:
From the ice shop,
I watch the people
passing by.
Kigo: 氷水  Korimizu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 船のぞく望遠鏡おく夏座敷
Romaji:
Fune nozoku
tomigane oku
natsu zashiki
My translation:
To look at boats
a telescope placed —
summer parlour.
Kigo: 夏座敷  Natsuzashiki  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 松風や池の月見るたかむしろ
Romaji:
Matsu kaze ya
ike no tsuki miru
takamushiro
My translation:
A pine-tree wind —
look at the pond's moon,
from a bamboo mat.
Kigo: 簟  Takamushiro  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 転寝の目に横雲や簟
Romaji:
Utatane no
me ni yokogumo ya
takamushiro
My translation:
In the dozing
eyes, a bank of clouds —
bamboo mat.
Kigo: 簟  Takamushiro  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 二つ吊し簾の透間花柘榴
Romaji:
Futatsu tsuri shi
sudare no sukima
hana zakuro
My translation:
Two blinds hung up,
and from between them,
pomegranate flowers.
Kigo: 簾  Sudare  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 簾おろし天の橋立うすくなる
Romaji:
Sudare oroshi
Ama no Hashidate
usuku naru
My translation:
The blinds rolled down,
Ama no Hashidate
became faint.
Ama no Hashidate: one of the 3 most scenic landscapes of Japan, in Tango north of Kyoto. It is a thin strip of land covered with pine trees, that projects into the bay.
Kigo: 簾  Sudare  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 世の中を美しと見し簾かな
Romaji:
Yo no naka wo
utsukushito mishi
sudare kana
My translation:
This world
looked beautiful,
through the blinds.
Kigo: 簾  Sudare  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 青簾むかしむかしのはなしかな
Romaji:
Ao sudare
mukashi mukashi no
hanashi kana
My translation:
Green blinds —
talk of long,
long ago.
Kigo: 簾  Sudare  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 鏡にも手のあと白し天瓜粉
Romaji:
Kagami ni mo
te no ato shiroshi
tenkafun
Kigo: 天瓜粉  Tenkafun  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 小さき子人形にうち粉天瓜粉
Romaji:
Chiisaki ko
ningyo ni uchimu
tenkafun
My translation:
Little child,
she put some on her doll,
talcum powder.
Kigo: 天瓜粉  Tenkafun  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: みめよくてにくらしき子や天瓜粉
Romaji:
Mime yokute
nikurashiki ko ya
tenkafun
My translation:
Nice looking,
but a detestable child!
Talcum powder.
Kigo: 天瓜粉  Tenkafun  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 天瓜粉月下の風にはげにけり
Romaji:
Tenkafun
gekka no kaze ni
hage ni keri
Kigo: 天瓜粉  Tenkafun  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 月影の蚊帳にひらめく団扇かな
Romaji:
Tsukikage no
kaya ni hirameku
uchiwa kana
My translation:
Moonlight
flutters in the mosquito net,
a round fan.
Kigo: 団扇  Uchiwa  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 風鈴に何処へも行かず暑しけり
Romaji:
Furin ni
doko e mo yukazu
kuwashi keri
My translation:
By a windbell,
without going out,
I spent the day.
Kigo: 風鈴  Furin  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 月さして風鈴の影生いけり
Romaji:
Tsuki sashite
furin no kage
umare keri
My translation:
The moon shone,
a windbell's shadow
was born.
Kigo: 風鈴  Furin  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 風鈴や水面に残る風のあと
Romaji:
Furin ya
minamo ni nokoru
kaze no ato
My translation:
A windbell —
on the water surface,
a trace of the wind.
Kigo: 風鈴  Furin  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 走馬灯はじめなければ終りなし
Romaji:
Somato
hajime nakereba
owari nashi
My translation:
Revolving lamp —
without a beginning
or end.
Kigo: 走馬灯  Somato  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 先の影後の影追ふ走馬灯
Romaji:
Saki no kage
ato no kage ou
somato
My translation:
The shadow in front
chases the shadow behind,
revolving lamp.
Kigo: 走馬灯  Somato  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 影を売るごと走馬灯売る男
Romaji:
Kage wo uru
goto somato
uru otoko
My translation:
Like selling shadows,
the man who sells
revolving lamps.
Kigo: 走馬灯  Somato  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 虫干や蔵の虫入に松の風
Romaji:
Mushi boshi ya
kura no deiri ni
matsu no kaze
My translation:
Insect airing —
going in and out the storehouse,
a pine-tree wind.
Kigo: 虫干  Mushiboshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 幕張て能の衣裳や土用干
Romaji:
Maku shatte
no no isho ya
doyo boshi
My translation:
A curtain put up,
Noh garments —
being aired.
Kigo: 虫干  Mushiboshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 田を植ゑししづかな音へ出でにけり
Romaji:
Ta wo ueshi
shizukana oto e
ide ni keri
My translation:
To the quiet
sounds of planting rice,
I went out.
Kigo: 田植  Taue  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 草刈女霞がのびきてつつみけり
Romaji:
Kusa kari me
moya ga nobikite
tsutsumi keri
My translation:
Grass cutter —
the haze reached and
enclosed her.
Kigo: 草刈  Kusa kari  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 草刈や日出でぬ間を刈り急ぐ
Romaji:
Kusa kari ya
hi idenu aida wo
kari isagu
My translation:
Grass-cutting —
hurry, before the sun
comes out!
Kigo: 草刈  Kusa kari  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 草刈るや萩に沈める紺法被
Romaji:
Kusa karu ya
hagi ni shizumeru
kon happi
My translation:
Cutting grass —
into bush clover sinks
a blue work-coat.
Kigo: 草刈  Kusa kari  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 草刈女さゆらぐ笠は鎌返り
Romaji:
Kusa kari me
sa yuragu kasa wa
kama togeri
My translation:
Grass-cutter —
her swaying hat,
sharpens a sickle.
Kigo: 草刈  Kusa kari  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 鰻簗木曽の夜汽車の照らし過ぐ
Romaji:
Unagi-yana
Kiso no yagisha no
terashi sugu
Kigo: 魚簗  Yana  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 簗守の影あらふなり簗しぶき
Romaji:
Yana-mori no
kage arau nari
yana shibuki
My translation:
The weir guardian's
shadow they wash,
weir sprays.
Kigo: 魚簗  Yana  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 大簗のとどろきに住む山家かな
Romaji:
O yana no
todoroki ni sumu
sanka kana
My translation:
By a giant weir's
thundering, to dwell,
mountain house.
Kigo: 魚簗  Yana  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 簗にゐてあめつち水の音となる
Romaji:
Yana ni ite
ametsuchi mizu no
oto to naru
My translation:
At a fish weir
heaven and earth are just
water sounds.
Kigo: 魚簗  Yana  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 雪洞を吹き消す風や涼み台
Romaji:
Bonbori wo
fuki-kesu kaze ya
suzumi-dai
My translation:
The hand-lantern,
blown out by a breeze —
platform for cooling.
Kigo: 納涼  Suzumi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 遠花火音して何もなかりけり
Romaji:
To hanabi
otoshite nani mo
nakari keri
My translation:
Distant fireworks —
only sounds,
nothing else.
Kigo: 花火  Hanabi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 夏まけとかくしがたなくやつれけり
Romaji:
Natsu make to
kakushigata naku
yatsure keri
My translation:
Lost to summer,
no hiding it —
so haggard.
Kigo: 夏痩  Natsu yase  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 夏痩や頬も色どらず束ね髪
Romaji:
Natsu yase ya
ho mo irodorazu
tabane gami
My translation:
Summer thinness —
cheeks without colour,
bundled hair.
Kigo: 夏痩  Natsu yase  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 旅の空矢車鳴りて端午なり
Romaji:
Tabi no sora
yaguruma narite
tango nari
My translation:
While traveling, the sky
resounds with arrow-wheels —
it's tango.
Kigo: 端午  Tango  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 雨がちに端午ちかづく父子かな
Romaji:
Ame gachi ni
tango chikazuku
oyako kana
Kigo: 端午  Tango  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 端午なほ深山ざくらは雲に咲く
Romaji:
Tango nao
miyama zakura wa
kumo ni saku
My translation:
Tango, and still
some deep mountain cherry flowers
bloom in clouds.
Kigo: 端午  Tango  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 風吹けば来るや隣の鯉幟
Romaji:
Kaze fukeba
kuru ya tonari no
koi nobori
My translation:
When the wind blows,
they come! the neighbor's
carp banners.
Kigo: 鯉幟  Koinobori  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 鯉幟風に折れ又風に伸ぶ
Romaji:
Koi nobori
kaze ni ore mata
kaze ni nobu
My translation:
Carp banners —
they fold, then stretch
in the wind.
Kigo: 鯉幟  Koinobori  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 町変り人も変りし鯉のぼり
Romaji:
Machi kawari
hito mo kawari shi
koi nobori
My translation:
The town has changed,
people, too, changed —
carp banners.
Kigo: 鯉幟  Koinobori  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 鯉幟下ろすときだけ庭狭し
Romaji:
Koi nobori
orosu toki dake
niwa semashi
My translation:
Carp banners —
when brought down,
the garden is small.
Kigo: 鯉幟  Koinobori  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 神田川祭の中をながれけり
Romaji:
Kanda-gawa
matsuri no naka wo
nagare keri
My translation:
Kanda river —
through the center of the festival,
it flowed.
Kigo: 祭  Matsuri  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 祭囃子目高の水に流れくる
Romaji:
Matsuri-bayashi
medaka no mizu ni
nagare kuru
My translation:
Festival music
comes flowing to
killifish' water.
Kigo: 祭  Matsuri  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: さかづきに映る祭の燈ものみほす
Romaji:
Sakazuki ni
utsuru matsuri no
hi mo nomi hosu
My translation:
The festival lamp
reflected in the wine cup,
drunk up.
Kigo: 祭  Matsuri  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 祇園会や錦の上に京の月
Romaji:
Gion e ya
nishiki no ue ni
kyo no tsuki
My translation:
Gion festival —
above the brocade,
the capital's moon.
Kigo: 祇園会  Gione  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 祇園会や古き錦に汗の玉
Romaji:
Gion e ya
furuki nishiki ni
ase no tama
My translation:
Gion festival —
on old brocade,
beads of sweat.
Kigo: 祇園会  Gione  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 青茅輪あざやかに野の匂いして
Romaji:
Ao chino wa
azayakani no no
nioi shite
My translation:
Green lalong wreath —
vivid with the fragrance
of fields.
Kigo: 夏越  Nagoshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 形代や今こそ掌より川波へ
Romaji:
Kata shiro ya
ima koso te yori
kawanami e
My translation:
Paper-doll image —
just now left the hand,
in river waves.
Kigo: 夏越  Nagoshi  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 金魚玉天神祭映りそむ
Romaji:
Kingyo dama
Tenjin matsuri
utsuri somu
Kigo: 金魚玉  Kingyodama  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 金魚玉夜の軽雷に汗ばめり
Romaji:
Kingyo dama
yo no keirai ni
ase bameri
My translation:
Goldfish bowl —
with night's light thunder,
some sweat beads.
Kigo: 金魚玉  Kingyodama  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 金魚玉かがやき昼寝人さめず
Romaji:
Kingyo dame
kagayaki hirune
bito samezu
My translation:
The goldfish bowl
shines — the napper
doesn't wake up.
Kigo: 金魚玉  Kingyodama  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 金魚玉眺めてメロン食ふことも
Romaji:
Kingyo dama
nagamete meron
ku koto mo
My translation:
A goldfish bowl
to look at, a melon
to eat, too.
Kigo: 金魚玉  Kingyodama  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 彼一語我一語新茶淹れながら
Romaji:
Kare ichigo
ware ichigo
shincha
ire nagara
My translation:
He — a word,
I — a word, while making
new tea.
Kigo: 新茶  Shincha  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: わが碗にをさめしづく新茶くむ
Romaji:
Waga wan ni
osameshi shizuku
shincha kumu
My translation:
Into my teacup
the drops settle,
pouring new tea.
Kigo: 新茶  Shincha  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 一筋の糸引出すや繭躍る
Romaji:
Hito suji no
ito hikidasu ya
mayu odoru
My translation:
A single line
of thread being drawn —
the cocoon dances.
Kigo: 繭  Mayu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 母がもぐ白繭黄繭露の中
Romaji:
Haha ga mogu
shiro mayu ki mayu
tsuyu no naka
My translation:
Mother picks
white, yellow cocoons,
in the dew.
Kigo: 繭  Mayu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 悉く繭となりたる静けさよ
Romaji:
Kotogotoku
mayu to naritaru
shizukesa yo
My translation:
Each and every one
turned into cocoons,
how quiet!
Kigo: 繭  Mayu  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 疲れ鵜の細きうなじを並べけり
Romaji:
Tsukare u no
hosoki unaji wo
narabekeri
My translation:
Tired cormorants —
their thin napes
in a row.
Kigo: 鵜飼  Ukai  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 行水の女にほれる烏かな
Romaji:
Gyozui no
onna ni horeru
karasu kana
My translation:
The tub-bathing
lady, he's fallen for —
Mr. Crow.
Kigo: 行水  Gyozui  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 行水や月に吹かるるあばら骨
Romaji:
Gyozui ya
tsuki ni fukaruru
abara bone
My translation:
Tub-bath —
in moonlight being blown,
the ribs.
Kigo: 行水  Gyozui  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 行水や暮れしゆく松の深みどり
Romaji:
Gyozui ya
kure yuku matsu no
fuka midori
My translation:
Tub-bath —
as dusk falls, the pine's
deep green.
Kigo: 行水  Gyozui  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 行水や児がつかみをる瓜の蔓
Romaji:
Gyozui ya
ko ga tsukami oru
uri no tsuru
My translation:
Tub-bath —
the child is clutching
a melon vine.
Kigo: 行水  Gyozui  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: ひとりづつ座を外しくる端居かな
Romaji:
Hitori zutsu
za wo hazushi kuru
hashi-i kana
My translation:
One by one
they leave their seats, come
to sit on the veranda.
Kigo: 端居  Hashi-i  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 端居よりこぼれてをり芝に坐し
Romaji:
Hashi-i yori
i koborete ori
shiba ni zashi
My translation:
From the veranda,
they spilled down,
sat on the turf.
Kigo: 端居  Hashi-i  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 端居して明日逢ふ人を思ひをり
Romaji:
Hashi-i shite
asu au hito wo
omoi ori
My translation:
Sitting on the veranda,
I think of the person
I'll see tomorrow.
Kigo: 端居  Hashi-i  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 早乙女や泥手にはさむ額髪
Romaji:
Saotome ya
doro te ni hasamu
hitaigami
My translation:
Rice-planting girl —
between muddy fingers,
a forelock.
Kigo: 早乙女  Saotome  [Summer / Jinji]

Poem: 峯入の老いてそのこる美男眉
Romaji:
Mine iri no
oite mo nokoru
biman mayyu
My translation:
He enters the peak —
aging, but still
handsome eyebrows.
Kigo: 峯入  Mine iri  [Summer / Shukyo]

Poem: 大空の下あるき来て花御堂
Romaji:
Ozora no
shita aruki kite
hana mido
My translation:
Walked under
the great sky — to the
flowery pavilion.
Kigo: 仏生会  Busshoe  [Spring / Shukyo]

Poem: 初鰹　聞きおよんだる　ばかりなり
Romaji:
Hatsugatsuo
kiki oyondaru
bakari nari
My translation:
The first bonito —
so far I've just
heard it.
Kigo: 初鰹 Hatsugatsuo — First Bonito

Poem: 夏虫や昼は美咲く　水ぼとり
Romaji:
Natsu mushi ya
hiru wa hishi saku
mizubotori
My translation:
Summer insects —
in daytime, where water
chestnuts bloom.
Kigo: 夏の虫 Natsu no mushi — Summer Insects [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 火取虫　外に出ている　宵の人
Romaji:
Hitori mushi
soto ni dete iru
yoi no hito
My translation:
Light-drawn insects —
people are all out
this evening.
Kigo: 火取虫 Hitori mushi — Light-Drawn Insects, Moths [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: はためくをやめて　あゆみ入る　火取虫
Romaji:
Hatameku wo
yamete ayumiru
hitori mushi
My translation:
They've stopped
fluttering, and walk now —
light-drawn insects.
Kigo: 火取虫 Hitori mushi — Light-Drawn Insects, Moths [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 毛虫いま　駱駝の瘤のごと急ぐ
Romaji:
Kemushi ima
rakuda no kobu no
goto isogu
My translation:
The caterpillar now,
with a camel's hump,
hurries.
Kigo: 毛虫 Kemushi — Caterpillar [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 毛虫もいま　みどりの餌を終へ　歩みそむ
Romaji:
Kemushi no ima
midori no ge wo oe
ayumisommu
My translation:
The caterpillar too,
done with a green meal,
starts to walk.
Kigo: 毛虫 Kemushi — Caterpillar [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 唖蝉も　鳴きをはりたる　さまをせり
Romaji:
Oshi zemi mo
naki owari taru
sama wo seri
My translation:
A dumb cicada, too,
made as though it just
finished a song.
Kigo: 蝉 Semi — Cicada [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 風わずかに　石の上なる　蝉の殻
Romaji:
Kaze wazuka ni
ishi no ue naru
semi no kara
My translation:
The wind slight,
on a rock,
a cicada shell.
Kigo: 空蝉 Utsusemi — Cicada Shell [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 空蝉の　目に見るものを　おそれけり
Romaji:
Utsusemi no
me ni miru mono wo
osore keri
My translation:
Cicada shell —
it frightened those
who saw it.
Kigo: 空蝉 Utsusemi — Cicada Shell [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 炎天や　瓦をすべる　兜虫
Romaji:
Enten ya
kawara wo suberu
kabuto mushi
My translation:
A blazing sky —
from roof tiles slips
a beetle.
Kigo: 兜虫 Kabutomushi — Beetle [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: ひっぱられ　糸　まっすぐや　兜虫
Romaji:
Hipparaneru
ito massugu ya
kabuto mushi
My translation:
The string being pulled,
perfectly straight —
a beetle.
Kigo: 兜虫 Kabutomushi — Beetle [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 縛されて　意力光る　兜虫
Romaji:
Bakusaute
nenriki hikaru
kabuto mushi
My translation:
Harnessed,
his will power gleams —
the beetle.
Kigo: 兜虫 Kabutomushi — Beetle [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 夜の山の　あをさ　動かす　兜虫
Romaji:
Yo no yama no
aosa ugokasu
kabuto mushi
My translation:
The night mountain's green
stirs —
beetles.
Kigo: 兜虫 Kabutomushi — Beetle [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 一つ追ひ　をれば　二つに　夜の蠅
Romaji:
Hitotsu oi
toreba futatsu ni
yoru no hae
My translation:
Chasing one,
now there are two —
nighttime flies.
Kigo: 蠅 Hae — Flies [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 叩かれて　昼の蚊を吐く　木魚かな
Romaji:
Takakarete
hiru no ka wo haku
mokugyo kana
My translation:
When struck, out came
a daytime mosquito —
sutra drum.
Kigo: 蚊 Ka — Mosquito [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 塵取にすこしかかりて　蟻の道
Romaji:
Chiritori ni
sukoshi kakarite
ari no michi
My translation:
On the dust-pan
a part of it lies —
the road of ants.
Kigo: 蟻 Ari — Ants [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 二階まで　蟻　のぼりきて　午後ふかし
Romaji:
Nikai made
ari nobori kite
gogo fukashi
My translation:
To the second floor,
ants have climbed —
late afternoon.
Kigo: 蟻 Ari — Ants [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 蟻の列　しづかに蝶を　うかべたる
Romaji:
Ari no retsu
shizuka ni cho wo
ukabetaru
My translation:
The row of ants —
quietly, a butterfly
afloat.
Kigo: 蟻 Ari — Ants [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: なめくぢの　左曲りと　右曲り
Romaji:
Namekuji no
hidari magari to
migi magari
My translation:
The slug's
left turn and
right turn.
Kigo: 蛞蝓 Namekuji — Slug [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: なめくぢり　身を絞りつつ　起き返り
Romaji:
Namekujiri
mi wo shibori tsutsu
okikaeri
My translation:
The slug,
wringing its body,
gets up.
Kigo: 蛞蝓 Namekuji — Slug [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: かたつむり　老いて眠りを　大切に
Romaji:
Katatsumuri
oite nemuri wo
taisetsu ni
My translation:
The snail,
growing old, takes a
lot of sleep.
Kigo: 蝸牛 Katatsumuri — Snail [Summer / Dobutsu]

Poem: 余花に逢ふ　再び逢ひし　人のごと
Romaji:
Yoka ni au
futatabi aishi
hito no goto
My translation:
To meet remnants of
flowers: like meeting
someone again.
Kigo: 余花 Yoka — Remnants of Flowers [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 一電車　早きばかりに　余花暮れず
Romaji:
Hito densha
hayoki bakari ni
yoka kurezu
My translation:
One tram sooner,
it wouldn't have dusked on
the remnants of flowers.
Kigo: 余花 Yoka — Remnants of Flowers [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 傘の内　随きくる鹿や　余花の雨
Romaji:
Kasa no uchi
tsuki kuru shika ya
yoka no ame
My translation:
Under the umbrella
a deer comes trailing —
rain on flower remnants.
Kigo: 余花 Yoka — Remnants of Flowers [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 夕風や　白薔薇の花　皆動く
Romaji:
Yu kaze ya
shiro bara no hana
mina ugoku
My translation:
An evening breeze —
the white roses
all sway.
Kigo: 薔薇 Bara — Rose [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 見るうちに　薔薇たわたわと　散り積る
Romaji:
Miru uchi ni
bara tawatawa to
chiri tsumoru
My translation:
While gazing,
the rose crumbled
into a pile.
Kigo: 薔薇 Bara — Rose [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: ばら展の　ばら競ひつつ　萎えてゆく
Romaji:
Bara ten no
bara kisoi tsutsu
naete yuku
My translation:
The roses
of a rose exhibit vie,
as they wither.
Kigo: 薔薇 Bara — Rose [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 石楠花に　碁の音響く　山深し
Romaji:
Shakunage ni
go no oto hibiku
yama fukashi
My translation:
Among rhododendrons,
the echoes of "go" —
the mountain is deep.
Kigo: 石楠花 Shakunage — Rhododendron [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 石楠花に　躍りゆく瀬や　室生川
Romaji:
Shakunage ni
odori yuku se ya
Murogawa
My translation:
By rhododendrons
dancing rapids flow —
Muro river.
Kigo: 石楠花 Shakunage — Rhododendron [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 石楠花を　隠さう雲の　急にして
Romaji:
Shakunage wo
kakuso kumo no
kyu ni shite
My translation:
Rhododendrons
will be hidden! The clouds,
so swift.
Kigo: 石楠花 Shakunage — Rhododendron [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 石楠花の　夕明りして　われ立てり
Romaji:
Shakunage no
yu akari shite
ware tateri
My translation:
In rhododendrons'
evening glow
I stood.
Kigo: 石楠花 Shakunage — Rhododendron [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 橘の　花や　したがふ　葉三枚
Romaji:
Tachibana no
hana ya shitagai
ha san mai
My translation:
A citrus
flower — and three leaves
that seem to follow it.
Kigo: 花橘 Hana tachibana — Citrus Flower [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 紫陽花や　白よりいでし　浅みどり
Romaji:
Ajisai ya
shiro yori ideshi
asa midori
My translation:
Hydrangeas —
from white came
pale green.
Kigo: 紫陽花 Ajisai — Hydrangea [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 谷坊を呼ぶ峰坊や　夏木立
Romaji:
Tani bo wo
yobu mine bo ya
natsu kodachi
Kigo: 夏木立 Natsu kodachi — Summer Grove [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 灯ともせば　雨音　わたる　茂りかな
Romaji:
Hi tomoseba
amaoto wataru
shigeri kana
My translation:
A light put on,
the sound of rain across
luxuriant growth.
Kigo: 茂 Shigeri — Luxuriant Growth [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 木の闇を　音なくて出づ　揚羽蝶
Romaji:
Ko no yami wo
oto nakute izu
agebacho
My translation:
Out of the trees'
darkness, silently,
a swallow-tail butterfly.
Kigo: 木下闇 Ko no shita yami — Under-Trees Darkness [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 若楓　縁の障子を　外しけり
Romaji:
Waka kaede
en no shoji wo
hazushi keri
My translation:
Young maple leaves —
the veranda's paper doors,
removed.
Kigo: 若楓 Waka kaede — Young Maple Leaves [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 若楓　枝を平らに　うち重ね
Romaji:
Waka kaede
eda wo taira ni
uchi kasane
My translation:
Young maple leaves —
their level boughs,
one over the other.
Kigo: 若楓 Waka kaede — Young Maple Leaves [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 山蛙　常緑木落葉　時らず
Romaji:
Yama kawazu
tokiwagi ochiba
toki shirazu
My translation:
Mountain frog —
evergreens' leaves fall
at any moment.
Kigo: 常緑木落葉 Tokiwagi ochiba — Evergreens' Fallen Leaves [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 旧道は　杉の落葉の　箱根かな
Romaji:
Kyudo wa
sugi no ochiba no
Hakone kana
My translation:
The old road,
with fallen cedar leaves,
Hakone.
Kigo: 常緑木落葉 Tokiwagi ochiba — Evergreens' Fallen Leaves [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 夏落葉　深く沈みて　露天風呂
Romaji:
Natsu ochiba
fukaku shizumite
rotenburo
My translation:
Summer fallen leaves
sinking deeply,
outdoor hot spring.
Kigo: 常緑木落葉 Tokiwagi ochiba — Evergreens' Fallen Leaves [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 野いばらの　あをむと見しや　花つぼみ
Romaji:
No ibara no
aomu to mishi ya
hana tsubomi
My translation:
As the field rose
bush turned green,
buds appeared.
Kigo: 茨の花 Ibara no hana — Field Rose [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 若竹や　鞭のごとくに　五六本
Romaji:
Wakatake ya
muchi no gotoku ni
go-roppon
My translation:
Young bamboo —
like whips, five or
six of them.
Kigo: 若竹 Waketake — Young Bamboo [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 禅堂の　ぐるりの闇の　今年竹
Romaji:
Zendo no
gururi no yami no
kotoshi dake
My translation:
The darkness
around a Zen hall —
this year's bamboo.
Kigo: 若竹 Waketake — Young Bamboo [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 白芥子や　どこに火を焚く　藁灰どり
Romaji:
Shira geshi ya
doko ni hi wo taku
wara bokori
My translation:
White poppies —
where is the bonfire?
Straw ash.
Kigo: 罌粟の花 Keshi no hana — Poppy Flowers [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 野の池や　葉ばかり伸びし　杜若
Romaji:
No no ike ya
ha bakari nobishi
kakitsubata
My translation:
A field pond —
only the leaves have grown,
flower de luce.
Kigo: 杜若 Kakitsubata — Flower De Luce [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 戸を開けて　又寝る雨の　杜若
Romaji:
To wo akete
mata neru ame no
kakitsubata
My translation:
Open the door,
go back to bed — Rain on
flowers de luce.
Kigo: 杜若 Kakitsubata — Flower De Luce [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 杜若　までの　寂しさ消えにけり
Romaji:
Kakitsubata
made no sabishisa
kie ni keri
My translation:
The loneliness
on the way to flowers de luce
vanished.
Kigo: 杜若 Kakitsubata — Flower De Luce [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 富士は雲に　沈みあやめは　濃紫
Romaji:
Fuji wa kumo ni
shizumi ayame wa
ko murasaki
My translation:
Mt. Fuji sunk in
clouds, the blue flags —
dark purple.
Kigo: あやめ Ayame — Blue Flag [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 野あやめの　離れては濃く　群れて淡し
Romaji:
No ayame no
hanarete wa koka
murete awashi
My translation:
Field blue flags —
when apart, dark,
in groups, faint.
Kigo: あやめ Ayame — Blue Flag [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 一人立ち　一人かがめる　あやめかな
Romaji:
Hitori tachi
hitori kagameru
ayame kana
My translation:
One person stands,
another bends over
the blue flag.
Kigo: あやめ Ayame — Blue Flag [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 夜蛙の　声となりゆく　菖蒲かな
Romaji:
Yo gaeru no
koe to nari yuku
shobu kana
My translation:
A night
frog voices begin,
among acorus.
Kigo: 菖蒲 Shobu — Acorus [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 鴨の子を盥に飼ふや　銭葵
Romaji:
Kamo no ko wo
tarai ni kau ya
zeni aoi
My translation:
Ducklings
being raised in a tub —
coin hollyhocks.
Kigo: 葵 Aoi — Hollyhock [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 立葵　咲き終りたる　高さかな
Romaji:
Tachi aoi
saki owaritaru
takasa kana
My translation:
Standing hollyhocks
all come to bloom,
how tall!
Kigo: 葵 Aoi — Hollyhock [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 三方に　蝶のわかれし　立葵
Romaji:
Sanbo ni
cho no wakare shi
tachi aoi
My translation:
In three directions
the butterflies parted,
standing hollyhocks.
Kigo: 葵 Aoi — Hollyhock [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 向日葵は　月光に堪へぬ　花をなる
Romaji:
Himawari wa
gekko ni taemu
hana wo naru
My translation:
The sunflower —
now a flower that
can't bear the moonlight.
Kigo: 向日葵 Himawari — Sunflower [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 向日葵の　影引きずりて　日が疲る
Romaji:
Himawari no
kage hikizurite
hi ga tsukaru
My translation:
Dragging the
sunflower's shadow along,
the sun, exhausted.
Kigo: 向日葵 Himawari — Sunflower [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 向日葵に　剣の如き　レールかな
Romaji:
Himawari ni
tsurugi no gotoki
reru kana
My translation:
By sunflowers,
the rail is
like a sword.
Kigo: 向日葵 Himawari — Sunflower [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 向日葵の　大声で立つ　枯れても尚
Romaji:
Himawari no
ogoe de tatsu
karete nao
My translation:
The sunflower
stands with a loud voice,
likewise when withered.
Kigo: 向日葵 Himawari — Sunflower [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 睡蓮は　みな花閉つ　宵の星
Romaji:
Suiren wa
mina hana tojitsu
yoi no hoshi
My translation:
The water lilies
have all closed up,
evening stars.
Kigo: 睡蓮 Suiren — Water Lily [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 睡蓮の　隙間の水は　雨の文
Romaji:
Suiren no
sukima no mizu wa
ame no aye
My translation:
Water lilies —
on the water between them,
rain patterns.
Kigo: 睡蓮 Suiren — Water Lily [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 睡蓮の　こそり　しりぞく　風のあり
Romaji:
Suiren no
kosori shirizoku
kaze no ari
My translation:
The water lilies
slide backwards
at the wind.
Kigo: 睡蓮 Suiren — Water Lily [Summer / Shokubutsu]

Poem: 睡蓮や　鯉の分けゆく　花二つ
Romaji:
Suiren ya
koi no wake yuku
hana futatsu
My translation:
Water lilies —
a carp makes way
between two flowers.
Kigo: 睡蓮 Suiren — Water Lily [Summer / Shokubutsu]
